commonMistakes: поднять настроение/вопрос are figurative collocations meaning "to lift one's spirits / raise an issue".

synonymComparison.note: a synonym with a more limited use for 'to raise' (abstract values, rank).

past.n.gloss: Prices went up across the board.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll raise a glass to you.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you bring up the topic at the meeting?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll raise the issue of pay.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you increase the budget for the project?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll raise the prices of services.

imperative.pl.gloss: Bring up the issue at the meeting.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of repeating; use the perfective повторить for a single completed repetition.
etymology: Prefix по- plus an archaic вторить ("to repeat").
commonMistakes: повторять ошибку is a standard phrase meaning "to repeat the same mistake".

examples.ru: Она повторяет одну ошибку снова и снова.
examples.gloss: She keeps repeating the same mistake over and over.
We repeat the exercise every week.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym with a stronger nuance of repetitive insistence — 'to keep saying the same thing.'

past.m.ru: Он повторял одно и то же.
past.m.gloss: He kept repeating the same thing.

past.f.gloss: She reviewed the lesson at home.

past.n.ru: Всё повторялось из года в год.

past.pl.gloss: We were repeating the lyrics of the song.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я повторяю себе это каждый день.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I tell myself this every day.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он повторяет одну и ту же фразу.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He keeps repeating the same phrase.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We review the material before the exam.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you repeating past mistakes?

etymology: Derived from an archaic root зд- related to building.
commonMistakes: Distinguish дом ("house") from здание ("building" in general, more formal).

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of swearing/vowing; use the perfective поклясться for a single completed vow.
etymology: Derived from клятва ("an oath").
commonMistakes: Takes клясться + instrumental (клясться жизнью = "to swear on one's life").

examples.ru: Он всегда клянётся и не держит слово.
examples.gloss: He always swears but doesn't keep his word.

synonymComparison.note: клясться ('to swear,' a stronger, ritualistic commitment) differs from обещать ('to promise,' more ordinary).

past.f.gloss: She swore to tell the truth.

past.pl.ru: Мы клялись не предавать друг друга.
past.pl.gloss: We swore not to betray each other.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you swear to tell the truth?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They swear allegiance to the flag.

etymology: Borrowed from English "ma'am"; an indeclinable title.
commonMistakes: As a loanword, its form stays the same across all cases.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "dull".
commonMistakes: The antonym of умный (smart) — note its somewhat insulting tone.

etymology: An agent noun derived from перевести ("to translate").
commonMistakes: As an animate noun, its accusative equals its genitive (нанять переводчика).

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root for choice; near-synonymous with или.
commonMistakes: The либо...либо pattern expresses an "either...or" choice.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin patiens ("one who suffers").
commonMistakes: As an animate noun, its accusative equals its genitive (принять пациента).

etymology: The adverbial form of особенный ("special").
commonMistakes: A focusing adverb meaning "especially", emphasizing a particular element of the sentence.

etymology: A lexicalized neuter short form of очевидный ("evident"), used sentence-initially.
commonMistakes: Distinguish очевидно (clearly, high confidence) from видимо (apparently, a softer guess).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "fish".
commonMistakes: Covers both the fish as a living creature and as a prepared dish — mind the context.

etymology: A colloquial word from an old root; the original sense is "a pile/heap".
commonMistakes: куча + plural genitive is a colloquial way to emphasize quantity (куча проблем = "a ton of problems").

etymology: Derived from шутить ("to joke").
commonMistakes: в шутку is a standard adverbial phrase meaning "jokingly/in jest".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/ongoing coercion; use the perfective заставить for a single completed act of forcing.
etymology: Prefix за- plus ставить ("to place").
commonMistakes: Takes заставлять + person + infinitive (заставлять его работать).

examples.gloss: She makes the kids do homework.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym with more of a 'forced by circumstance' nuance — 'to compel.'

past.m.gloss: He forced himself to endure it.

past.n.gloss: Everything gave one pause to think.

past.pl.gloss: We were forcing ourselves to work more.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you making us reconsider the plan?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They make us follow the rules.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of proving; use доказывать for repeated/ongoing proving.
etymology: Prefix до- plus an archaic казать ("to show") — "to show through to proof".
commonMistakes: доказать свою любовь is a figurative phrase meaning "to prove one's love through actions".

example.gloss: He proved to me that he was right.

examples.ru: Он постоянно доказывает свою точку зрения.
examples.gloss: He's always trying to prove his point.

synonymComparison.note: a more specific synonym for 'to confirm' (an existing claim).

past.pl.gloss: We proved we were right with facts.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you prove your case in court?

etymology: A natural filler interjection used while thinking, equivalent to English "um".
commonMistakes: A pure filler/hesitation word with no grammatical function in the sentence.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of protecting; use защищать for repeated/ongoing protection.
etymology: Prefix за- plus щит ("shield") — "to shield".
commonMistakes: защитить диссертацию is the standard academic phrase meaning "to defend a dissertation".

example.gloss: He protected the child from danger.

examples.gloss: The lawyer defended the client in court.

synonymComparison.note: a more military/organizational synonym for 'to defend' (a territory, position).

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll defend the project before the committee.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you protect clients' rights?

etymology: Derived from an archaic пол- ("half").
commonMistakes: половина is followed by the singular genitive (половина яблока = "half an apple").

etymology: Derived from доказать ("to prove").
commonMistakes: Distinguish the noun доказательство (evidence/proof) from the verb доказать (to prove) by part of speech.

etymology: Borrowed from English "business".
commonMistakes: Unlike some older loanwords, it declines fully and regularly in modern Russian.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "tongue"; carries both the "tongue" and "language" senses.
commonMistakes: Carries both the body-part "tongue" sense and the "language" sense — mind the context.

etymology: The adverbial form of обязательный ("mandatory").
commonMistakes: не обязательно is a standard phrase meaning "not necessarily".

etymology: Borrowed from French hôtel.
commonMistakes: Distinguish гостиница (the native Russian word) from отель (a borrowed, slightly more upscale/international-sounding synonym).

etymology: Borrowed from French dame, ultimately from Latin domina ("mistress of the house").
commonMistakes: дама сердца is a figurative idiom meaning "the lady one loves".

etymology: Borrowed from Latin forma ("shape").
commonMistakes: Polysemous — "shape", "uniform", "[physical] condition (в форме)" — mind the context.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "shining thing".
commonMistakes: Note the figurative use in кинозвезда ("movie star").

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of crying. заплакать is the perfective partner marking the onset of crying.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European onomatopoeic root meaning "to cry".
commonMistakes: Takes плакать от + genitive to express the cause (плакать от счастья = "to cry from happiness").

examples.gloss: The toddler started crying from fright.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym for a more intense form of crying — 'to sob/wail.'

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you crying because of the movie?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you cry at weddings?

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't cry, everything will be fine.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "stranger/guest".
commonMistakes: Mind the genitive plural гостей (regular but easy to forget).

etymology: Derived from the root of шагать ("to stride").
commonMistakes: шаг за шагом is a standard adverbial phrase meaning "step by step".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of occupying/borrowing; use занимать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix за- plus an archaic нять ("to take") — "to take and occupy".
commonMistakes: Takes занять денег у + genitive (занять денег у друга = "to borrow money from a friend").

example.gloss: He borrowed money from a friend.

examples.gloss: This topic has occupied my mind for a long time.

synonymComparison.note: a more specific synonym for 'to borrow/lend' money or items.

past.m.gloss: He took the seat by the window.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you take out a loan from the bank?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you fill the vacancy?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они займут первое место в рейтинге.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll take first place in the ranking.

etymology: A colloquial shortening of the conditional particle бы.
commonMistakes: б is a colloquial shortening of бы after a vowel — not used in formal registers.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of removing/filming; use the perfective снять for a single completed instance.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of снять.
commonMistakes: Polysemous — "to take off clothes", "to rent an apartment", "to shoot a film" — mind the context.

example.gloss: I take off my shoes at the entrance.

examples.gloss: The director finished shooting the film in a year.

synonymComparison.note: a more administrative/legal synonym for 'to rent/lease.'

past.m.gloss: He was filming video on his phone.

past.f.gloss: She rented the apartment for three years.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you renting the apartment alone?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's filming an ad for the company.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you withdrawing money from the account?

etymology: Borrowed from French madame; an indeclinable title.
commonMistakes: As a loanword, its form stays the same across all cases.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "rain", with a fleeting vowel (дождь→дождя).
commonMistakes: The instrumental дождём has the stress shift to the ending.

etymology: Negative prefix не- plus медленно ("slowly") — "without delay".
commonMistakes: A stronger, more urgent/commanding adverb than сразу.

etymology: Borrowed from Greek narkotikos ("numbing").
commonMistakes: Don't confuse лекарство (medicine) with наркотик (narcotic/drug), though some medical narcotics overlap.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of setting off; use отправляться for repeated/ongoing departure.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of отправить ("to send") — "to send oneself off → set out".
commonMistakes: отправиться в путь is a standard idiom meaning "to set off on a journey".

example.gloss: He set off on a journey.

examples.gloss: She set off for home late.

examples.ru: Мы отправляемся каждый год в отпуск.
examples.gloss: We go on vacation every year.

synonymComparison.note: отправиться ('to set off,' more formal/written) differs in register from поехать ('to leave by vehicle,' more general).

past.m.gloss: He set off on his journey early.

past.f.gloss: She set off looking for adventure.

past.pl.gloss: We set off on a tour.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you set off on the expedition?

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing the state of "lying down", with no true perfective counterpart (полежать is a related word meaning "to lie down for a while"). Compare ложиться–лечь, the separate verb pair for the act of lying down.
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to lie".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse лежать (the state of lying) with ложиться/лечь (the act of lying down).

examples.gloss: He's in the hospital (lying in bed).
The book is lying on the table.
Let me lie down for a minute.
He lay down for a bit and got up.

synonymComparison.note: an important contrast: лежать is the stative 'to be lying,' while ложиться–лечь (a different root) is the action of lying down.

past.f.gloss: She was lying there with a book.

past.n.gloss: Everything was lying around in disarray.

past.pl.gloss: We were lying on the beach.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you lying on your back?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The document is in the folder.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you sunbathing for a long time?

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed instance of a device/plan "working/triggering"; use срабатывать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix с- plus работать ("to work") — "to work and produce a result".
commonMistakes: Used for mechanisms, plans, and strategies "working" — not typically for a person's own activity.

examples.gloss: The alarm went off at night.

synonymComparison.note: сработать ('to work,' for mechanisms/plans) differs from получиться ('to turn out well,' a broader result).

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я сработаю как надо, не волнуйся.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: (personified, rare usage) Don't worry, I'll perform as needed.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты сработаешь на этот раз лучше?
nonpast.2sg.gloss: (personified, rare usage) Will you perform better this time?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The plan will work if we're lucky.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: (personified, rare usage) We'll work together smoothly.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: (personified, rare usage) You'll function as a single team.

imperative.sg.gloss: (personified, rare usage) Perform exactly according to plan.

imperative.pl.gloss: (personified, rare usage) Work together smoothly this time.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of protecting; use the perfective защитить for a single completed defense.
etymology: Derived from защита ("defense").
commonMistakes: Takes защищать от + genitive (защищать от опасности = "to protect from danger").

examples.gloss: The cream protects skin from the sun.

synonymComparison.note: a more military/organizational synonym for 'to defend' (a territory, position).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I defend my point of view.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you protect consumer rights?

etymology: Derived from the root of удовлетворить ("to satisfy").
commonMistakes: С удовольствием! is a frequent standalone response meaning "Gladly!"

etymology: Derived from an archaic способить ("to suit").
commonMistakes: способный на + accusative can also mean "capable of [doing]" (способен на всё = "capable of anything").

etymology: Derived from начало ("beginning/head"); the sense is "one who stands at the head → boss".
commonMistakes: Also used for a female boss (a feminine начальница exists but is more colloquial).

etymology: Derived from служить ("to serve").
commonMistakes: Distinguish работа (work in general) from служба (official service/duty).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of pulling out/rescuing; use вытаскивать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix вы- plus тащить ("to drag/pull") — "to pull out".
commonMistakes: вытащить из беды is a figurative phrase meaning "to rescue [someone] from trouble".

governance.pattern: accusative (object pulled out) + из + genitive (from where)

example.gloss: He pulled the key out of his pocket.

examples.gloss: Rescuers pulled him out of the water.

examples.ru: Он всегда вытаскивает телефон из сумки.
examples.gloss: He always pulls his phone out of his bag.

synonymComparison.note: вытащить ('to pull/yank out') differs from достать ('to reach and get,' more general).

past.pl.gloss: We pulled the car out of the mud.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll pull him out of trouble.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you pull out the nail?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll pull out the splinter himself.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you pull out the weed's root?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll pull the car out of the snowdrift.

imperative.pl.gloss: Take the things out of the box.

etymology: на plus конец ("end") — "finally".
commonMistakes: наконец-то! is an emphatic exclamation meaning "finally!"

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of winning; use побеждать for repeated/ongoing winning. This verb is defective, lacking a standard 1st-person singular form.
etymology: Prefix по- plus беда ("hardship", archaically also "strife").
commonMistakes: The 1st-person singular (*победю) is non-standard, so a periphrastic form like смогу победить or одержу победу is used instead.

examples.gloss: Good triumphs over evil in fairy tales.

synonymComparison.note: a close synonym: победить is to defeat an opponent, while выиграть is to win a prize/game.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll win thanks to his experience.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you win the contest?

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual departure by vehicle; use the perfective уехать for a single completed departure.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of уехать.
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair уезжать (habitual) versus уехать (a single completed departure).

examples.ru: Она уезжает каждое лето к морю.
examples.gloss: She goes to the seaside every summer.
We leave early in the morning.

synonymComparison.note: an important contrast: уезжать is 'to leave by vehicle,' while уходить is 'to leave on foot.'

past.f.gloss: She used to be away for the whole weekend.

past.n.gloss: Everything was carried off on this train.

past.pl.gloss: We used to go away for a few days.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you going away for long?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's going on a business trip.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you leaving by car?

etymology: An affectionate diminutive of an archaic девка ("girl", slang).
commonMistakes: A casual, colloquial word — avoid it in formal settings.

etymology: Derived from защитить ("to protect").
commonMistakes: Distinguish защита (defense/protection) from защитник (a defender/attorney) by part of speech.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to flow".
commonMistakes: A feminine noun with an irregular stress shift (accusative реку).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of falling; use падать for repeated/ongoing falling.
etymology: Prefix у- plus an archaic пасть ("to fall").
commonMistakes: упасть духом is a figurative idiom meaning "to lose heart/become discouraged".

governance.pattern: с + genitive (fallen from) + на + accusative (fallen onto)

example.ru: Он упал с лестницы на пол.
example.gloss: He fell from the stairs onto the floor.

examples.gloss: She fell and broke her arm.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym for a more dramatic, sudden collapse — 'to crash down.'

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll fall if you're not careful.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The rate will drop by year's end.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы упадёте, если побежите так быстро.
nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll fall if you run that fast.

etymology: Borrowed from English "bar".
commonMistakes: Unrelated etymologically to барьер ("barrier") — different root.

etymology: Borrowed from English "state"; carries both the "US state" and "staff/headcount" senses.
commonMistakes: Carries two very different senses — "[US] state" and "[company] staff/headcount" — mind the context.

etymology: Derived from an archaic цвет, which also once meant "flower".
commonMistakes: Note the fleeting vowel that drops in declension (цветок→цветка).

etymology: ни plus что ("nothing") — a negative pronoun.
commonMistakes: The nominative is ничто, but ничего is the usual oblique-case form.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin documentum ("proof/lesson").
commonMistakes: A general term for "a document" — distinct from a specific type like справка (certificate).

etymology: The adverbial form of смешной ("funny").
commonMistakes: Used alone as an exclamation ("funny!") and also ironically to mean "ridiculous".

etymology: Borrowed from Latin tabella ("little board").
commonMistakes: Distinguish лекарство (medicine in general) from таблетка (the specific pill form).

etymology: The adverbial form of абсолютный ("absolute").
commonMistakes: абсолютно верно is a standard way to agree, "absolutely right".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of proposing; use the perfective предложить for a single completed proposal.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of предложить.
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair предлагать (ongoing proposing) versus предложить (a completed proposal).

synonymComparison.note: советовать ('to advise') differs from предлагать ('to offer/propose') — giving an opinion vs. offering an option.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you proposing a different plan?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you offer discounts to regular customers?

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of "acting/having an effect". подействовать is a related word meaning "to take effect / act for a while" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Derived from действие ("action").
commonMistakes: Covers both "[a person] acting" and "[a drug/thing] taking effect" — context decides which.

example.gloss: The medicine acts on the pain.

examples.gloss: The law has been in effect since January.
The threat had an effect on him.

synonymComparison.note: a more mechanical/systemic synonym for 'to function.'

past.m.gloss: He acted according to the instructions.

past.n.gloss: Everything functioned as a single mechanism.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I act according to the plan.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He acts in the company's interest.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you acting in coordination?

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to hate".
commonMistakes: As an animate noun, its accusative equals its genitive (победить врага).

etymology: за plus a case form of утро ("morning") — the first meal, before the rest of the morning.
commonMistakes: Refers only to "breakfast" — the specific morning meal.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of gathering/getting ready; use собираться for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of собрать ("to gather") — "to gather oneself".
commonMistakes: собраться с мыслями is a figurative idiom meaning "to collect one's thoughts".

governance.pattern: infinitive (what one is about to do)

examples.gloss: I got ready in five minutes.
He's planning to start a business.

examples.ru: Мы собираемся на площади каждую субботу.
examples.gloss: We gather at the square every Saturday.

synonymComparison.note: a more formal/deliberate synonym for intending to do something; собраться sounds more natural in speech.

past.n.gloss: Everything came together into one picture (figurative).

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you be ready in an hour?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll get ready for the trip quickly.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you all gather together?

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual arrival by vehicle; use the perfective приехать for a single completed arrival.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of приехать.
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair приезжать (habitual) versus приехать (a single completed arrival).

example.ru: Он приезжает в город каждый месяц.
example.gloss: He comes to the city every month.

examples.ru: Она приезжает к нам на праздники.
examples.gloss: She comes to us for the holidays.

synonymComparison.note: a more formal/official synonym for 'to arrive,' used for transport announcements.

past.m.gloss: He used to come here every summer.

past.n.gloss: Everything used to arrive on time.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you come by car?

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "word/reputation".
commonMistakes: Слава богу! is a frequent idiom meaning "thank goodness".

etymology: Derived from молодой ("young"); originally meant "a young man/hero".
commonMistakes: In modern usage it's a gender-neutral exclamation of praise, "well done!"

etymology: Derived from желать ("to wish").
commonMistakes: по собственному желанию is a standard phrase meaning "of one's own free will".

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of worry/experience, with no true perfective counterpart (попереживать is a related word meaning "to worry for a while").
etymology: Prefix пере- plus жить ("to live") — "to live through → to experience".
commonMistakes: Takes переживать за + accusative (переживать за ребёнка = "to worry about a child").

examples.gloss: She's going through a difficult period.

synonymComparison.note: nearly synonymous, but переживать implies a deeper, more sustained worry/experience.

past.m.gloss: He was worried about his family.

past.f.gloss: She went through the breakup painfully.

past.pl.gloss: We went through the crisis together.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you worried about the exam?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're going through the changes together.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you worried about the company?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're going through a difficult stage.

aspectUsage: A biaspectual verb (same form for both aspects), used for a man "getting married".
etymology: Derived from жена ("wife").
commonMistakes: Takes жениться на + prepositional (жениться на ней = "to marry her"). For a woman marrying, use выйти замуж instead.

synonymComparison.note: an important distinction: жениться is used for a man marrying, while выйти замуж is used for a woman marrying.

past.f.gloss: (note: for a daughter, выйти замуж is correct; женилась would be a misuse).

past.n.gloss: Everything was settled when he got married.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you going to marry her?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're getting married in the fall.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you getting married soon?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're getting married in a month.

imperative.pl.gloss: Get married if you love each other.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of driving/transporting someone; use отвозить for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix от- plus везти ("to transport").
commonMistakes: Distinguish отвезти (transport by vehicle) from отнести (carry on foot).

example.gloss: He drove me to the airport.

examples.gloss: She drove the kids to school.
We took the furniture to the dacha.
He drives the kids every morning.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym focusing more on reaching the destination — 'to get someone/something there.'

past.m.gloss: He delivered the cargo to the warehouse.

past.f.gloss: She took the package to the post office.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you drive us to the station?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll deliver the goods to the client.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы отвезём вещи на новую квартиру.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll move the things to the new apartment.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you deliver the documents to the office?

etymology: Derived from расследовать ("to investigate").
commonMistakes: Distinguish следствие (a formal legal inquiry) from расследование (investigation more broadly).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root for a season.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the noun's instrumental form with the fixed adverb летом ("in summer").

etymology: A lexicalized past participle of an archaic известить ("to inform"), used as an impersonal predicate.
commonMistakes: как известно is a standard phrase meaning "as is well known".

etymology: Borrowed from French rôle; the original sense is "a rolled-up script".
commonMistakes: играть роль can also figuratively mean "to matter" (это не играет роли = "it doesn't matter").

etymology: не plus чего (the genitive of что) — a negative predicate.
commonMistakes: нечего делать is a standard phrase meaning "there's nothing to do", taking an impersonal construction with an infinitive.

etymology: Derived from an archaic уровнять ("to level").
commonMistakes: уровень жизни is a standard collocation meaning "standard of living".

etymology: Borrowed from English "OK"; a colloquial agreement particle.
commonMistakes: A very casual expression — use хорошо in formal registers.

etymology: Derived from an archaic мнить ("to think").
commonMistakes: по моему мнению is a standard introductory phrase meaning "in my opinion".

etymology: Derived from владеть ("to possess"); a soft-stem feminine noun.
commonMistakes: власть над собой is a figurative idiom meaning "self-control".

etymology: Derived from искать ("to search").
commonMistakes: в поисках is a standard phrase meaning "in search of".

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "rest".
commonMistakes: оставить в покое is a standard idiom meaning "to leave [someone] alone".

etymology: Borrowed from Latin director ("one who directs").
commonMistakes: The plural директора has an irregular stress shift.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "wind", with a fleeting vowel (ветер→ветра).
commonMistakes: бросать слова на ветер is a figurative idiom meaning "to speak in vain".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of finishing eating; use съедать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix с- ("completely") plus есть ("to eat") — "to eat up".
commonMistakes: Distinguish есть (eating, general/ongoing) from съесть (finishing eating, perfective).

examples.gloss: He eats everything in one go.
I only eat half a portion.

synonymComparison.note: the key contrast: есть is the ongoing act of eating, while съесть is the perfective, 'to eat up/finish.'

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll eat it all by evening.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you finish the soup?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll eat it all in a minute.

imperative.pl.gloss: Eat it all, don't be shy.

etymology: Borrowed via English "station", ultimately from Latin statio ("a standing place").
commonMistakes: Distinguish остановка (a bus/tram stop) from станция (a larger station facility).

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing the ongoing state of "being called [something]". назваться is a related word mainly meaning "to identify oneself by name" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of называть ("to name") — "to be named [by someone else]".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the transitive называть ("to name") with the intransitive называться ("to be called").

examples.gloss: The movie has an interesting name.
This street is called something else now.

synonymComparison.note: a more archaic/literary synonym for 'to be called'; называться is the standard, widely used choice.

past.m.gloss: The project used to be called something else.

past.f.gloss: The company used to be called something else.

past.n.gloss: Everything used to be named simply.

past.pl.gloss: These places used to be called differently.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm listed under a different name in the documents.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: What's your name in the game?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The movie has a strange name.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы называемся по-новому с этого года.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We've gone by a new name since this year.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: What's your official name?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: These products are called the same thing.

etymology: The adverbial form of тихий ("quiet").
commonMistakes: Also used alone as a command, "Quiet!"

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of singing; use the perfective спеть for a single completed song.
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to sing".
commonMistakes: Distinguish петь (the ongoing act) from спеть (finishing singing one song).

synonymComparison.note: a more specific synonym for 'to sing along.'

past.f.gloss: She sang with her whole heart.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to sing with joy.

past.pl.gloss: We were singing in a choir.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We sing together in the evenings.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you sing at weddings?

etymology: Derived from приказать ("to order/command").
commonMistakes: Distinguish приказ (a formal/military order) from просьба (a request) by register.

etymology: Borrowed from English "taxi"; an indeclinable neuter noun.
commonMistakes: As a loanword, its form stays the same across all cases.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of doubt; use the perfective усомниться for a single completed onset of doubt.
etymology: Derived from сомнение ("doubt").
commonMistakes: Takes сомневаться в + prepositional (сомневаться в себе = "to doubt oneself").

examples.gloss: He began to doubt her honesty.
We doubted the plan right away.

synonymComparison.note: сомневаться ('to doubt,' a more general uncertainty) differs from подозревать ('to suspect,' a specific accusation).

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to doubt its own correctness.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you doubt the quality?

etymology: Borrowed from Latin factum ("a thing done").
commonMistakes: Distinguish факт (an undisputed fact) from мнение (a personal opinion).

etymology: The neuter nominalized form of многий ("many").
commonMistakes: Distinguish много (the quantity adverb) from многое (the nominalized pronoun "many things").

etymology: A lexicalized adverbial/impersonal-predicate use of сложный ("complex").
commonMistakes: Note the impersonal construction сложно + dative (мне сложно = "it's hard for me").

etymology: A nominalized use of the adjective животный ("of life"), related to an archaic жизнь.
commonMistakes: As an adjective-origin noun, it declines like an adjective (hard-stem pattern).

etymology: Originally meaning "pancake", lexicalized colloquially as an interjection of mild surprise or annoyance.
commonMistakes: Distinguish the literal food sense from the interjection use — casual contexts only.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "one's own".
commonMistakes: свобода слова is a standard political collocation meaning "freedom of speech".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of taking care of someone/something; use the perfective позаботиться for a single completed instance.
etymology: Derived from забота ("care/concern").
commonMistakes: Takes заботиться о + prepositional (заботиться о себе).

example.gloss: He takes care of the children.

examples.gloss: She takes care of her elderly parents.
He took care of the tickets.

synonymComparison.note: a more specific synonym for 'to tend/care for' (physical caregiving).

past.m.gloss: He took care of the business.

past.f.gloss: She took care of her health.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to care about order.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you care about the future?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you take care of your staff?

etymology: Borrowed from French costume, from Italian costume ("custom/habit").
commonMistakes: Beyond "suit", it also means "costume [for a purpose]" (купальный костюм = "swimsuit").

etymology: Derived from an archaic очередовать ("to alternate/take turns").
commonMistakes: без очереди is a standard idiom meaning "without waiting in line / with priority".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual lying; use the perfective солгать for a single completed lie.
etymology: A literary verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to lie".
commonMistakes: Distinguish врать (colloquial, frequent) from лгать (more literary/formal) by register.

examples.gloss: She doesn't know how to lie.
She lied for the sake of peace.

synonymComparison.note: nearly synonymous, but врать is more colloquial/everyday, while лгать has a more literary/formal ring.

past.n.gloss: Everything in this report was false.

past.pl.gloss: We were lying to each other.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He lies without a shred of guilt.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you lying intentionally?

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to know".
commonMistakes: знак внимания is a figurative collocation meaning "a gesture of consideration".

etymology: как ("how") plus an archaic вно ("like") — a comparative conjunction.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with как будто, but словно has a more literary tone.

etymology: Derived from опасность ("danger").
commonMistakes: опасно для жизни is a standard warning phrase meaning "life-threatening".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of recognizing/finding out; use the perfective узнать for a single completed instance.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of узнать.
commonMistakes: Distinguish узнавать (the ongoing process of recognizing/learning) from узнать (the completed act).

examples.gloss: He gets his news from newspapers.

examples.ru: Мы узнаём друг друга по голосу.
examples.gloss: We recognize each other by voice.

synonymComparison.note: a more formal synonym for 'to acknowledge/recognize' (officially).

past.m.gloss: He used to recognize people by their faces.

past.f.gloss: She used to catch up on the news every morning.

past.n.gloss: Everything was gradually coming to light.

past.pl.gloss: We were learning the details over time.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I recognize my friends from a distance.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He learns the results every week.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We get our news from the app.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you check the schedule ahead of time?

imperative.sg.gloss: Keep up with the news regularly.

etymology: The adverbial form of спокойный ("calm").
commonMistakes: Also used alone as a command, "Calm down!"

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of tidying up/leaving; use the perfective убраться for a single completed instance.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of убрать ("to tidy/remove").
commonMistakes: Covers both "to tidy up a room" and "get out!" (rude, imperative) — mind the context.

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to clean up, intransitive)

examples.gloss: We clean up before guests arrive.
She finished cleaning in an hour.
We finished cleaning before the holiday.

synonymComparison.note: убираться (colloquially also 'get out!') overlaps in context with уйти ('to leave,' more neutral).

past.m.gloss: He was tidying up the garage.

past.n.gloss: Everything was being cleaned in a hurry.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you clean before guests arrive?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you clean yourselves?

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to turn/bend"; originally meant "steep".
commonMistakes: Distinguish the literal "steep" sense from the colloquial "cool/awesome" sense by context.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed instance of (water level, heat, etc.) subsiding; use спадать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix с- ("down") plus an archaic пасть ("to fall").
commonMistakes: Its past tense спал is a homograph of the past tense of спать ("to sleep") — note the ambiguity.

examples.gloss: The swelling went down the next day.
The heat eased off by evening.

synonymComparison.note: a more general synonym for 'to decrease.' Спасть is used specifically for water levels, swelling, heat, etc.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The water will recede by morning.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: The swelling will subside in a day.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я спаду, как лист, к земле (поэт. личностный образ).
nonpast.1sg.gloss: "I will fall, like a leaf, to the ground" (poetic personification, rare usage).

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты спадёшь, волна, обратно в море (поэт. образ).
nonpast.2sg.gloss: "You will recede, wave, back into the sea" (poetic personification, rare usage).

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы спадём духом, если не поддержим друг друга (образно, редкое употребление).
nonpast.1pl.gloss: "Our spirits will sink if we don't support each other" (figurative, rare usage).

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы спадёте с лица, если продолжите так работать (образно, редкое употребление).
nonpast.2pl.gloss: "You'll look worn out if you keep working like that" (figurative, rare usage).

imperative.sg.ru: Спади же, жара, дай нам отдохнуть! (поэт. обращение, редкое употребление).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Subside already, heat, let us rest!" (poetic address, rare usage).

imperative.pl.ru: Отёки, спадите скорее! (образное обращение, редкое употребление).
imperative.pl.gloss: "Swelling, go down quickly!" (figurative address, rare usage).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed attempt at trying hard; use стараться for repeated/ongoing effort.
etymology: Prefix по- plus стараться ("to try hard").
commonMistakes: Постараюсь is a common hedging response meaning "I'll try" (not a firm promise).

examples.gloss: He made an effort and made it in time.
We tried with all our might.
We're trying to improve the service.

synonymComparison.note: постараться ('to try hard, make an effort') differs from попытаться ('to attempt') in the sustained, diligent nuance.

past.m.gloss: He tried to explain everything in detail.

past.f.gloss: She tried not to be late.

past.n.gloss: Everything tried to work out well.

past.pl.gloss: We tried to take all the feedback into account.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll try to finish on time.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you try to come earlier?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll try not to let the team down.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll try to do everything possible.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you try to respond quickly?

imperative.pl.gloss: Try to make it on time.

etymology: A compound of с ("from") + ума ("mind") + сшедший (the participle of сойти, "gone") — "gone from one's mind".
commonMistakes: The nominalized use (сумасшедший = "a madman") is also common — distinguish it from the adjective use.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of touching/moving someone emotionally; use the perfective тронуть for a single completed instance.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to push/move".
commonMistakes: Covers both "to touch physically" and "to move emotionally" — context decides which.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym for a lighter, more delicate touch — 'to graze/brush against.'

past.m.gloss: He was touching the keys gently.

past.f.gloss: She caressed the painting with her gaze (figurative).

past.n.gloss: Everything was touching to the heart.

past.pl.gloss: We were touching the exhibits carefully.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm touching this for the first time.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're touching the exhibit with our hands.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you touching something you shouldn't?

etymology: A nominalized past participle of пройти ("to pass by").
commonMistakes: As a nominalized neuter adjective (from прошлый), it declines like an adjective.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "quiet".
commonMistakes: The short forms тих/тиха/тихо are used in predicate position.

etymology: Derived from an archaic разниться ("to differ").
commonMistakes: Distinguish разница (a quantitative/qualitative difference) from отличие (a distinguishing feature).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of reaching an agreement; use договариваться for repeated/ongoing negotiation.
etymology: Prefix до- plus говорить ("to speak") — "to talk through to an agreement".
commonMistakes: Takes договориться с + instrumental (договориться с другом).

governance.pattern: с + instrumental (person agreed with) + о + prepositional (about what)

example.ru: Мы договорились с партнёром о встрече.
example.gloss: We agreed with the partner on a meeting.

examples.gloss: The parties are negotiating the terms.
We make arrangements in advance every time.

synonymComparison.note: договориться ('to come to a mutual agreement,' bilateral) differs from согласиться ('to agree,' one-sided acceptance).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll sort it out with him myself.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you work it out with the boss?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll work out the details later.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you agree on the deadlines?

imperative.sg.gloss: Work it out with him yourself.

etymology: Borrowed from French contrôle.
commonMistakes: потерять контроль is a figurative idiom meaning "to lose control/composure".

etymology: Borrowed from Latin series.
commonMistakes: Covers both "[TV] episode" and "series/sequence" — mind the context.

etymology: Derived from the root of мечтать ("to dream/aspire").
commonMistakes: Distinguish сон (a dream while asleep) from мечта (an aspirational dream).

etymology: Borrowed from Greek planetes ("wanderer").
commonMistakes: планета Земля is a standard phrase specifying "[the] planet Earth".

etymology: Borrowed from French chef, ultimately from Latin caput ("head").
commonMistakes: Covers both "head chef" (шеф-повар) and "boss" in general — mind the context.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin universitas ("a whole / community").
commonMistakes: Distinguish институт (a more specialized single-subject college) from университет (a comprehensive university).

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of losing; use the perfective потерять for a single completed loss.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to wear away".
commonMistakes: терять терпение is a figurative idiom meaning "to lose one's patience".

examples.gloss: The company is gradually losing customers.

synonymComparison.note: a synonym for a more serious loss — 'to be deprived of' something important.

past.pl.gloss: We were losing money every month.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're wasting your time.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of entering; use the perfective войти for a single completed entry.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of войти.
commonMistakes: входить в состав is a figurative collocation meaning "to be a member of / be included in".

examples.ru: Она входит в класс каждое утро.
examples.gloss: She enters the classroom every morning.
People come in here one at a time.

synonymComparison.note: входить (the direct act of entering) differs from заходить ('to drop in/stop by'), a close synonym with a different purpose.

past.f.gloss: She was the last to enter.

past.n.gloss: Everything was included in the set.

past.pl.gloss: We were entering one by one.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you on the committee?

etymology: в plus an archaic виду ("sight/view") — "in view of → because of".
commonMistakes: ввиду is a literary preposition requiring the genitive.

etymology: A nominalized neuter form of главный ("main").
commonMistakes: As a nominalized adjective, it declines like главный (adjective pattern).

etymology: по plus мой ("my") — a discourse adverb meaning "in my view".
commonMistakes: A frequent parenthetical for softening an opinion — set off by commas.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing the ongoing state of "belonging", with no true perfective counterpart.
etymology: Prefix при- plus an archaic надлежать ("to belong").
commonMistakes: Takes принадлежать + dative (эта книга принадлежит мне = "this book belongs to me").

example.gloss: He belongs to the older generation.

examples.gloss: This land belongs to the state.

synonymComparison.note: like являться, this stative verb has no perfective, but принадлежать means 'to belong/be owned by' while являться means 'to be (equal to).'

past.m.gloss: That style belonged to the past.

past.f.gloss: The idea originally belonged to him.

past.pl.gloss: The lands belonged to the family for centuries.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you belong to their circle?

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он принадлежит к редкому типу людей.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He belongs to a rare type of person.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We belong to the same culture.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you belong to this organization?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: These paintings belong to the museum.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of shouting; use the perfective крикнуть for a single completed shout.
etymology: A basic verb from an onomatopoeic root.
commonMistakes: Takes кричать на + accusative (кричать на ребёнка = "to yell at a child").

examples.gloss: The crowd is shouting with excitement.
I let out a shout of surprise.

synonymComparison.note: крикнуть ('to let out one shout,' single action) differs from закричать ('to start shouting,' an inchoative derivative).

past.f.gloss: She was screaming with all her strength.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to scream of danger (figurative).

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's shouting loud enough for the whole street to hear.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're shouting for no reason.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of getting in touch; use связываться for repeated/ongoing contact.
etymology: A reflexive derivative of связать ("to tie together") — "to connect oneself [to someone]".
commonMistakes: Takes связаться с + instrumental (связаться с другом).

example.ru: Он связался со мной по телефону.

examples.gloss: She got in touch with support.
We contacted a lawyer right away.

examples.ru: Он связывается с клиентами каждый день.
examples.gloss: He gets in touch with clients every day.
We keep in touch through a messenger app.

synonymComparison.note: связаться ('to get in touch,' neutral) differs from обратиться ('to formally approach/consult someone'), a close synonym implying more formality.

past.m.gloss: He got mixed up with a gang by chance (figurative, can have a negative connotation).

past.n.gloss: Everything linked together into one chain (figurative).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы свяжемся с вами по почте.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы свяжетесь с нами при необходимости?
nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you contact us if needed?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они свяжутся с партнёрами на неделе.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll contact the partners this week.

imperative.sg.gloss: Get in touch with me right away.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of showing; use the perfective показать for a single completed instance.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of показать.
commonMistakes: Distinguish показывать (the ongoing act) from показать (the completed act).

examples.gloss: He's showing progress in his studies.
The screen is showing an error.
He showed results on the exam.

synonymComparison.note: a more formal/technical synonym for 'to demonstrate/present.'

past.m.gloss: He was showing slides at the meeting.

past.pl.gloss: We were showing the guests around the city.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you showing growth trends?

imperative.pl.gloss: Show the works one at a time.

etymology: Derived from судить ("to judge"); masculine but declines like a feminine -я noun.
commonMistakes: A masculine (common-gender) noun that follows the -я declension pattern.

etymology: A place name derived from the explorer Amerigo Vespucci.
commonMistakes: Distinguish США (the United States) from Америка (the Americas as continents).

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of leaving something behind; use the perfective оставить for a single completed instance.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of оставить.
commonMistakes: оставлять без внимания is a figurative idiom meaning "to ignore/disregard".

example.gloss: He leaves his things in the room.

examples.gloss: She leaves notes in the kitchen.
He left his keys at home.
She left her mark on history (figurative).

synonymComparison.note: оставлять ('to leave behind' an object) differs from покидать ('to abandon/leave' a place or person).

past.m.gloss: He used to leave hints for us.

past.f.gloss: She used to leave the doors open.

past.n.gloss: Everything left something to be desired (figurative idiom).

past.pl.gloss: We used to leave the car in the parking lot.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you leaving the light on?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's leaving the choice up to you.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We leave reviews about the service.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you leave comments?

etymology: Derived from обвинить ("to accuse").
commonMistakes: Distinguish the noun обвинение (accusation) from обвиняемый (the accused person).

etymology: Borrowed from Greek programma ("something written beforehand").
commonMistakes: Covers both "plan/schedule" and "[computer] program" — mind the context.

etymology: Derived from страх ("fear").
commonMistakes: страшно интересно is a colloquial intensifier meaning "incredibly interesting".

etymology: Derived from an archaic ткнуть ("to poke"); the original sense is "a poked mark → a point".
commonMistakes: точка зрения is a standard figurative collocation meaning "point of view".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of striking; use ударять for repeated/ongoing striking.
etymology: Derived from удар ("a blow").
commonMistakes: ударить по рукам is a figurative idiom meaning "to seal a deal with a handshake".

example.gloss: He hit him in the face.

examples.gloss: She pounded her fist on the table.
The waves pound against the rocks.

synonymComparison.note: ударить ('to strike once, perfective') contrasts with бить ('to beat repeatedly, imperfective') — a related verb differing in single vs. repeated action.

past.pl.gloss: We shook hands on the deal (idiom).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll strike first if I have to.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll strike at the last moment.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you seal the deal today?

etymology: на plus много ("much") — an adverb intensifying a comparison.
commonMistakes: Used with comparatives (намного лучше, not "намного хороший").

etymology: Borrowed from Greek hērōs ("demigod hero").
commonMistakes: Besides "hero", also used for "the protagonist [of a story]".

etymology: The adverbial form of тяжёлый ("heavy").
commonMistakes: Note the impersonal construction тяжело + dative (мне тяжело = "it's hard for me").

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to blow".
commonMistakes: на свежем воздухе is a standard phrase meaning "out in the fresh air".

etymology: Derived from пять ("five"), referring to the fifth day of an old week-counting scheme.
commonMistakes: Days of the week use в + accusative (в пятницу, not "на пятницу").

etymology: A natural exclamation expressing surprise or relief.
commonMistakes: Can express surprise, delight, or relief depending on context — don't translate it rigidly.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of gathering; use собирать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix со- plus an archaic брать ("to take") — "to take together → to gather".
commonMistakes: Mind the aspect pair собрать (completed) versus собирать (the ongoing process of gathering).

examples.gloss: He's been collecting stamps since childhood.

synonymComparison.note: собрать ('to gather,' broad meaning) differs from накопить ('to accumulate/save up,' mainly money or resources).

past.n.gloss: Everything came together into one system.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you gather everyone for the meeting?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll assemble a team by Monday.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы соберём данные к концу недели.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll gather the data by the end of the week.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you collect signatures?

etymology: Derived from течь ("to flow").
commonMistakes: в течение + genitive is the standard phrase for "during [a period]" (not "в течении").

etymology: Derived from судить ("to judge"); the original sense is "that which is decided → fate".
commonMistakes: ирония судьбы is a standard idiom meaning "irony of fate".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for repeated/habitual hitting; use the perfective побить for a single completed beating.
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to hit".
commonMistakes: сердце бьётся is a standard intransitive collocation, "the heart beats".

synonymComparison.note: бить ('to beat repeatedly, imperfective') contrasts with ударить ('to strike once, perfective').

past.m.gloss: He was kicking the ball hard.

past.n.gloss: Everything was dazzling to the eye (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: The waves were pounding against the shore.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: Rain is beating against the window.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы бьём в барабаны на параде.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're beating the drums at the parade.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're shooting at the goal accurately.

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они бьют рекорды один за другим.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're breaking records one after another.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of surviving; use выживать for repeated/ongoing survival.
etymology: Prefix вы- ("out") plus жить ("to live") — "to live through".
commonMistakes: Distinguish выжить (to survive) from пережить (to live through / outlast something, a broader sense).

examples.ru: Мы выживаем благодаря поддержке друг друга.
examples.gloss: We survive thanks to supporting each other.

synonymComparison.note: выжить ('to survive,' more general) differs from уцелеть ('to remain unharmed/intact'), a close synonym for a different survival context.

past.f.gloss: She survived thanks to the doctors.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The business won't survive without investment.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you survive in these conditions?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll survive thanks to their experience.

imperative.sg.ru: Выживи во что бы то ни стало.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root for the numeral "seven".
commonMistakes: Like other numerals 5+, it's followed by the genitive plural (семь часов).

etymology: Related to долгий ("long"); the original sense is "something owed for a long time".
commonMistakes: Covers both "debt" and "duty/obligation" — context decides which.

etymology: Derived from беда ("hardship"); the sense developed to "afflicted → poor".
commonMistakes: Also used sympathetically to mean "poor [thing]" (бедный малыш = "poor little one").

etymology: Derived from отделить ("to separate").
commonMistakes: Distinguish отдел (a department) from отделение (a branch/ward).

etymology: Borrowed via French armée, from Latin armare ("to arm").
commonMistakes: A collective noun for the whole military — individual soldiers are солдат.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of stepping away; use отходить for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix от- ("away") plus идти ("to go").
commonMistakes: отойти от темы is a figurative idiom meaning "to stray from the topic".

governance.pattern: от + genitive (what one steps away from)

example.gloss: He stepped away from the window.

examples.gloss: He stepped away from the business (figurative).
The train departs in a minute.

examples.ru: Он постепенно отходит от старых привычек.
examples.gloss: He's gradually moving away from old habits.

synonymComparison.note: отойти ('to step a short distance away, temporarily') differs from уйти ('to leave entirely').

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll step away for a minute.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you step away from the door?

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы отойдём от основной темы ненадолго.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll briefly digress from the main topic.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you step away from the microphone?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll depart from the old strategy.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "new".
commonMistakes: свежие новости is a figurative collocation meaning "the latest news".

etymology: Derived from тяжесть ("weight").
commonMistakes: Covers both "heavy (physically)" and "hard/difficult (figuratively)" — mind the context.

etymology: From a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "middle" — a preposition.
commonMistakes: Takes среди + genitive (среди людей, not "среди людям").

etymology: Borrowed from Greek kyriakon ("house of the Lord").
commonMistakes: Distinguish храм (a more general "temple") from церковь (a Christian "church") in nuance.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of firing/dismissing; use увольнять for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix у- plus an archaic воля ("freedom") — "to free [from a job] → to fire".
commonMistakes: Don't confuse уволить (to fire someone, transitive) with увольняться (to quit on one's own, reflexive).

example.gloss: He was fired from his position.

examples.gloss: The company lays people off every quarter.

synonymComparison.note: уволить ('to fire,' can be for personal reasons) differs from сократить ('to lay off due to downsizing/restructuring').

past.n.gloss: Management would have fired him sooner.

past.pl.gloss: We let a few people go.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll fire him if it happens again.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you fire the whole team?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll only fire those at fault.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you fire me over this?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll fire the entire warehouse staff.

etymology: Derived from the root of брать ("to take"); the original sense is "taking [a wife] → marriage".
commonMistakes: A homograph: the "marriage" sense and the separate "defect/reject" sense come from entirely different etymological roots.

aspectUsage: The imperfective unidirectional verb of "carrying". понести is a related word meaning "to start carrying".
etymology: A basic verb tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to carry".
commonMistakes: нести ответственность is a standard figurative collocation meaning "to bear responsibility".

examples.gloss: She's carrying the child in her arms.
He bears responsibility for the decision.

synonymComparison.note: нести (unidirectional, carrying right now) contrasts with носить (multidirectional, habitually carrying) — the classic motion-verb pair.

past.m.gloss: He was carrying a heavy load.

past.f.gloss: She was carrying flowers to the wedding.

past.n.ru: Всё несло на себе отпечаток эпохи.
past.n.gloss: Everything bore the imprint of the era (figurative).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you carrying the load alone?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're carrying the banner at the front.

etymology: An adjective-origin noun derived from выходить ("to go out"); the original sense is "a day off work".
commonMistakes: As an adjective-origin noun, it declines like an adjective (hard-stem pattern).

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed instance of "making it in time"; use успевать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix у- plus an archaic спеть ("to hurry") — "to hurry and arrive in time".
commonMistakes: Takes успеть + infinitive (успеть сделать).

governance.pattern: infinitive (the action made in time) + на + accusative (what one makes it to, e.g. transport)

example.gloss: He made it to the train on time.

examples.gloss: She managed to finish the report in time.
He always makes it to meetings on time.
I'm not keeping up with the schedule.

synonymComparison.note: успеть ('to make it in time,' result-focused) differs from торопиться ('to hurry,' process-focused).

past.f.gloss: She made it to the flight.

past.n.gloss: Everything managed to happen before lunch.

past.pl.gloss: We managed to prepare in time.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll manage to finish this today.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you make it by six?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll make it to the meeting.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll manage to finish the project in time.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you make it to the train?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll manage to get everything ready.

imperative.sg.gloss: Make sure to come a bit early.

imperative.pl.gloss: Make sure to get seats in time.

etymology: The adverbial form of вероятный ("likely").
commonMistakes: Note the different confidence levels: возможно (lower confidence) versus вероятно (higher confidence).

aspectUsage: A delimitative perfective meaning "to stand for a while" — not a true perfective counterpart of стоять in the usual pairing sense.
etymology: Prefix по- (delimitative) plus стоять ("to stand").
commonMistakes: Постой! is a common everyday call meaning "Wait a sec!"

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to stand for a while, intransitive)

example.gloss: He stood by the door for a while.

examples.gloss: She stood in line for a bit.

examples.ru: Мы постояли на мосту, глядя на реку.
examples.gloss: We stood on the bridge for a while, looking at the river.

synonymComparison.note: постоять (a delimitative derivative of стоять, 'to stand for a while') differs from стоять (imperfective, standing continuously) by its time-limited sense.

past.m.gloss: He stood silently for a while.

past.f.gloss: She stood by the window for a bit.

past.n.ru: Всё постояло на месте и двинулось дальше.
past.n.gloss: Everything paused for a moment and then moved on (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We stood in silence for a minute.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll stand here for a bit.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you stand with me for a while?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll stand in the shade for a while.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll stand here for a while and wait.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you stand next to me for a bit?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll stand by the entrance for a while.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of putting on clothing; use надевать for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix на- plus an archaic деть ("to put") — "to put on".
commonMistakes: Distinguish надеть (putting clothing on oneself) from одеть (dressing someone else).

examples.gloss: He put on his coat before going out.
She put the ring on her finger.

examples.ru: Он надевает костюм каждый день на работу.
examples.gloss: He wears a suit to work every day.
I put on glasses for reading.

synonymComparison.note: надеть (the single act of putting something on) contrasts with носить (the habitual state of wearing it).

past.m.gloss: He put on a hat before the cold set in.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you put on a helmet?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll wear a tie to the meeting.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll put on uniforms for the performance.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you put on masks?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll wear suits to the party.

imperative.sg.gloss: Put on a hat, it's cold.

etymology: Derived from the root of помнить ("to remember").
commonMistakes: на память is a standard idiom meaning "as a keepsake".

etymology: Derived from the root of весело ("cheerfully").
commonMistakes: The short forms весел/весела/весело are used in predicate position.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of getting rid of something; use избавляться for repeated/ongoing instances.
etymology: Prefix из- plus an archaic бавить ("to leave/abandon") — "to take away".
commonMistakes: Takes избавиться от + genitive (избавиться от проблемы).

example.gloss: He got rid of the habit.

examples.gloss: She got rid of her stress.
We got rid of the old furniture.
He's gradually getting out of debt.

examples.ru: Мы избавляемся от ненужных вещей каждый год.
examples.gloss: We get rid of unnecessary things every year.

synonymComparison.note: избавиться ('to get rid of' something unwanted) differs from освободиться ('to become free' from a constraint).

past.m.gloss: He got rid of his fear.

past.f.gloss: She got rid of a bad habit.

past.n.gloss: Everything got rid of the excess.

past.pl.gloss: We got rid of our debts.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll get rid of this junk.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you get rid of the tension?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you get rid of the restrictions?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll do away with the old systems.

etymology: Derived from родить ("to give birth"); refers to Christ's birth.
commonMistakes: In Russia it's celebrated on January 7 per the Orthodox calendar — a different date than Western Christmas.

etymology: Derived from an archaic root meaning "to know".
commonMistakes: Distinguish известный (known) from знаменитый (famous, a stronger degree of renown).

etymology: Borrowed from French adresse.
commonMistakes: Mind the irregular plural адреса, with a stress shift.

aspectUsage: A biaspectual verb (same form for both aspects) meaning "to be born".
etymology: A reflexive derivative of родить ("to give birth").
commonMistakes: The past forms родился/родилась/родилось/родились are usually understood with perfective force.

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to be born, intransitive) + в + prepositional (place/year)

examples.gloss: She will be born next month (future sense).
He was born in 1990 (past sense, same form).

synonymComparison.note: родиться ('to be born,' a specific sense) differs from появиться ('to appear,' more general).

past.m.gloss: He was born in a small town.

past.pl.gloss: They were born on the same day.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я родюсь заново в этом деле (образно, редкое употребление).
nonpast.1sg.gloss: "I will be reborn in this work" (figurative, rare usage).

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты родишься вновь, если изменишь взгляды (образно, редкое употребление).
nonpast.2sg.gloss: "You'll be reborn if you change your views" (figurative, rare usage).

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The baby is due to be born in a month.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы родимся друг для друга заново (образно, редкое употребление).
nonpast.1pl.gloss: "We will be reborn for each other" (figurative, rare usage).

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы родитесь к новой жизни после этого решения (образно, редкое употребление).
nonpast.2pl.gloss: "You'll be born into a new life after this decision" (figurative, rare usage).

nonpast.3pl.gloss: The twins are due to be born in May.

imperative.sg.gloss: "Be born healthy" (a traditional blessing, rare usage).

imperative.pl.gloss: "Be born happy" (a traditional blessing, rare usage).

etymology: A vulgar word tracing to an old Slavic root, originally an insult.
collocations: expresses strong surprise or anger as an exclamation
commonMistakes: An extremely vulgar interjection/curse word — never appropriate in ordinary or formal conversation.

etymology: наконец ("finally") plus the emphatic particle -то.
commonMistakes: Carries a stronger sense of relief/exclamation than plain наконец.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of dancing; use the perfective станцевать for a single completed dance.
etymology: A verb based on a loan from German tanzen.
commonMistakes: Mind the stem alternation (танцевать→танцую, -ева- becomes -у- in 1st person).

examples.ru: Он станцевал один танец с ней.
examples.gloss: He danced one dance with her.

synonymComparison.note: танцевать ('to dance,' broad) differs from кружиться ('to spin/whirl'), which describes just one specific dance movement.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to dance with joy (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We were dancing at the wedding.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он танцует с ней каждый раз.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He dances with her every time.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We've been dancing together for a year now.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you dance at parties?

etymology: Negative prefix не- plus важно ("important") — an adverb/impersonal predicate.
commonMistakes: Besides "unimportant", it historically also carried a now-rare sense of "feeling unwell".

etymology: Derived from действовать ("to act").
commonMistakes: Covers "action", a drug's "effect", and a film's "plot/setting" — mind the context.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "meat".
commonMistakes: An uncountable collective noun used only in the singular.

aspectUsage: Imperfective expressing an ongoing state of regret. пожалеть is a related word that can also mean "to pity/spare" — not a true aspectual pair.
etymology: Prefix со- plus жалеть ("to pity").
commonMistakes: Takes сожалеть о + prepositional (сожалеть об ошибке).

examples.ru: Он пожалел о своём решении позже.

examples.gloss: She felt sorry for the stray cat (пожалеть can also mean 'to pity').

synonymComparison.note: сожалеть ('to regret,' relatively mild) differs from раскаиваться ('to repent,' a stronger, more moral form of regret).

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to regret the missed chance (figurative).

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He mourns the loss of his friend.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you regret what you said?

imperative.sg.gloss: Don't dwell on regrets about the past.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't regret the choice you made.

etymology: From an old word for a crossbred animal, developed into a human insult.
commonMistakes: An extremely insulting word — avoid it in ordinary conversation.

etymology: Borrowed from English "college", ultimately Latin collegium ("a community").
commonMistakes: In the Russian system, колледж refers to a less academically advanced vocational-level institution than a university.

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of touching/relating to; use the perfective коснуться for a single completed contact.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "to touch".
commonMistakes: что касается is a standard parenthetical meaning "as for...".

examples.gloss: Her hand is touching the keys.
The speaker touched on an important topic.

synonymComparison.note: касаться ('to touch lightly/concern,' takes genitive) differs from трогать ('to touch with the hand,' takes accusative) in government and nuance.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I don't touch on this topic.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You're touching on an important issue.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: This concerns each one of us.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you touching on personal matters?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: These rules apply to all clients.

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "stone", with a fleeting vowel (камень→камня).
commonMistakes: камень на сердце is a figurative idiom meaning "a weight on one's heart".

aspectUsage: Imperfective for the ongoing act of explaining; use the perfective объяснить for a single completed explanation.
etymology: The imperfective derivative of объяснить.
commonMistakes: Distinguish объяснять (the ongoing process) from объяснить (the completed act).

example.gloss: He's explaining the rule to me.

examples.gloss: The teacher explains the topic in detail.

examples.ru: Она объясняет своё решение каждый раз.
examples.gloss: She explains her decision every time.
He explained the situation to his boss.

synonymComparison.note: объяснить ('to explain,' a reason or mechanism) differs from рассказать ('to tell/narrate' events).

past.m.gloss: He was patiently explaining the rules.

past.f.gloss: She was explaining the assignment to the students.

past.pl.gloss: We were explaining the situation to clients.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm explaining the project to the team.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's explaining the reason for the refusal.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you explain the details in advance?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They explain the rules to newcomers.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of feeling; use чувствовать for an ongoing sensation/state.
etymology: Prefix по- plus чувствовать ("to feel").
commonMistakes: Takes почувствовать себя + instrumental adjective (почувствовать себя лучше = "to feel better").

examples.ru: Она почувствовала, что что-то не так.
examples.gloss: She sensed that something was wrong.
He feels guilty about the mistake.

synonymComparison.note: почувствовать ('to feel,' broad) is closely synonymous with ощутить ('to sense/perceive distinctly').

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to sense the change in the air (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We felt the tension in the room.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll feel the difference right away.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll feel the results in a month.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll feel relief.

imperative.sg.gloss: Make yourself at home (literally: feel as if at home).

etymology: A basic word tracing to a Proto-Indo-European root meaning "milk".
commonMistakes: An uncountable collective noun used only in the singular.

etymology: Derived from the root of надеяться ("to hope").
commonMistakes: терять надежду is a standard collocation meaning "to lose hope".

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of preparing/cooking; use готовить for repeated/ongoing cooking.
etymology: Prefix при- plus готовить ("to prepare").
commonMistakes: Distinguish приготовить (completed cooking) from готовить (the ongoing process).

examples.gloss: He's preparing a report for the meeting.

synonymComparison.note: приготовить ('to prepare/cook,' broad) differs from сварить ('to boil,' a specific cooking method).

past.f.gloss: She prepared the presentation in advance.

past.n.gloss: Everything was ready for the guests' arrival.

past.pl.gloss: We set up the stage for the performance.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll have lunch ready by two.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you make a cake for the celebration?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll have the report ready by Friday.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll get everything ready for the meeting.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you prepare the documents in advance?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll prepare the hall for the conference.

aspectUsage: Perfective for a single completed act of waking up; use просыпаться for repeated/habitual waking.
etymology: Prefix про- plus a root related to emerging from sleep.
commonMistakes: Distinguish проснуться (the moment of waking) from просыпаться (the habitual/ongoing process).

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to wake up, intransitive)

examples.gloss: She woke up from the noise.
I woke up in a good mood.

examples.ru: Он просыпается в семь каждый день.
examples.gloss: He wakes up at seven every day.
She often wakes up at night.

synonymComparison.note: проснуться ('to wake up,' the moment consciousness returns) differs from вставать ('to get out of bed'), a close synonym for a later stage.

past.m.gloss: He woke up in a cold sweat.

past.f.gloss: She was the first to wake up.

past.pl.gloss: We woke up at the same time.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll wake up a bit earlier tomorrow.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you wake up by eight?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you wake up in time for the train?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll wake up to the alarm clock.

imperative.pl.gloss: Wake up, it's time to get up.

etymology: Derived from старый ("old").
commonMistakes: Fairly casual/blunt in tone — use пожилой человек in polite contexts.

etymology: Borrowed from Italian soldato ("one who is paid").
commonMistakes: The plural genitive солдат is irregular, differing from the plural nominative солдаты.

etymology: в plus низ ("down") — a directional adverb.
commonMistakes: Distinguish вниз (directional "downward") from внизу (static "down below").

aspectUsage: Бросать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective бросить (to throw / to quit, a single completed act).
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Slavic root denoting the motion of throwing.
commonMistakes: Learners confuse ongoing/repeated бросать with the single completed act expressed by the perfective бросить.

examples.gloss: She's throwing stones into the water.
He always gives up on what he's started.
She threw the bag on the floor.

synonymComparison.note: бросать ('to throw,' general/neutral) is nearly synonymous with кидать ('to throw,' more colloquial).

past.m.gloss: He used to throw stones as a child.

past.f.gloss: She quit her job several times.

past.n.gloss: Everything was enough to make one shiver (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We were throwing the ball to each other.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm gradually giving up the habit.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You give up on everything halfway through.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He casts a shadow of doubt on the reputation (figurative).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you abandoning the project halfway?

aspectUsage: Убедиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective убеждаться.
etymology: From убедить (to convince) plus the reflexive -ся, built on the root вед- (knowing/leading).
commonMistakes: Confusing убедиться (to become convinced oneself) with убедить (to convince someone else).

example.gloss: He made sure he was right.

examples.gloss: She made sure the door was closed.
We confirmed the quality of the product.

examples.ru: Он снова убеждается в своей правоте.
examples.gloss: He's becoming convinced again that he's right.

examples.ru: Мы убеждаемся в этом каждый раз.
examples.gloss: We become convinced of this every time.

synonymComparison.note: убедиться ('to become convinced/sure,' a mental process) differs from проверить ('to check,' an actual action).

past.m.gloss: He became convinced of his mistake.

past.n.gloss: Everything proved itself in the end (figurative).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll make sure of that myself.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll become convinced that I'm right.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll become convinced he was wrong.
