nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll be able to confirm the quality yourself.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll become convinced the decision was right.

etymology: From на + верный (true/sure).
commonMistakes: Confusing the high-certainty наверняка ("for sure") with the more tentative наверное ("probably").

aspectUsage: Покинуть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective покидать.
etymology: Traces to Old Church Slavonic покинути.
commonMistakes: Confusing the abandonment-tinged покинуть with оставить (to leave something behind, without necessarily abandoning it).

examples.ru: Он никогда не покидает друзей в трудную минуту.
examples.gloss: He never abandons friends in a difficult moment.
Residents are leaving the city due to flooding.

synonymComparison.note: покинуть ('to leave/abandon' a place or person, more formal) differs from оставлять ('to leave behind' an object).

past.m.gloss: He left the hall to applause.

past.f.gloss: She voluntarily resigned from her post.

past.pl.gloss: We left the office at six.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you leave your family for your career?

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он покинет пост в конце года.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll step down from his post at year's end.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll leave the building in an hour.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you leave the company after the merger?

imperative.pl.gloss: Exit the hall through the door on the right.

aspectUsage: Опаздывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective опоздать.
etymology: Built on the root позд- (late).
commonMistakes: Confusing habitual/ongoing опаздывать with the single-instance perfective опоздать.

governance.pattern: на + accusative (thing one is late for)

example.gloss: He's running late for the meeting.

examples.gloss: Trains are often delayed in winter.

synonymComparison.note: опаздывать ('to be late for a set time') differs from задерживаться ('to be delayed/held up longer than planned').

past.n.gloss: Everything was running late this week.

past.pl.gloss: We were running late because of traffic.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's going to be late for the train.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're going to be late for the show.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you going to be late for the flight?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're always late for the meeting.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't be late for the rehearsal.

etymology: Derived from война (war).
commonMistakes: Overlooking that военный also functions as a noun meaning "serviceman," not just as an adjective.

aspectUsage: Сломать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective ломать.
etymology: From с- + ломать (to break).
commonMistakes: Confusing transitive "to break something" сломать with the reflexive/intransitive "to break down" сломаться.

examples.gloss: The construction workers are demolishing the old building.

synonymComparison.note: сломать ('to break,' broad) differs from разбить ('to shatter/smash,' glass or similar), which specifies the manner of breaking.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll break the phone doing that.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll undermine the system from within (figurative).

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll break down the old barriers (figurative).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll break tradition with this decision.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll break stereotypes about the profession.

etymology: From особа (person/individual) plus the suffix -енный.
commonMistakes: Confusing everyday "special" особенный with the more formal/official "specific" особый.

etymology: From Proto-Slavic *cvětъ, historically sharing a root with цветок (flower).
commonMistakes: "Color" цвет and "flower" цветок share a root but differ in meaning, and their plurals also differ: цвета (colors) vs. цветы (flowers).

etymology: From the imperative of здравствовать ("to be healthy").
commonMistakes: Confusing the informal ты-form здравствуй with the formal/plural вы-form здравствуйте.

etymology: A diminutive of руб (cloth/garment).
commonMistakes: Confusing the modern "shirt" рубашка with the looser, more old-fashioned рубаха.

aspectUsage: Судить is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for its general sense. посудить exists as a delimitative meaning "to judge/reflect for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sǫditi.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to judge" судить with "to condemn/sentence" осудить.

governance.pattern: accusative (person judged) + о + prepositional (what is judged)

example.ru: Не судите о людях по внешности.
example.gloss: Don't judge people by their appearance.

examples.gloss: The judge is trying the case fairly.

synonymComparison.note: судить ('to judge/referee,' more authoritative) differs from оценивать ('to evaluate,' more neutral).

past.n.gloss: Everything was judged strictly by the law.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы судим о книге по содержанию.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We judge the book by its content.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're judging us too quickly.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They judge based on their own experience.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't judge by a single meeting.

etymology: Adverb derived from весёлый (cheerful).
commonMistakes: Confusing the adverb/predicate весело ("fun") with the adjective весёлый describing a person.

etymology: From the archaic adjective гораздый (skilled/able), whose meaning shifted into an intensifier.
commonMistakes: Гораздо is used only with comparatives, confused with очень ("very"), which pairs with plain adjectives.

etymology: From ванна (bathtub) with an adjectival ending, substantivized into a noun.
commonMistakes: Confusing "bathroom" (the room) ванная with "bathtub" (the fixture) ванна.

etymology: From в + первые (first ones).
commonMistakes: Confusing "for the first time" впервые with "at first/initially" сначала, which marks temporal sequence rather than a first-ever occurrence.

aspectUsage: Получаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective получиться.
etymology: From получать (to receive) plus the reflexive -ся, shifted to mean "to turn out."
commonMistakes: Confusing "to turn out/work out" получаться with "to receive" получать, which concerns a concrete object.

governance.pattern: у + genitive (the person it's working out for) — impersonal construction

example.gloss: I'm managing/it's working out for me.

examples.gloss: He managed to pass the exam.

synonymComparison.note: получаться ('to turn out/work out,' result-focused) is nearly synonymous with удаваться ('to succeed,' more formal); получаться is more natural in everyday speech.

past.m.gloss: Everything used to come easily to him.

past.f.gloss: The photo was turning out blurry.

past.n.gloss: Everything was going according to plan.

nonpast.1sg.ru: У меня получается медленно, но верно.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm making progress slowly but surely.

nonpast.2sg.ru: У тебя получается лучше, чем раньше.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: Our new strategy is working out.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you managing to retain clients?

imperative.sg.ru: Получайся, пожалуйста, с первого раза (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Please work out on the first try" (figurative, rare usage, addressed to a thing/outcome).

imperative.pl.ru: Получайтесь удачно, задуманные планы (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.pl.gloss: "May you turn out well, planned things" (figurative, rare usage).

aspectUsage: Дышать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of breathing. подышать exists as a delimitative meaning "to breathe for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *dyšati.
commonMistakes: Confusing continuous дышать with the single in/out breath verbs вдохнуть/выдохнуть, which are true perfectives of different verbs.

examples.gloss: She's breathing heavily after the run.

synonymComparison.note: дышать ('to breathe,' a general continuous action) differs from вдыхать ('to inhale,' specifically the inward breath).

past.f.gloss: She was breathing steadily in her sleep.

past.pl.gloss: We were breathing the fresh mountain air.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I breathe deeply before a performance.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We breathe the same air (also used figuratively).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Can you breathe freely now?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're breathing the clean sea air.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *čьjь. Its forms are masculine чей, feminine чья, neuter чьё, and plural чьи.
commonMistakes: Чей agrees in gender/number with the noun it modifies, not with the possessor — a frequent error for learners.

aspectUsage: Бороться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general sense of struggling. побороться exists as a delimitative meaning "to fight for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *borti sę.
commonMistakes: Confusing ongoing бороться ("to struggle/fight") with победить ("to win"), a separate verb and not its perfective pair.

governance.pattern: с + instrumental (what one fights against) + за + accusative (what one fights for)

synonymComparison.note: бороться ('to fight/struggle,' broad, also figurative) differs from сражаться ('to do battle,' more military/physical).

past.pl.gloss: We fought until the very end.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you fighting for your independence?

aspectUsage: Отправляться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective отправиться.
etymology: From отправлять (to send) plus the reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to set off oneself" отправляться with "to send something/someone" отправлять.

examples.gloss: We usually set off early in the morning.
He set off on a journey.

examples.ru: Они отправились в горы на выходные.
examples.gloss: They set off for the mountains for the weekend.

synonymComparison.note: отправляться ('to depart/set off,' often used for transport/journeys) is closely related to уезжать ('to leave,' more general).

past.m.ru: Он отправлялся в путь с рассветом.
past.m.gloss: He used to set off at dawn.

past.f.gloss: The expedition set off every year.

past.n.gloss: Everything used to depart on schedule.

past.pl.gloss: We used to set off together.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm setting off on vacation tomorrow.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you heading off on a business trip?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The train departs in five minutes.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you heading to the conference?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're setting off on an expedition.

etymology: From водить (to drive/lead) plus the agent suffix -тель.
commonMistakes: Confusing the modern, neutral "driver" водитель with the older/more informal шофёр.

etymology: From какой (what kind) plus -ство.
commonMistakes: "Quality" качество and "quantity" количество sound similar but have opposite meanings.

etymology: Acronym for Федеральное бюро расследований (Federal Bureau of Investigation).
commonMistakes: ФБР is indeclinable; agreement would formally follow the core noun бюро (neuter), though colloquially it is sometimes treated as masculine.

etymology: From место (place) plus the suffix -ный.
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective местный ("local") with the noun местность ("locality").

etymology: From French signal, Latin signum.
commonMistakes: Confusing the noun сигнал ("signal") with the verb сигналить ("to signal/honk").

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *ostrovъ, referring to that which is cut off / surrounded by water.
commonMistakes: The plural is the irregular острова (with a stress shift), not островы.

etymology: A diminutive of сын (son).
commonMistakes: Confusing the affectionate address term сынок (also used toward young men generally) with the neutral сын.

aspectUsage: Вызывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective вызвать.
etymology: From вы- + зывать (to call), related to звать.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to summon/provoke" вызывать with the unrelated "to name/call something" называть, despite surface similarity.

examples.gloss: The teacher calls on students in turn.
The film sparked a storm of emotions.

synonymComparison.note: вызывать ('to cause,' neutral) differs from провоцировать ('to provoke,' more deliberate).

past.f.gloss: She drew admiration from her colleagues.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you calling a technician to your home?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They provoke envy in many people.

aspectUsage: Решать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective решить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *rešiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing process of deciding/solving решать with the completed result решить.

synonymComparison.note: решать ('to decide/solve,' broad) differs from определять ('to determine/define,' more specific).

past.m.gloss: He was solving problems all night.

past.f.gloss: She was trying to decide what to do next.

past.n.gloss: Everything was being decided at the board meeting.

past.pl.gloss: We were solving the problem together.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Is the issue decided collectively?

etymology: Borrowed from French/English sexuel/sexual, ultimately from Latin sexus.
commonMistakes: Сексуальный can mean both the clinical "sexual" and the colloquial "sexy" — context determines which.

aspectUsage: Расслабиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective расслабляться.
etymology: Built on the root слабый (weak).
commonMistakes: Confusing the achieved relaxed state расслабиться with the ongoing process расслабляться.

examples.gloss: She relaxed after a tough day.
We relaxed for the first time in a week.

examples.ru: Он расслабляется под музыку каждый вечер.
examples.gloss: He relaxes to music every evening.

synonymComparison.note: расслабиться ('to relax,' releasing tension, also physical) differs from успокоиться ('to calm down,' emotion-focused).

past.m.ru: Он расслабился впервые за долгое время.
past.m.gloss: He relaxed for the first time in a long while.

past.f.gloss: She relaxed in a warm bath.

past.n.gloss: The whole room seemed to relax (figurative).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you ever relax?

etymology: From воз- + расти (to grow), denoting "how much one has grown."
commonMistakes: Confusing "age" возраст with век, which only means "old age" in certain fixed expressions.

aspectUsage: Ошибаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective ошибиться.
etymology: Related to the root шиб- (to strike), with the idea of "missing the mark."
commonMistakes: Confusing habitual "to be wrong" ошибаться with the single mistake expressed by ошибиться.

governance.pattern: в + prepositional (thing one is wrong about)

example.gloss: He's making a mistake in his calculations.

synonymComparison.note: ошибаться ('to be mistaken,' one's own error) differs from путать ('to mix up/confuse'), which implies conflating things.

past.n.gloss: Everything about this forecast was wrong (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We were wrong about the deadlines.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я не ошибаюсь на этот счёт.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're sometimes wrong in our forecasts.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're mistaken about me.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They regularly make errors in their calculations.

aspectUsage: Признать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective признавать.
etymology: From при- + знать (to know).
commonMistakes: Confusing "to acknowledge/admit" признать with the more personal/emotional "to confess" признаться.

examples.gloss: The world is gradually recognizing these rights.

synonymComparison.note: признать ('to admit/acknowledge' a fact or mistake) differs from согласиться ('to agree' with an opinion or proposal).

past.f.gloss: She acknowledged her colleague was right.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он признает факт только под давлением.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He only admits the fact under pressure.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you acknowledge your responsibility?

aspectUsage: Научиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective учиться.
etymology: From на- + учиться (to study/learn).
commonMistakes: Confusing the achieved skill научиться with the ongoing process of studying учиться.

examples.gloss: He learned to cook on his own.
She learned the language in a year.
He's learning to play the guitar.

synonymComparison.note: научиться ('to learn/become able to,' the process) differs from уметь ('to know how to,' the resulting state) — an important related pair.

past.m.gloss: He learned to drive a car.

past.n.gloss: Everything learned to run on its own (figurative).

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll learn the new software quickly.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll learn to work more efficiently.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you learn a new language?

aspectUsage: Совершить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective совершать.
etymology: From со- + вершить (to complete, from верх/вершина "top/peak").
commonMistakes: Overlooking that the formal/elevated совершить ("to commit/carry out") differs in register from the general сделать ("to do").

examples.gloss: We carry out deals every day.

synonymComparison.note: совершить ('to accomplish/commit,' a notable act) differs from выполнить ('to carry out/fulfill' an assigned task).

past.m.gloss: He made a breakthrough in science.

past.f.gloss: She took a tour around the city.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты совершишь поступок, о котором пожалеешь.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы совершим прорыв в этом году.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll make a breakthrough this year.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you take the trip in the fall?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они совершат переход к новой системе.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll carry out the transition to the new system.

aspectUsage: Гордиться is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general state of being proud. погордиться exists as a delimitative meaning "to feel proud for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: From гордый (proud) plus -иться.
commonMistakes: Гордиться takes the instrumental case (гордиться кем/чем); using the genitive or accusative instead is a frequent error.

examples.gloss: We're proud of the team's achievements.

synonymComparison.note: гордиться ('to be proud,' an internal feeling) differs from хвалиться ('to boast,' showing off to others).

past.m.gloss: He was proud of his children.

past.f.gloss: She was proud of the work's result.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed proud of its heritage (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We were proud of our history.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you proud of your success?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you proud of your work?

etymology: From French aéroport, Greek aero- plus French port.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "в аэропорту" rather than the standard "в аэропорте."

etymology: The singular imperative of the perfective поверить (to believe).
commonMistakes: Поверь functions almost as a discourse interjection ("believe me") rather than a literal command in casual speech.

aspectUsage: Управлять is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general sense of managing/driving. поуправлять exists as a delimitative meaning "to manage/drive for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: From у- + править (to rule/steer), related to прав- (right/correct).
commonMistakes: Управлять takes the instrumental case (чем); using the accusative instead is a frequent error.

synonymComparison.note: управлять ('to manage/operate,' can include physically operating something) differs from руководить ('to lead/direct,' limited to human leadership).

past.m.gloss: He ran the factory for ten years.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you manage the finances yourselves?

etymology: From опасный (dangerous) plus -ость.
commonMistakes: Confusing the threat itself опасность with риск, which concerns probability/chance of harm.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *rodъ.
commonMistakes: Conflating the senses of grammatical gender, type/kind, and clan/lineage, all carried by род.

etymology: A derivative of коло (circle), Proto-Slavic.
commonMistakes: The genitive plural колец looks irregular but needs no inserted vowel, since the stem already contains one.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin linea via Polish/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing the geometric/abstract линия ("line") with очередь ("a queue of people") — a false-friend trap for English speakers.

aspectUsage: Выбирать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective выбрать.
etymology: From вы- + бирать (to pick/take, related to брать).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing process of choosing выбирать with the completed choice выбрать.

governance.pattern: accusative (thing chosen) + из + genitive (from among what)

example.gloss: She's choosing a dress from among many.

synonymComparison.note: выбирать ('to choose,' an act of decision) differs from предпочитать ('to prefer,' merely indicating a preference).

past.m.gloss: He was choosing for a long time.

past.f.gloss: She was carefully choosing a gift.

past.n.gloss: Everything was being chosen according to taste.

past.pl.gloss: We were choosing a place for vacation.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you choosing between two offers?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They choose their strategy in advance.

aspectUsage: Поздравлять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поздравить.
etymology: Related to здравие (health/well-being); originally meant "to wish someone well."
commonMistakes: Поздравлять requires "с + instrumental"; omitting с or using the wrong case is a frequent error.

example.ru: Он поздравляет её с днём рождения.
example.gloss: He's congratulating her on her birthday.

examples.ru: Мы поздравляем коллег с победой каждый раз.
examples.gloss: We congratulate colleagues on their wins every time.

examples.ru: Он поздравляет всех с праздником лично.
examples.gloss: He personally congratulates everyone on the holiday.
She congratulated her friend on his success.
He congratulated the team on their win.

synonymComparison.note: поздравлять ('to congratulate') differs from благодарить ('to thank') in purpose — celebrating vs. expressing gratitude.

past.m.gloss: He used to congratulate everyone by phone.

past.f.gloss: She was personally congratulating the guests.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to congratulate us on our success (figurative).

past.pl.ru: Мы поздравляли друг друга с праздником.
past.pl.gloss: We were congratulating each other on the holiday.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I congratulate you on your success.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's congratulating the staff on the anniversary.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We congratulate clients on the holidays.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you congratulate employees in person?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're congratulating us on the anniversary.

etymology: From the plural of the archaic adjective многий (many).
commonMistakes: Confusing the plural-only, noun/adjective-like многие with много ("much/many"), which takes the genitive and denotes general quantity.

etymology: From при- + ятный (acceptable, related to имати "to take/receive").
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective приятный, describing a person or thing, with the adverb/predicate приятно ("it is pleasant").

etymology: From король (king) plus the feminine suffix -ева; король itself derives from Carolus (Charlemagne).
commonMistakes: Confusing the Carolus-derived королева with царица, a distinct Russian/Slavic tsarist title.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *lъžь.
commonMistakes: The oblique forms shift to the stem лж- (лжи, not ложи) — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Обсудить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective обсуждать.
etymology: From об- + судить (to judge).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed discussion обсудить with the ongoing discussion обсуждать.

examples.gloss: Colleagues are constantly discussing the news.
We've been discussing this issue for weeks.

synonymComparison.note: обсудить ('to discuss,' verbal) differs from рассматривать ('to consider/review,' more analytical/written).

past.m.gloss: He discussed the issue with his colleagues.

past.f.gloss: She discussed the plan with management.

past.pl.gloss: We discussed the budget for the year.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я обсужу это с тобой позже.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll discuss this with you later.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you discuss this with your boss?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll discuss the strategy at the meeting.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you discuss the contract details?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll discuss the action plan tomorrow.

imperative.pl.gloss: Discuss the issue with the whole team.

aspectUsage: Продолжить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective продолжать.
etymology: From про- + длить (to extend, from длина "length").
commonMistakes: Confusing the single act of resuming продолжить with the ongoing continuation продолжать.

examples.ru: Мы продолжили переговоры на следующий день.
examples.gloss: We continued the negotiations the next day.

examples.ru: Он продолжает учиться несмотря на трудности.
examples.gloss: He keeps studying despite the difficulties.

examples.ru: Мы продолжаем сотрудничество уже пять лет.
examples.gloss: We've been continuing our cooperation for five years already.

synonymComparison.note: продолжить ('to continue' without interruption) differs from возобновить ('to resume' after a pause).

past.f.ru: Она продолжила карьеру в другой компании.
past.f.gloss: She continued her career at another company.

past.pl.ru: Мы продолжили спор на следующий день.
past.pl.gloss: We continued the argument the next day.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you continue studying after the break?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll continue the presentation in a minute.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы продолжим проект в следующем квартале.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll continue the project next quarter.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you continue the negotiations later?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll continue the research in the future.

etymology: From French saison, Latin satio (sowing time).
commonMistakes: Confusing сезон (TV/sports season) with время года (season of the year in the calendar sense).

aspectUsage: Показаться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective казаться.
etymology: From по- + казаться (to seem).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single-impression/appearance показаться with the ongoing impression казаться.

example.gloss: It seemed to me that he was sad.

examples.gloss: It seemed to her that the door was open.
His silence seemed strange to us.

synonymComparison.note: показаться/казаться ('to seem,' a subjective impression) differs from выглядеть ('to look,' a visual impression) — an important contrast.

past.n.ru: Всё показалось простым на первый взгляд.
past.n.gloss: Everything seemed simple at first glance.

past.pl.gloss: They seemed pleased with the result.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я покажусь странным, если скажу это.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll seem strange if I say this.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll appear calm on the outside.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы покажемся наивными с этим планом.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll seem naive with this plan.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll come across as convincing at the meeting.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll seem confident in the negotiations.

imperative.sg.ru: Покажись увереннее на интервью (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Come across as more confident at the interview" (figurative, rare usage).

imperative.pl.ru: Покажитесь достойно на презентации (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.pl.gloss: "Present yourselves with dignity at the presentation" (figurative, rare usage).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *strachъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing general "fear" страх with the stronger "horror" ужас.

etymology: From ни + куда (to where).
commonMistakes: Confusing никуда (nowhere, with motion verbs) with нигде (nowhere, with static location verbs).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *zъlo.
commonMistakes: Confusing the abstract noun зло ("evil") with the adjective злой describing a person or thing.

etymology: A derivative of смотреть/глядеть (to look) with the prefix в-.
commonMistakes: Confusing взгляд (a glance, or a figurative "viewpoint") with зрение (eyesight, the physical sense).

etymology: From большой (large) plus -инство.
commonMistakes: Confusing большинство ("the majority of," countable) with многие ("many"), a different quantifier.

etymology: An adjective derived from сложить (to put together).
commonMistakes: Confusing multi-part "complex" сложный with simply "hard to do" трудный.

aspectUsage: Открывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective открыть.
etymology: From крыть (to cover) plus the prefix от-.
commonMistakes: Confusing ongoing/habitual открывать with the completed result открыть.

examples.gloss: She opens the shop at nine.
He opened the door with a key.

synonymComparison.note: открывать ('to open,' physical/general) differs from раскрыть ('to open wide/reveal,' more figurative/thorough).

past.m.gloss: He used to open the shop every morning.

past.f.ru: Она открывала новые возможности для всех.
past.f.gloss: She was opening up new opportunities for everyone.

past.n.ru: Всё открывалось для посетителей в десять.
past.n.gloss: Everything used to open to visitors at ten.

past.pl.ru: Мы открывали счета в банке регулярно.
past.pl.gloss: We regularly opened accounts at the bank.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я открываю новое направление в бизнесе.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm opening up a new business direction.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You open the door too abruptly.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он открывает новую страницу в жизни.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's turning a new page in his life (figurative).

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы открываете офис в новом городе?
nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you opening an office in a new city?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они открывают филиалы по всей стране.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're opening branches across the country.

imperative.pl.gloss: Open the doors one at a time.

aspectUsage: Подписать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective подписывать.
etymology: From под- + писать (to write).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of signing подписать with the ongoing/repeated signing process подписывать.

examples.ru: Мы подписываем контракты с партнёрами регулярно.
examples.gloss: We regularly sign contracts with partners.

synonymComparison.note: подписать ('to sign,' the final procedural act) differs from заключить ('to conclude a deal,' the agreement itself coming into being).

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы подпишем договор на следующей неделе.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll sign the contract next week.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you sign the agreement today?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll sign the papers after the review.

etymology: Borrowed via Polish/German, ultimately from Italian palla (ball).
commonMistakes: Confusing "bullet" пуля with "cartridge" патрон, which includes the casing.

etymology: From от + туда (to there).
commonMistakes: Confusing "from there" оттуда with "from here" отсюда.

etymology: From the Proto-Slavic root маз- (to smear/grease).
commonMistakes: Масло broadly covers both "butter" and "oil"; unlike English, it is one word, disambiguated by context (сливочное = butter, растительное/моторное = oil).

etymology: Borrowed from French normal, Latin norma.
commonMistakes: Colloquially нормальный can mean "decent/good enough," not just statistically average — easy to miss.

etymology: Shortened from фотография, from Greek phos (light) + graphein (to write).
commonMistakes: Фото is indeclinable in every case, unlike the full form фотография, which declines normally.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *mostъ.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form often takes the locative-type ending "на мосту" rather than "на мосте."

etymology: From French bombe, Latin bombus (booming sound).
commonMistakes: Confusing бомба (the device) with взрыв (the resulting explosion/event).

aspectUsage: Позвать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective звать.
etymology: From по- + звать (to call).
commonMistakes: Confusing позвать (to call someone over) with позвонить (to phone someone), a separate verb.

examples.gloss: He called a friend for help.
We invited everyone to the celebration.
What's your name? (literally: what do they call you).

synonymComparison.note: позвать ('to call out to,' casual/everyday) differs from вызывать ('to summon,' more formal).

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to call him back (figurative).

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я позову тебя, когда будет готово.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll call you when it's ready.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you invite him to the party?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you invite us to the wedding?

aspectUsage: Позволять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective позволить.
etymology: From по- + волить (to permit, from воля "will").
commonMistakes: Confusing everyday позволять ("to allow") with the more formal/official разрешать ("to authorize").

example.gloss: He allows the children to play.

examples.gloss: She rarely allows herself to rest.
The budget allows us to travel.

synonymComparison.note: позволять ('to allow,' broad — resources/circumstances can be the subject) differs from разрешать ('to permit,' more official/regulatory).

past.m.gloss: He used to allow himself a lot.

past.f.gloss: She used to let the children go out alone.

past.pl.gloss: We sometimes allowed ourselves a luxury.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я позволяю себе отдых по выходным.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I allow myself rest on weekends.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You let him get away with too much.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We let clients choose the terms.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you allow employees to work remotely?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They sometimes allow themselves too much.

etymology: From French scène, Latin scaena.
commonMistakes: Confusing the physical "stage" or a narrative "scene" сцена with эпизод (episode, a narrative segment).

etymology: Borrowed from English test.
commonMistakes: Confusing тест (test/quiz) with тесто (dough) — similar-looking but unrelated (genitive теста vs. тесто).

etymology: From ни + как (how).
commonMistakes: Confusing никак ("cannot by any means," with a verb) with ничуть ("not at all," negating degree).

etymology: From не + давно (long ago).
commonMistakes: Confusing недавно ("recently") with давно ("long ago/for a long time") — near-opposite meanings from similar-looking words.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin professor via German/French.
commonMistakes: The plural is the irregular, stress-shifted профессора, not профессоры.

aspectUsage: Опоздать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective опаздывать.
etymology: Built on the root позд- (late).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed lateness опоздать with the habitual/ongoing опаздывать.

governance.pattern: на + accusative (thing one is late for)

examples.gloss: She was late for the interview.
We were late for the start of the show.

examples.ru: Автобусы опаздывают в это время года.
examples.gloss: Buses run late at this time of year.

synonymComparison.note: опоздать ('to be late for a set time,' perfective) differs from задержаться ('to be held up/delayed longer than planned').

past.m.gloss: He was very late for work.

past.f.gloss: She was only a minute late.

past.n.ru: Всё опоздало на этой неделе из-за погоды.
past.n.gloss: Everything was delayed this week because of the weather.

past.pl.ru: Мы опоздали из-за аварии на дороге.
past.pl.gloss: We were late because of an accident on the road.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я опоздаю на пять минут сегодня.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll be five minutes late today.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll be late if you don't hurry.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's definitely going to miss his flight.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll be a bit late for the meeting.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you be late for the ceremony?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're definitely going to miss the train.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't be late for the exam.

etymology: From не + счастный (from счастье "happiness").
commonMistakes: Confusing the stative adjective несчастный with the noun несчастье (misfortune).

etymology: From French sergent, Latin serviens (serving).
commonMistakes: Confusing the non-commissioned rank сержант with the broader category of "officer" офицер.

etymology: From не + вероятно (likely, from вера "faith").
commonMistakes: Невероятно can act as an intensifier ("incredibly") or carry its literal meaning ("unbelievably") — context determines which.

aspectUsage: Наблюдать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective понаблюдать.
etymology: Borrowed partly via Church Slavonic, related to блюсти (to watch over).
commonMistakes: Confusing systematic/scientific "to observe" наблюдать with simply "to watch/look at" смотреть.

examples.gloss: We're monitoring how the situation develops.
He observed the process for a while.
Let's observe the reaction for a bit.

synonymComparison.note: наблюдать ('to observe,' neutral) differs from следить ('to track/monitor closely,' more vigilant/sustained).

past.m.ru: Он наблюдал за игрой с трибуны.
past.m.gloss: He watched the game from the stands.

past.f.gloss: She silently watched what was happening.

past.n.gloss: Everything was being observed from the outside.

past.pl.gloss: We were monitoring the project's progress.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты наблюдаешь за детьми на площадке?
nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you watching the kids at the playground?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you constantly watch the weather?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они наблюдают за показателями каждый день.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They monitor the metrics every day.

etymology: From French variante, Latin varians.
commonMistakes: Confusing вариант (an option/version) with альтернатива (alternative, implying an exclusive either/or choice).

etymology: From Church Slavonic, ultimately from Hebrew Shabbat.
commonMistakes: The double б spelling (суббота) is often misspelled with a single б by learners.

etymology: From Italian gazzetta, via French/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing "newspaper" газета with "magazine" журнал — both print media but different formats.

etymology: From спать (to sleep) plus -льня.
commonMistakes: Confusing "bedroom" (the room) спальня with "bed" (the furniture) кровать.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *zvukъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing general "sound" звук with шум (noise, specifically unwanted/loud sound).

aspectUsage: Злиться is imperfective, denoting the general state of being angry. The perfective разозлиться is a related verb meaning "to become angry" — a transition into that state, not a true pair.
etymology: From злой (angry/evil) plus -иться.
commonMistakes: Mistaking злиться and разозлиться for a true aspectual pair, when they actually relate a state to its onset.

governance.pattern: на + accusative (person/thing one is angry at)

examples.gloss: She sometimes gets angry for no reason.

synonymComparison.note: злиться ('to be angry,' a stronger emotion) differs from раздражаться ('to get irritated,' a milder annoyance).

past.m.ru: Он злился на себя за ошибку.
past.m.gloss: He was angry at himself for the mistake.

past.n.gloss: Everything in that house seemed on edge (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We were constantly angry at the system.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я злюсь, когда меня не слушают.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I get angry when I'm not listened to.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You're angry at me for nothing.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's angry about his colleague's lateness.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you angry about the new rules?

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't be angry at each other.

etymology: Derived from значить (to mean).
commonMistakes: Confusing "meaning/significance" значение with смысл (sense, more about underlying purpose/logic).

etymology: A diminutive of рука (hand).
commonMistakes: Ручка carries two common senses — "pen" and "door handle" — both from "little hand," which learners often confuse.

aspectUsage: Привезти is perfective, pairing with the imperfective привозить.
etymology: From при- + везти (to carry by vehicle).
commonMistakes: Confusing привезти (to bring by vehicle) with принести (to bring by carrying on foot) — distinguished by mode of transport.

examples.gloss: She brought fruit from the market.
We brought furniture from the store.
He brings in goods every week.
We bring food from the village.

synonymComparison.note: привезти ('to bring by vehicle') differs from принести ('to bring by carrying in hand') in the means of transport.

past.f.gloss: She brought the kids for the weekend.

past.n.gloss: Everything was brought in on time.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll bring souvenirs from the trip.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you bring the documents with you?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll deliver the cargo tomorrow morning.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll bring the materials to the construction site.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you bring samples to the meeting?

etymology: A derivative of жалеть (to pity) with the prefix со-.
commonMistakes: The frequent collocation к сожалению ("unfortunately") is often confused with раскаяние (remorse, implying guilt over one's own actions).

etymology: Derived from грозить (to threaten).
commonMistakes: Confusing угроза (the declared threat itself) with опасность (danger, the general risk/hazard).

etymology: A slang derivative of дурак (fool) with the prefix при-.
commonMistakes: Придурок is a slang insult, inappropriate in polite settings — easy to overlook.

etymology: From French parc, ultimately from Medieval Latin parricus.
commonMistakes: Confusing парк (a public green space) with сад (garden, more cultivated/private).

etymology: From благо (good) + дать (to give), the originally verbal "to thank" grammaticalized into a preposition.
commonMistakes: Благодаря takes the dative and is used for positive causes, distinguishing it from из-за (negative cause, taking the genitive) — easy to overlook.

etymology: From на + всегда (always).
commonMistakes: Confusing навсегда (forever, a permanent end-state) with всегда (always, a habitual/recurring state).

etymology: From в plus an old case form of полный (full).
commonMistakes: Confusing вполне (quite, a moderate intensifier) with совсем (completely, an absolute intensifier) — overlapping but different in strength.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sokъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing сок (juice) with сироп (syrup, a thicker sweetened liquid).

aspectUsage: Ложиться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective лечь.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *lagati, related to лежать (to be lying).
commonMistakes: Confusing the process of lying down ложиться with already being in a lying position лежать — both imperfective but different in meaning.

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to lie down, intransitive)

examples.gloss: She goes to bed early every evening.
Snow is quietly settling on the ground.
He lay down on the sofa.

synonymComparison.note: ложиться ('to lie down') differs from садиться ('to sit down'), which has its own aspect pair садиться/сесть.

past.m.gloss: He used to go to bed late every day.

past.f.ru: Она ложилась с книгой в руках.
past.f.gloss: She used to lie down with a book in her hands.

past.n.ru: Всё ложилось на свои места постепенно.
past.n.gloss: Everything was gradually falling into place (figurative).

past.pl.ru: Мы ложились спать вместе в детстве.
past.pl.gloss: We used to go to bed together as children.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I go to bed at ten.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you usually go to bed this late?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's being admitted for surgery tomorrow.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы ложимся спать раньше в будни.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We go to bed earlier on weekdays.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you often go to bed after midnight?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They go to bed on a schedule.

imperative.sg.gloss: Go to bed a bit earlier today.

imperative.pl.gloss: Go to sleep, it's already late.

etymology: From French surprise.
commonMistakes: Confusing сюрприз (a planned, intentional surprise) with неожиданность (an unexpected occurrence, not necessarily planned).

aspectUsage: Относиться is an imperfective stative verb with no perfective counterpart in the sense of "to relate to/treat."
etymology: From носить (to carry) plus the prefix от- and reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to treat/regard" относиться with the literal "to carry" носить.

examples.ru: Этот вопрос относится к другой теме.
examples.gloss: This question relates to a different topic.

synonymComparison.note: относиться ('to have an attitude toward' / 'to belong to a category') differs from касаться ('to concern/relate to').

past.pl.ru: Мы относились к проекту с энтузиазмом.
past.pl.gloss: We approached the project with enthusiasm.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты относишься к ней с уважением.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you take risks seriously?

imperative.pl.ru: Относитесь друг к другу с терпением.

etymology: From French cabinet.
commonMistakes: Confusing кабинет (a private office/study) with офис (office, the broader business workspace).

aspectUsage: Напугать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective пугать.
etymology: From на- + пугать (to frighten).
commonMistakes: Confusing напугать (to scare someone, pf) with испугаться (to become scared oneself), a separate reflexive verb.

examples.gloss: He frightens children with his stories.

synonymComparison.note: напугать and испугать are near-synonyms for 'to frighten/scare,' with only slight differences in usage context.

past.m.gloss: He scared everyone with his shout.

past.f.gloss: She startled the guests with a joke.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll give him a sudden scare.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll scare the little one with that sound.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll startle the neighbors with his appearance.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll surprise them with a sudden visit.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll scare everyone with this news.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll startle the audience with the effect.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't scare the children with a loud noise.

etymology: From French lieutenant.
commonMistakes: Confusing лейтенант (a specific rank) with капитан (a higher rank), both military/police titles.

etymology: A derivative of за- + дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Confusing задача (a task/problem with a goal) with задание (an assignment, more about given instructions).

aspectUsage: Приходиться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective прийтись.
etymology: From ходить (to come) plus the prefix при- and reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing the impersonal "to have to" приходиться with the literal, repeated "to come" sense related to ходить.

governance.pattern: dative (person obligated) + infinitive (action required) — impersonal construction

example.gloss: He has to work a lot.

examples.gloss: We have to economize every month.
She has to get up early.

synonymComparison.note: приходиться ('to be forced by circumstances to') differs from нужно ('to simply need to').

past.m.gloss: He had only one way out (figuratively, 'no choice').

past.f.gloss: The situation happened to be convenient (a different sense: 'to come in handy').

past.n.gloss: Everything had to be explained all over again.

past.pl.gloss: We were forced into difficult decisions.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I have to put up with this.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Тебе приходится выбирать между двумя вариантами.
nonpast.2sg.gloss: You have to choose between two options.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He has to work on weekends.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We have to wait for an answer.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you have to travel often?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They have to decide this themselves.

imperative.sg.ru: Приходись здесь всегда кстати (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Always be fitting/convenient here" (figurative, rare usage, context-dependent).

imperative.pl.ru: Приходитесь каждому к месту (образно, редкое употребление).

aspectUsage: Ставить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поставить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *staviti, related to стоять (to stand).
commonMistakes: Confusing ставить (to place something upright) with класть (to lay something flat) — both mean "to put" but differ by orientation.

example.gloss: He's placing the vase on the table.

examples.gloss: We're putting the question up for discussion.

synonymComparison.note: ставить ('to place upright') differs from класть ('to lay flat,' the imperfective of положить) in the object's orientation.

past.m.gloss: He was putting plates on the table.

past.f.gloss: She used to place candles by the window.

past.n.gloss: Everything was being called into question (figurative).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I set the alarm for seven.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You set goals that are too high.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он ставит интересы компании выше своих.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He puts the company's interests above his own.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы ставим новые задачи каждый квартал.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We set new goals every quarter.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you set the conditions in advance?

etymology: The past participle of закрыть (to close).
commonMistakes: Confusing the resulting-state adjective/participle закрытый with the verb закрыть (the action of closing).

etymology: Derived from положить (to put/place).
commonMistakes: Confusing abstract/social положение (situation/position) with позиция (a more concrete position or stance).

etymology: From воз- + расти (to grow).
commonMistakes: Overlooking that взрослый also functions as a noun meaning "an adult," not just as an adjective.

etymology: From за + муж (husband).
commonMistakes: Замуж is used specifically for a woman marrying; жениться is used for a man — easy to confuse.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *pustъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing пустой (empty, lacking contents) with свободный (free/available, lacking obligations or occupancy).

etymology: From Turkic alaša.
commonMistakes: Confusing the general word лошадь (horse) with конь (a stallion/riding horse, more poetic and often male).

etymology: The adverbial form of определённый (definite).
commonMistakes: Confusing the certainty adverb определённо with the verb определить (to determine).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *χolodьnъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective холодный with the adverb/predicate холодно, used for ambient temperature.

etymology: Derived from охранять (to guard).
commonMistakes: Confusing охрана (security, the institution or act of guarding) with защита (protection, a broader concept).

aspectUsage: Установить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective устанавливать.
etymology: From у- + ставить (to place).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of installing/establishing установить with the ongoing process устанавливать.

synonymComparison.note: установить ('to establish' a rule/fact, broad) differs from основать ('to found' an organization, more specific).

past.f.gloss: She identified the cause of the failure.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll install the new version today.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you establish contact with the client?

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы установим систему к концу месяца.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll have the system installed by the end of the month.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you install the equipment on-site?

etymology: Derived from учить (to teach).
commonMistakes: Confusing ученик (a school pupil, usually younger) with студент (a university student).

aspectUsage: Покончить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective кончать.
etymology: From по- + кончить (to finish).
commonMistakes: Confusing "покончить с чем-то" (to be done with something for good, с + instrumental) with simply "to finish" закончить.

example.gloss: He put an end to that habit.

examples.gloss: She put the past behind her.
We paid off all our debts.

examples.ru: Мы кончаем переговоры на этой неделе.
examples.gloss: We're wrapping up the negotiations this week.

synonymComparison.note: покончить ('to decisively end/break with' something, с + instrumental) differs from закончить ('to simply finish,' more neutral).

past.m.gloss: He put an end to his doubts.

past.f.gloss: She put an end to her indecisiveness.

past.pl.gloss: We broke with the old methods.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll put an end to this today.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you finally put an end to this?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll quickly put an end to the competition.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы покончим с проблемой раз и навсегда.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll settle the problem once and for all.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you put an end to this dispute?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll put an end to the uncertainty.

imperative.sg.ru: Покончи с этим раз и навсегда.
imperative.sg.gloss: Put an end to this once and for all.

imperative.pl.gloss: Put an end to the disagreements.

aspectUsage: Обожать is a stative verb of emotion with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: From Church Slavonic, originally meaning "to worship as divine."
commonMistakes: Confusing обожать (to adore, a strong liking) with the more neutral/general любить (to love/like).

synonymComparison.note: обожать ('to adore,' a stronger emotion) differs from любить ('to love,' more general).

past.f.ru: Она обожала эту песню в юности.
past.f.gloss: She adored this song in her youth.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to love this atmosphere (figurative).

past.pl.ru: Мы обожали этот фильм в детстве.
past.pl.gloss: We loved this movie as children.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I love walking in the rain.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты обожаешь эту книгу, я знаю.
nonpast.2sg.gloss: I know you adore this book.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you love classical music?

imperative.sg.ru: Обожай жизнь во всех её проявлениях (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Adore life in all its forms" (figurative, rare usage).

imperative.pl.ru: Обожайте то, что имеете (образно, редкое употребление).

etymology: Derived from показать (to show).
commonMistakes: Confusing показание (testimony, or an instrument reading) with показатель (an indicator/metric, a different derivative).

etymology: From всё + таки (nevertheless).
commonMistakes: Confusing the concessive всё-таки with the near-synonym всё же, interchangeable in most contexts.

aspectUsage: Заслуживать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective заслужить.
etymology: From за- + служить (to serve).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to deserve" заслуживать with заслужить (pf, having earned through specific effort).

synonymComparison.note: заслуживать ('to deserve,' through merit/effort) differs from стоить ('to be worth,' a more neutral evaluation).

past.pl.gloss: We deserved a rest after the project.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You deserve gratitude.

imperative.sg.ru: Заслуживай доверие своими делами (образно, редкое употребление).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Earn trust through your actions" (figurative, rare usage).

etymology: The adverbial form of страшный (scary).
commonMistakes: Confusing the impersonal predicate страшно (dative subject: мне страшно, "I'm scared") with the adjective страшный describing a noun directly.

etymology: Via Church Slavonic from Greek Hades.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "в аду" rather than "в аде."

aspectUsage: Испортить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective портить.
etymology: From ис- + портить (to damage).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed damage испортить with ongoing/habitual damage портить.

examples.gloss: She ruined the dress with a stain.

synonymComparison.note: испортить ('to spoil/ruin,' broad, function or state) differs from ломать ('to break,' physical damage).

past.f.gloss: She damaged her relationship with her colleague.

past.n.gloss: Everything in the fridge went bad.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll ruin everything if I tell.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll ruin the celebration with that.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll make a bad impression if we're late.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll spoil the surprise effect.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll damage the goods in transit.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't ruin the celebration for everyone.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *radostь.
commonMistakes: Confusing радость (joy, a momentary emotion) with счастье (happiness, a broader/more lasting state).

etymology: Borrowed from French idéal, Greek idea.
commonMistakes: Confusing идеальный (ideal, an abstract best case) with совершенный (perfect, describing the actual achieved quality).

aspectUsage: Заключить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective заключать.
etymology: From за- + ключ (key), with the sense "to lock in / conclude."
commonMistakes: Заключить has two distinct senses — "to conclude an agreement" and "to lock someone up" — that require context to disambiguate.

examples.gloss: The parties concluded a peace agreement.

examples.ru: Текст заключает в себе глубокий смысл.

synonymComparison.note: заключить ('to conclude' an agreement, the deal itself) differs from подписать ('to sign,' the final procedural act).

past.f.gloss: She negotiated a truce with the neighbors.

past.n.gloss: Everything was summed up in one sentence.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я заключу договор на следующей неделе.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll conclude the contract next week.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you make a deal with them?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll form an alliance with the partners.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы заключим соглашение к концу месяца.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll have the agreement concluded by month's end.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you conclude the contract officially?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll make peace after the negotiations.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *životъ, originally meaning "life."
commonMistakes: Confusing живот (belly, the general external term) with желудок (stomach, the internal organ specifically).

aspectUsage: In the sense "to plan," планировать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective спланировать. It also has an unrelated sense, "to glide."
etymology: Borrowed from German/French plan.
commonMistakes: Confusing "to plan" планировать (impf) with the homonymous "to glide" sense, which is unrelated.

examples.gloss: We plan the budget every year.
He planned the route in advance.
We planned the budget for the year.

synonymComparison.note: планировать ('to plan,' concrete) differs from намереваться ('to intend,' more abstract).

past.m.gloss: He planned his career in advance.

past.f.gloss: She had been planning the trip for months.

past.pl.gloss: We were planning the strategy together.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm planning a meeting for tomorrow.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you planning to move soon?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you planning a vacation this summer?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're planning a reform of the system.

etymology: Borrowed from French restaurant.
commonMistakes: Confusing ресторан (a formal restaurant) with кафе (a more casual café).

etymology: From the root мк- (to close), related to закрыть.
commonMistakes: За́мок ("castle," stressed on the first syllable) and замо́к ("lock," stressed on the second) are spelled identically but differ in stress and meaning — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Учить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective выучить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *učiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing учить (to teach someone, or to study/memorize something) with the reflexive учиться (to study, to be a learner).

governance.pattern: accusative (thing studied/taught) + dative or infinitive (when meaning 'to teach')

examples.ru: Она выучила язык за два года.
examples.gloss: She learned the language in two years.

synonymComparison.note: учить ('to learn/teach,' specific items) differs from изучать ('to study systematically,' more academic).

past.n.gloss: Everything taught us to be more attentive (figurative).

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я учу новые слова каждый день.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I learn new words every day.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you study foreign languages?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're studying history for the exam.

etymology: The adverbial form of близкий (near).
commonMistakes: Confusing близко (close, distance-related) with рядом (nearby, often implying side-by-side proximity).

aspectUsage: Плевать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective плюнуть.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *plьvati.
commonMistakes: The idiom "мне плевать" ("I don't care") is very common and easily confused with the literal "to spit."

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to spit, intransitive); figuratively на + accusative (not to care)

examples.gloss: He's spitting sunflower seed shells on the floor.
She doesn't care about other people's opinions.

examples.ru: Она плюнула на всё и уехала.
examples.gloss: She gave up on everything and left (figurative).

synonymComparison.note: плевать/плюнуть share the figurative 'not to care' sense with наплевать, a more emphatic colloquial synonym.

past.m.gloss: He never cared about the rules.

past.f.gloss: She spat to the side demonstratively.

past.n.ru: Всё плевало ему в лицо, казалось (образно).
past.n.gloss: It seemed like everything was spitting in his face (figurative).

past.pl.ru: Мы плевали на условности в молодости.
past.pl.gloss: We didn't care about conventions when we were young.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I don't care about the crowd's opinion.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You don't care about the warnings.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He doesn't care about the consequences.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Don't you care about the company rules?

imperative.sg.ru: Плюй на это и живи дальше (образно).
imperative.sg.gloss: "Don't worry about it and move on with life" (figurative).

etymology: From Америка (America) plus the suffix -ский.
commonMistakes: Confusing the adjective американский with the noun американец (an American person).

etymology: An adjective derived from чёрт (devil).
commonMistakes: Чертовый is a slang curse-word modifier, inappropriate in polite settings — easy to overlook.

etymology: Possibly of Turkic or Slavic dialectal origin, originally a nickname.
commonMistakes: Confusing дурак (fool, a somewhat harsher insult) with глупый (stupid, the milder adjective).

etymology: Borrowed from English/French partner.
commonMistakes: Confusing the formal партнёр (business/romantic partner) with напарник (a casual work buddy).

etymology: An archaic interrogative/relative pronoun tracing to Proto-Slavic, surviving mainly in fixed expressions.
commonMistakes: Overlooking that кой no longer stands independently in modern Russian, surviving only inside fixed expressions.

aspectUsage: Мечтать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of dreaming/aspiring. The derived помечтать exists as a delimitative meaning "to daydream for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Derived from мечта (dream, ideal).
commonMistakes: Confusing мечтать (to dream/aspire, hoping for the future) with видеть сон (to have a dream while sleeping).

examples.gloss: She dreams of becoming a doctor.

examples.ru: Мы мечтаем о доме у моря.
examples.gloss: We dream of a house by the sea.

synonymComparison.note: мечтать ('to dream,' an aspiration that may or may not come true) differs from надеяться ('to hope,' expecting realization).

past.m.ru: Он мечтал о славе в юности.
past.m.gloss: He dreamed of fame in his youth.

past.f.gloss: She dreamed of having her own business.

past.n.gloss: Everything seemed to dream of a better future (figurative).

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты мечтаешь о карьере в музыке?
nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you dream of a career in music?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He dreams of having his own business.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы мечтаем о путешествии вокруг света.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We dream of traveling around the world.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you dream of moving?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они мечтают о победе на турнире.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They dream of winning the tournament.

aspectUsage: Прощать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective простить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *prostiti, related to простой (simple).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to forgive" прощать with the single completed act простить.

example.gloss: She forgives him for the mistake.

examples.gloss: He forgave the person who wronged him.

synonymComparison.note: прощать ('to forgive,' can include serious wrongs) differs from извинять ('to excuse,' lighter offenses).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you forgive such behavior?

etymology: From право (right) plus the suffix -ительство.
commonMistakes: Confusing правительство (the government, the executive body) with государство (the state, a broader entity).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *bojь, related to бить (to strike).
commonMistakes: Confusing бой (a battle/fight, often military or combat sport) with драка (a casual brawl between individuals).

aspectUsage: Научить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective учить.
etymology: From на- + учить (to teach).
commonMistakes: Confusing научить (to successfully teach someone, pf, result achieved) with учить (impf, the ongoing teaching process).

governance.pattern: accusative (person taught) + dative or infinitive (skill taught)

examples.gloss: She taught her son to cook.

examples.ru: Он учит сестру кататься на велосипеде.
examples.gloss: He's teaching his sister to ride a bike.

synonymComparison.note: научить ('to teach,' everyday) differs from обучить ('to train/educate,' more formal/professional).

past.m.ru: Он научил меня играть в шахматы.
past.m.gloss: He taught me how to play chess.

past.f.gloss: She taught her friend to knit.

past.n.gloss: Everything taught him to be more careful (figurative).

past.pl.gloss: We taught the newcomers the basics of the job.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я научу тебя готовить этот суп.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll teach you how to make this soup.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you teach me to drive?

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он научит сына читать к школе.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll teach his son to read before school.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll teach the team the new system.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you teach us this method?

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *grudь.
commonMistakes: The instrumental form грудью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Сохранить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective сохранять.
etymology: From со- + хранить (to keep).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed "to save/preserve" сохранить with the related but not directly paired imperfective хранить (to store/keep).

examples.ru: Он сохраняет хладнокровие в любой ситуации.
examples.gloss: He keeps his cool in any situation.

synonymComparison.note: сохранить ('to save/preserve,' the act/result) differs from хранить ('to keep/store,' an ongoing state).

past.m.gloss: He saved the documents in a folder.

past.n.gloss: Everything was preserved in its original form.

past.pl.ru: Мы сохранили отношения несмотря на расстояние.
past.pl.gloss: We maintained the relationship despite the distance.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you save a copy of the document?

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы сохраним историю для будущих поколений.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll preserve the history for future generations.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you save the file to the cloud?

etymology: A derivative of со- + быть (to be).
commonMistakes: Confusing событие (a significant/notable event) with случай (a general occurrence, which can be mundane).

etymology: Derived from великий (great).
commonMistakes: Confusing the address form величество (capitalized, "Your Majesty") with величие (greatness, the abstract noun).

etymology: The Russian spelling of the English name Harry.
commonMistakes: The foreign name Гарри is indeclinable in Russian, keeping the same form in every case — easy to overlook.

etymology: From стлать (to spread/lay out).
commonMistakes: Confusing постель (the bedding/made bed) with кровать (the bed frame furniture itself).

etymology: Derived from преступить (to cross a line, break the law).
commonMistakes: Confusing преступник (a convicted/established criminal) with подозреваемый (a suspect, not yet proven).

etymology: From не + правильно (correctly).
commonMistakes: Confusing неправильно (incorrect, factually wrong) with нечестно (unfair/dishonest, a moral judgment).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *gъrlo.
commonMistakes: Confusing горло (throat, the internal passage) with шея (neck, the external body part).

etymology: From бог (God), originally meaning "blessed by God."
commonMistakes: Богатый's etymological link to бог (God) is easily overlooked — the modern meaning "rich" has no religious sense.

etymology: Derived from уличить (to catch out/expose).
commonMistakes: Confusing улика (a physical clue in an investigation) with доказательство (proof/evidence in a broader, including legal-argument, sense).

aspectUsage: Разрешить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective разрешать.
etymology: From раз- + решить (to solve).
commonMistakes: Разрешить carries two senses — "to permit" and "to resolve (a problem)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

example.gloss: He allowed the children to go out.

examples.gloss: He allows the children to play here.

synonymComparison.note: разрешить ('to permit,' more official/rule-based) differs from позволить ('to allow,' more personal/softer).

past.m.gloss: He resolved the issue quickly (a different sense: 'to resolve').

past.f.gloss: She resolved the dispute between colleagues.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you let me take a look?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll allow the data to be used.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll grant access to the file.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you permit us to attend?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll approve the changes to the project.

aspectUsage: Включить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective включать.
etymology: From в- + ключить (to lock/include).
commonMistakes: Confusing "to turn on/include" включить with its opposite, "to turn off" выключить.

examples.gloss: We added him to the list.
He turns on the TV every evening.

synonymComparison.note: включить ('to turn on') is the direct opposite of выключить ('to turn off').

past.m.gloss: He turned on the computer in the morning.

past.f.gloss: She turned on the air conditioner.

past.pl.ru: Мы включили новые пункты в договор.
past.pl.gloss: We added new clauses to the contract.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you turn on the heater?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll arm the alarm for the night.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы включим эти расходы в бюджет.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll include these costs in the budget.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы включите этот пункт в отчёт?
nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you include this item in the report?

etymology: Borrowed from German/Polish Ring (circle, marketplace).
commonMistakes: Confusing рынок (a market, also the economic concept) with базар (a traditional/informal bazaar).

etymology: The adverbial form of личный (personal).
commonMistakes: Confusing лично (personally, expressing one's own view/involvement) with частно (privately, in a non-official capacity).

etymology: From French rayon.
commonMistakes: Confusing район (a city district/neighborhood) with область (a larger administrative region).

aspectUsage: Напасть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective нападать.
etymology: From на- + пасть (to fall, from Proto-Slavic *padati).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of attacking напасть with the more formal, borrowed, biaspectual synonym атаковать.

synonymComparison.note: напасть ('to attack,' somewhat sudden/general) differs from атаковать ('to attack,' more organized/military).

past.m.gloss: He found a lead on the criminal (figurative: 'to come upon').

past.n.gloss: Everything hit him all at once (figurative).

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll attack first if I have to.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты нападёшь на эту тему в статье?
nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you tackle this topic critically in the article?

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы нападём на проблему с другой стороны.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll tackle the problem from a different angle (figurative).

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you attack the competitors openly?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll raid the camp at night.

etymology: A diminutive of лодь (an archaic word for boat).
commonMistakes: Confusing лодка (a small, often rowed boat) with корабль (a large ship).

etymology: From Greek thema via Latin.
commonMistakes: Confusing тема (a topic/theme) with вопрос (a question specifically).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *kostь.
commonMistakes: The instrumental form костью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Подать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective подавать.
etymology: From по- + дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of submitting/serving подать with the ongoing подавать.

example.gloss: She served tea to the guests.

examples.gloss: The restaurant serves breakfast until eleven.

synonymComparison.note: подать ('to serve/submit,' concrete/immediate) differs from предоставить ('to provide,' more formal/institutional).

past.m.gloss: He offered his hand to the lady.

past.pl.gloss: We filed the complaint on time.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you submit the application today?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you file the declaration on time?

imperative.pl.gloss: Submit the documents to the front desk.

etymology: Derived from принять (to receive/accept).
commonMistakes: Приём has multiple senses — a doctor's appointment, a social reception, and a technique/method — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Derived from часть (part).
commonMistakes: Confusing участок (a plot of land, or a police precinct/road section) with часть (a general "part," a much broader word).

aspectUsage: Выбраться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective выбираться.
etymology: From вы- + браться (to make one's way with effort, related to браться).
commonMistakes: Confusing выбраться (to manage to get out, with effort) with simply выйти (to exit, without implying difficulty).

example.gloss: He made his way out of the forest.

examples.ru: Она выбралась из пробки через час.
examples.gloss: She got out of the traffic jam after an hour.

examples.ru: Мы выбрались на природу в выходные.
examples.gloss: We got out into nature on the weekend.
He rarely gets out of the city.
We go out on picnics in summer.

synonymComparison.note: выбраться ('to make one's way out,' with effort) differs from выходить ('to simply exit').

past.m.gloss: He finally got out of debt.

past.f.gloss: She made her way out of a difficult situation.

past.pl.gloss: We finally made it out to the theater.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я выберусь к тебе в гости скоро.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll make it over to visit you soon.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you be able to get away this weekend?

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы выберемся на природу в субботу.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll get out into nature on Saturday.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you be able to make it to the reunion?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll get out of their difficulties.

etymology: A fixed expression from the reflexive third person of разуметь (to understand).
commonMistakes: Разумеется and конечно are near-synonyms, but разумеется is slightly more formal/literary — easy to overlook.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *osmь.
commonMistakes: Восемь, like other numerals 5 and up, takes the genitive plural on the noun it counts — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Поступать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective поступить.
etymology: From по- + ступать (to step/walk).
commonMistakes: Поступать carries two senses — "to act/behave" and "to enroll (in a university etc.)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

governance.pattern: used with adverbs/context (to act); в + accusative (institution enrolled in)

examples.gloss: Money comes into the account regularly.
She was admitted to the institute.

synonymComparison.note: поступать ('to act,' implying a judgment/outcome) differs from действовать ('to act,' more neutral).

past.pl.gloss: We acted cautiously in the negotiations.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I act according to my conscience.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We act in accordance with the law.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы поступаете разумно в этом случае.
nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're acting sensibly in this case.

etymology: The adverbial form of видимый (visible).
commonMistakes: Confusing видимо (apparently, a guess based on evidence) with заметно (noticeably, describing the visibility of a fact).

aspectUsage: Убедить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective убеждать.
etymology: From у- + a root related to persuasion (вед-).
commonMistakes: Confusing убедить (to convince someone else) with the reflexive убедиться (to become convinced oneself).

governance.pattern: accusative (person persuaded) + в + prepositional (thing persuaded of)

example.ru: Он убедил меня в своей правоте.
example.gloss: He convinced me he was right.

examples.gloss: We convinced the investors to invest money.

examples.ru: Она убеждает себя, что всё хорошо.
examples.gloss: She keeps convincing herself everything is fine.

synonymComparison.note: убедить ('to convince,' through logic) differs from уговорить ('to talk someone into it,' more emotional/persuasive).

past.m.ru: Он убедил всех в своей идее.
past.m.gloss: He convinced everyone of his idea.

past.f.gloss: She convinced the board of directors.

past.n.ru: Всё убедило нас в правильности пути.
past.n.gloss: Everything convinced us our path was right.

past.pl.gloss: We convinced the partners of the benefit.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я убежу его в необходимости перемен.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll convince him of the need for change.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you convince her to stay?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll win over the jury with his presentation.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll win over clients with quality.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы убедите совет в необходимости бюджета?
nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you convince the board of the budget's necessity?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они убедят всех в своей правоте.

imperative.pl.gloss: Convince the committee of the project's importance.

etymology: An old comparative form of мало (little).
commonMistakes: Менее forms the analytic comparative meaning "less," the counterpart to более ("more") — easy to overlook.

etymology: From Latin studens.
commonMistakes: Confusing студент (a university student specifically) with ученик (a school pupil).

etymology: An onomatopoeic interjection.
commonMistakes: Хм, a thinking-pause interjection, is easily confused with угу, which expresses agreement.

etymology: From работать (to work); a substantivized adjective.
commonMistakes: Рабочий functions both as the adjective "work-related" and as the noun "a worker" — context determines which.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *въкусъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing вкус (taste, both physical flavor and aesthetic preference) with запах (smell, a distinct sense).

aspectUsage: Забирать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective забрать.
etymology: From за- + бирать (to take, related to брать).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/habitual забирать with the single completed act забрать.

example.gloss: He picks up the kids from school.

examples.gloss: She picks up packages from the post office.

examples.ru: Мы забираем вещи из химчистки каждую неделю.
examples.gloss: We pick up clothes from the dry cleaner every week.
He picked up the documents yesterday.

synonymComparison.note: забирать ('to pick up/take away,' from a specific place) differs from брать ('to take,' more general).

past.m.gloss: He used to pick up the mail every day.

past.f.ru: Она забирала детей из сада вовремя.
past.f.gloss: She picked up the children from daycare on time.

past.n.gloss: Everything was gradually being removed from the warehouse.

past.pl.gloss: We picked up orders in person.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm picking up the car from the shop.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Are you picking up the package today?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's picking up his things tomorrow.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're picking up the cargo from the warehouse.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you picking up the documents yourselves?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're picking up the goods at the warehouse.

imperative.pl.gloss: Pick up your things by Friday.

aspectUsage: Признаться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective признаваться.
etymology: From знать (to know) plus the prefix при- and reflexive -ся.
commonMistakes: Confusing the personal/emotional "to confess" признаться with the more objective "to acknowledge" признать.

examples.gloss: She's admitting her fear to herself.

synonymComparison.note: признаться ('to confess,' broad) differs from сознаться ('to admit guilt,' more legal in tone).

past.f.gloss: She confided a secret to her friend.

past.n.ru: Всё призналось само собой со временем.
