example.gloss: He got up out of bed.

examples.gloss: We were slowly climbing the hill (process).
He got up and left (one completed act).
Come up to the second floor.

synonymComparison.note: подняться centres on a change in height — going up or rising; встать is simply to stand up or get up. Use встать for getting out of bed, подняться for going up stairs.

past.m.gloss: He went up to the fifth floor.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll come up in a minute.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you come up with me?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: The lift goes up to the tenth floor.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you take the lift up?

imperative.sg.gloss: Please come up to the third floor.

etymology: From Latin interesse via French/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing интерес (interest, curiosity/engagement) with любопытство (curiosity, specifically the desire to know).

etymology: Derived from вспомнить (to recall).
commonMistakes: Confusing воспоминание (a specific memory/recollection) with память (memory, the general faculty).

aspectUsage: Контролировать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective проконтролировать.
etymology: Borrowed from French contrôler.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to control/monitor" контролировать with the single completed check проконтролировать.

examples.ru: Он не контролирует себя, когда злится.
examples.gloss: He loses control of himself when he's angry (a recurring state).
Check that the task gets done (one completed check).

synonymComparison.note: контролировать is continuous oversight; проверять is a discrete check. Compare контролировать процесс with проверять документы.

past.m.gloss: He had the situation under control.

past.f.gloss: She kept a tight grip on spending.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I keep track of my spending.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you have the situation under control?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you in charge of this process?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They control access to the data.

imperative.pl.gloss: Please keep an eye on the deadlines.

etymology: Derived from вкус (taste).
commonMistakes: Confusing вкусный (tasty, describing food once eaten) with аппетитный (appetizing, the visual/aromatic appeal before tasting).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *čislo.
commonMistakes: Число carries two senses — "number" and "date (of the month)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Traces to a Proto-Slavic root related to carrying a burden/pregnancy.
commonMistakes: Беременный grammatically has masculine/neuter/plural forms, but in practice is used only for women — easy to overlook.

etymology: From Latin mille (thousand).
commonMistakes: Confusing миля (mile, an imperial unit) with километр (kilometer, the metric unit commonly used in Russia).

aspectUsage: Сдать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective сдавать.
etymology: From с- + дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Сдать carries several senses — "to pass (an exam)," "to rent out (an apartment)," "to hand over (an item)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

governance.pattern: + accusative + в + accusative (to hand something in)

example.gloss: Take the clothes to the dry cleaner's.

examples.gloss: I'm taking the exam on Monday (planned, in process).
They rent the flat out to students (ongoing).
I passed all my exams (completed result).
Hand in the report by Friday.

synonymComparison.note: сдать квартиру (to let) and снять квартиру (to rent) are opposites: the landlord сдаёт, the tenant снимает. The direction is what matters.
The reflexive сдаться means 'to surrender' — Я сдаюсь ('I give up') is something else entirely.

past.m.ru: Он сдал экзамен с первого раза.
past.m.gloss: He passed the exam on the first try.

past.f.gloss: She submitted the documents on time.

past.n.gloss: The agency let the office out.

past.pl.ru: Мы сдали вещи в камеру хранения.
past.pl.gloss: We left our bags at the luggage room.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll take the exam in June.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you hand the work in today?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll submit the report on time.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you check your luggage here?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll hand the keys back to the owner.

imperative.sg.gloss: Hand the work in before noon.

etymology: Derived from слышать (to hear).
commonMistakes: Слух carries two senses — "hearing" and "rumor" — requiring context to disambiguate.

aspectUsage: Добиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective добиваться.
etymology: From до- + бить (to strike, "until reaching").
commonMistakes: Confusing добиться (to achieve through struggle/effort) with достичь (to reach/attain, without the "struggle" connotation).

governance.pattern: + от + genitive + genitive (to get something out of someone)

example.gloss: I got an answer out of him.

examples.gloss: He spent years working toward this position (sustained effort).
We got what we were after (completed result).

synonymComparison.note: добиться implies winning something through effort; достичь is simply reaching a point or level, with less sense of struggle. Both govern the genitive.

past.n.gloss: The movement secured changes in the law.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll get there if you don't give up.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он добьётся успеха в этом деле.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll achieve more than this.

imperative.sg.gloss: See it through — don't give up.

imperative.pl.gloss: Get a clear answer out of them.

aspectUsage: Угадать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective угадывать.
etymology: From у- + гадать (to guess).
commonMistakes: Confusing угадать (to guess correctly, a successful guess) with гадать (the general act of guessing/speculating, without implying correctness).

examples.gloss: She always reads my thoughts right (repeated).
He spent a long time trying to guess the password (process).
I got it on the first try (completed result).

synonymComparison.note: угадать means guessing correctly; гадать is guessing or divining, with no implication of being right — it also covers fortune-telling, as in гадать на картах.

past.f.gloss: She guessed what my present was.

past.n.gloss: The app identified the song in a second.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll get it in three tries.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You won't guess the price.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *věra.
commonMistakes: Confusing вера (faith/belief, often religious or in a person) with доверие (trust, a more interpersonal/practical confidence).

aspectUsage: Прятаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective спрятаться.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Slavic root meaning "to hide."
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/habitual прятаться with the single completed act of hiding спрятаться.

example.gloss: The child is hiding behind a tree.

examples.gloss: Children love hiding in the wardrobe (habitual).
The cat hid under the bed (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: прятаться is the everyday physical hiding; скрываться carries the heavier sense of being in hiding or on the run — скрываться от полиции.

past.m.gloss: He was hiding behind the curtain.

past.n.gloss: The sun was hiding behind the clouds.

past.pl.ru: Мы прятались от дождя под деревом.
past.pl.gloss: We sheltered from the rain under a tree.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I stay home out of the heat.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He hides behind other people's words.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're avoiding the conversation.

imperative.pl.gloss: Get out of the sun, into the shade.

aspectUsage: Ценить is an imperfective stative verb meaning "to value/appreciate." The related оценить ("to evaluate/recognize value") differs in meaning.
etymology: Derived from цена (price/value).
commonMistakes: Confusing ценить (to value/appreciate, a stative feeling) with оценить (to evaluate/assess, a more active judgment process).

governance.pattern: + accusative + за + accusative (to value someone for something)

example.gloss: I value him for his honesty.

examples.gloss: I value time over money (a standing attitude).

synonymComparison.note: ценить is the ongoing attitude of valuing something; оценить is the one-off act of appraising or putting a price on it. Я ценю ('I appreciate') differs from Я оценил ('I appraised / I sized it up').
ценить is to recognise worth; уважать is to hold in respect. Both work with people, but only ценить works with things and time.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты не ценишь то, что имеешь.
nonpast.2sg.gloss: You don't value what you have.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you value things like this?

imperative.pl.ru: Цените то, что у вас есть.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *lěvъ.
commonMistakes: Левый carries both a directional sense ("left") and a political sense ("left-wing") — context determines which.

etymology: From Latin productus.
commonMistakes: Confusing продукт (a product, general sense or food item) with товар (goods, a commercial/sales-oriented term).

aspectUsage: Устраивать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective устроить.
etymology: From у- + строить (to organize/build).
commonMistakes: Устраивать carries two senses — "to organize/arrange" and "to suit someone" — requiring context to disambiguate.

governance.pattern: + accusative + на + accusative (to get someone a position)

example.gloss: He got his son a job.

examples.gloss: That schedule works for me (a state).
We threw him a surprise (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: устраивать is the colloquial 'to throw, to arrange'; организовать is the official 'to organise, to run.' устроить вечеринку among friends, организовать конференцию at work.

past.m.gloss: He put on concerts every year.

past.f.gloss: She was arranging nursery places for the children.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Does that price work for you?

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We're putting on an exhibition in the autumn.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you hold events like this often?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: The new rules don't suit them.

aspectUsage: Пустить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective пускать.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *pustiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of letting go/in пустить with the ongoing/habitual пускать.

governance.pattern: + accusative (what you let flow or release)
+ accusative + в + accusative (to let someone in)

example.gloss: Don't let him into the house.

governance.pattern: + accusative + infinitive (to let someone go do something)

example.gloss: Let the children go out to play.

examples.gloss: Dogs aren't allowed in here (a rule, repeated).
The guard let us inside (one completed act).
Let me by, I need to get through.

synonymComparison.note: пустить is physically letting someone through or in; разрешить is granting abstract permission. Пусти меня ('let me through') vs Разреши мне ('allow me').

past.m.gloss: He started a rumour around the office.

past.f.gloss: She put us up for the night.

past.n.gloss: Management let journalists into the plant.

past.pl.gloss: They wouldn't let us in without a ticket.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я пущу тебя, но только на минуту.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll let you in, but only for a minute.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He won't let us go any further.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы пустим воду в семь утра.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll turn the water on at seven.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы пустите нас на пять минут?
nonpast.2pl.gloss: Could you let us in for five minutes?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они пустят автобус по новому маршруту.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll run the bus on a new route.

aspectUsage: Возражать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective возразить.
etymology: From воз- + разить (to strike, shifted to "object").
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to object" возражать with the single completed objection возразить.

example.gloss: He talked back to his boss.

examples.gloss: I have no objection (a state of assent).

examples.ru: Он всегда возражает по любому поводу.

examples.gloss: She objected sharply and fell silent (one completed act).
I have nothing to say against it.

synonymComparison.note: возражать is a one-way objection; спорить is a two-way argument. Note the case government too: возражать против + genitive, спорить о + prepositional.

past.n.gloss: The ministry objected to the amendments.

past.pl.ru: Мы возражали, но нас не слушали.
past.pl.gloss: We objected, but no one listened.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я не возражаю, если ты пойдёшь.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I don't mind if you go.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы не возражаете, если я закурю?
nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you mind if I smoke?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They object to the price increase.

imperative.pl.gloss: Please keep objections to the substance.

etymology: Derived from заявить (to declare).
commonMistakes: Заявление carries two senses — "a public statement" and "an application form" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Derived from скорый (quick).
commonMistakes: The instrumental form скоростью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Служить is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of serving. The derived послужить exists as a delimitative meaning "to serve for a certain period," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *služiti.
commonMistakes: Confusing служить (to serve, a role/duty with purpose) with работать (to work, a more general/neutral term for employment).

examples.ru: Он служил на флоте три года.
examples.gloss: He served in the navy for three years (ongoing).
This room serves as a study (a state).

synonymComparison.note: служить is serving — in the military, public office, or a cause; работать is simply working. служить в армии vs работать в офисе.

past.n.gloss: The building served as a school.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я служу в этой организации десять лет.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I've served in this organisation for ten years.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Have you served here long?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They serve as an example to others.

aspectUsage: Воспользоваться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective пользоваться.
etymology: From вос- + пользоваться (to use).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of making use воспользоваться with the ongoing/habitual пользоваться.

governance.pattern: + instrumental (to make use of someone's help or position)

example.gloss: He made use of my help.

examples.ru: Я пользуюсь этим приложением каждый день.
examples.gloss: I use this app every day (habitual).
He enjoys his colleagues' respect (a state).
I acted on your advice (one completed use).

synonymComparison.note: воспользоваться / пользоваться take the instrumental and mean making use of a tool or chance; использовать takes the accusative. The case difference is the thing to watch.

past.n.gloss: Management took advantage of the situation.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you be using our services?

etymology: From French carrière.
commonMistakes: Confusing карьера (career, the professional trajectory) with работа (job, the concrete employment itself).

etymology: Derived from заняться (to engage in).
commonMistakes: Занятие carries two senses — "activity/hobby" and "a class/lesson" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: From среда (the middle), yielding "that which lies between — a means."
commonMistakes: Средство carries two senses — "a means" and "a product/preparation (medicine, detergent)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: The adverbial form of видный (visible).
commonMistakes: Видно carries both the literal "visible" sense and the parenthetical "apparently, it seems" sense — both coexist in modern use.

aspectUsage: Назначить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective назначать.
etymology: From на- + значить (to mean/designate).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of appointing/scheduling назначить with the ongoing/repeated назначать.

governance.pattern: + accusative + на + accusative (to appoint to a post, or set for a time)

example.gloss: He was appointed to the director's post.

examples.gloss: The doctor prescribes treatment case by case (habitual).
They used to schedule meetings every Friday (repeated).

examples.ru: Я назначил встречу на три часа.
examples.gloss: I set the meeting for three o'clock (one completed decision).
Pick a date and let me know.

synonymComparison.note: назначить is setting a time or making an appointment unilaterally; договориться is agreeing on it mutually — договориться о встрече implies both sides.

past.m.gloss: He set the meeting for tomorrow.

past.pl.gloss: We set the deadline for Friday.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll set the meeting for the morning.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you pick the time yourself?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you set the date today?

etymology: A fixed expression from the 1st person plural future of сказать (to say).
commonMistakes: Скажем is a parenthetical particle for giving examples, distinct from its literal meaning "we will say" — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Извиняться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective извиниться.
etymology: The reflexive of извинить (to forgive).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/repeated извиняться with the single completed apology извиниться.

example.gloss: He is apologising to his colleagues.

examples.gloss: He apologises at the slightest thing (repeated, characteristic).
Don't apologise, it's fine (negative command, imperfective).
I apologised right away (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: извиняться is the everyday 'to apologise'; просить прощения (with the genitive) is heavier and more earnest — Прошу прощения for serious occasions.

past.f.gloss: She apologised for every little thing.

past.pl.gloss: We were apologising to the guests.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: There's no need for you to apologise.

imperative.sg.ru: Не извиняйся, это не твоя вина.
imperative.sg.gloss: Don't apologise, it isn't your fault.

imperative.pl.gloss: Please don't apologise, it's all right.

etymology: Possibly borrowed from a Turkic language.
commonMistakes: Confusing ящик (a box/drawer, often larger or wooden) with коробка (a smaller, usually cardboard box).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *glubokъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing глубокий (deep, both physical and figurative) with its opposite мелкий (shallow).

etymology: Derived from разрешить (to permit).
commonMistakes: Разрешение carries several senses — "permission," "resolution (of a conflict)," "resolution (of a screen)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

aspectUsage: Перевести is perfective, pairing with the imperfective переводить.
etymology: From пере- + вести (to lead).
commonMistakes: Перевести carries several senses — "to translate," "to transfer money," "to lead someone across" — requiring context to disambiguate.

governance.pattern: + accusative + на + accusative (to translate into a language)
+ accusative + dative (to transfer money to someone)

example.gloss: I transferred money to my brother.

governance.pattern: + accusative + через + accusative (to take someone across)

example.gloss: He walked the old lady across the street.

examples.gloss: She translates books from English (profession, ongoing).
I spent a long time translating this text (process).
I translated the letter in an hour (completed result).

synonymComparison.note: For money, перевести (to transfer between accounts) is close to отправить (to send), but banking language uses перевести деньги as standard.

past.m.gloss: He translated the article into Russian.

past.n.gloss: The agency translated the documents quickly.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you translate a couple of lines for me?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll transfer the money in the morning.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы переведём сайт на три языка.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll translate the site into three languages.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you transfer the payment today?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll translate the text by Friday.

imperative.pl.gloss: Please transfer the sum to this account.

aspectUsage: Предупредить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective предупреждать.
etymology: From пред- + упредить (to act first).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of warning предупредить with the ongoing/habitual предупреждать.

governance.pattern: + accusative (whom you warn) + о + prepositional (about what)

example.gloss: He warned me about the danger.

governance.pattern: + accusative + что clause (to let someone know in advance)

example.gloss: Let me know in advance if you'll be late.

examples.gloss: I always give notice in advance (habitual).
We weren't being told about the changes (ongoing).
I warned him in time (one completed act).
Let me know if the plans change.

synonymComparison.note: предупредить is to warn or give advance notice; сообщить is simply to inform or report. предупредить carries the sense of putting someone on guard.

past.f.gloss: She gave notice that she'd be late.

past.n.gloss: The agency gave notice of the delay.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я предупрежу тебя, если что-то изменится.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll let you know if anything changes.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you give me advance notice?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you let us know before you visit?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll warn the neighbours about the renovation.

imperative.sg.gloss: Let me know if you'll be held up.

etymology: From Latin temperatura.
commonMistakes: Confusing температура (temperature, the measurement) with жар (fever, the specific symptom of elevated body temperature).

etymology: The possessive adjective of сука (female dog).
commonMistakes: Сукин is normally used only inside the curse phrase "сукин сын" (son of a bitch) — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from длина (length).
commonMistakes: Confusing длинный (long, physical length/extent) with долгий (long, temporal duration).

etymology: The comparative of рано (early).
commonMistakes: Confusing the formal, written ранее ("previously") with the colloquial synonym раньше.

etymology: A derivative of кончить (to finish), from a past-participle form.
commonMistakes: Confusing the derogatory colloquial конченый ("a wreck, done for") with the plain "finished" законченный.

etymology: From раз- + a root related to measuring.
commonMistakes: Confusing размер (size, a specific measurement/dimension) with величина (magnitude, a more abstract/general quantity).

aspectUsage: Рисковать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective рискнуть.
etymology: Borrowed from French risquer.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/general "to take risks" рисковать with the single completed risky act рискнуть.

governance.pattern: + infinitive (to run the risk of doing something)

examples.gloss: I took the chance and won (one completed gamble).
Let's chance it one more time.

synonymComparison.note: рисковать is accepting the possibility of loss; осмелиться is summoning the nerve to act. рисковать takes the instrumental, осмелиться an infinitive.

past.m.gloss: He was risking everything he had.

past.n.gloss: The company was risking investors' money.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're taking a pointless risk.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't put your health at risk.

etymology: Borrowed from English gentleman.
commonMistakes: Confusing джентльмен (a well-mannered gentleman) with господин (a neutral term of address, "Mr./sir").

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *хрѣнъ.
commonMistakes: Хрен carries both the neutral sense "horseradish" and vulgar slang senses like "damn/hell" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Derived from вызвать (to call).
commonMistakes: Вызов carries two senses — "a call/summons" and "a challenge" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: From Hebrew Yeshua via Greek Iēsous.
commonMistakes: Beyond the religious context, иисус also appears in exclamatory use ("Иисусе!") similar to English "Jesus!" — easy to overlook.

etymology: Borrowed from German Schaff.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "в шкафу" rather than "в шкафе."

etymology: Derived from исток (source/headwaters).
commonMistakes: Confusing источник (a source, of information or water) with причина (cause, a more abstract origin of an event).

etymology: Derived from вернуть (to give back).
commonMistakes: Confusing возвращение (return, the act of coming back) with отъезд (departure, its opposite).

etymology: From French code, Latin codex.
commonMistakes: Confusing код (code, a system of symbols/instructions) with шифр (cipher, specifically for encryption).

etymology: Derived from полк (regiment).
commonMistakes: Confusing полковник (colonel, a specific rank) with генерал (general, a higher rank).

etymology: The adverbial form of забавный (amusing).
commonMistakes: Confusing забавно (amusing, lighthearted fun) with смешно (funny, specifically causing laughter).

etymology: A shortening of за- + плата (payment).
commonMistakes: Confusing зарплата (salary/wages, regular pay for work) with доход (income, a broader concept including other sources).

aspectUsage: Влюбить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective влюблять.
etymology: From в- + любить (to love).
commonMistakes: Confusing the transitive влюбить (to make someone fall in love) with the reflexive влюбиться (to fall in love oneself).

governance.pattern: + accusative + в + accusative (to make someone fall for someone)

example.gloss: She made him fall in love with her.

governance.pattern: reflexive влюбиться + в + accusative (to fall in love with)

example.gloss: I fell in love with her at once.

examples.ru: Этот город влюбляет в себя всех.
examples.gloss: This city makes everyone fall for it (a general property).

examples.ru: Она влюбляла в себя одного за другим.
examples.gloss: She made them fall for her one after another (repeated).

examples.ru: Он влюбил её в себя за один вечер.
examples.gloss: He made her fall for him in a single evening (one completed act).

examples.ru: Невозможно не влюбить в себя этого ребёнка.
examples.gloss: It's impossible not to adore this child.

synonymComparison.note: влюбить is transitive — making someone else fall in love; the reflexive влюбиться is falling in love yourself. In everyday speech влюбиться в + accusative is far more common.

past.m.ru: Он влюбил её в себя шутками.
past.m.gloss: He won her over with his jokes.

past.f.ru: Она влюбила в себя весь класс.
past.f.gloss: She had the whole class smitten.

past.n.ru: Это место влюбило в себя туристов.

past.pl.ru: Они влюбили публику в свою музыку.
past.pl.gloss: They made the audience fall for their music.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я влюблю его в себя за неделю.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll have him falling for me within a week.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты влюбишь в себя кого угодно.
nonpast.2sg.gloss: You could make anyone fall for you.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Этот голос влюбит в себя слушателей.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: That voice will win listeners over.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы влюбим зрителей в этот спектакль.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll make the audience fall for this play.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы влюбите в себя детей сразу.
nonpast.2pl.gloss: The children will adore you immediately.

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они влюбят в себя новых клиентов.

imperative.sg.gloss: Make them fall for your product.

imperative.pl.gloss: Make the audience fall for this story.

etymology: Derived from один (one).
commonMistakes: Confusing одинокий (lonely, an emotional state) with единственный (the only one, a quantitative/exclusivity sense).

etymology: From в + низ (below).
commonMistakes: Confusing внизу (location, "down below") with вниз (direction, "downward").

aspectUsage: Случаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective случиться.
etymology: Derived from случай (chance/occurrence).
commonMistakes: Confusing the habitual случаться with the single occurrence случиться.

governance.pattern: impersonally in the 3rd person singular ('it happens that…')

example.gloss: It happens that he's late sometimes.

examples.gloss: Accidents had happened here before too (repeated).

synonymComparison.note: случаться is the colloquial 'to happen (by chance)'; происходить is more neutral and written. Что происходит? asks about something underway, Что случилось? about something completed.

past.m.gloss: A case like that had happened before.

past.f.ru: Авария случалась на этом повороте дважды.
past.f.gloss: An accident had happened at this bend twice.

past.pl.gloss: Mistakes like that happened to everyone.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я случаюсь в их разговорах как пример.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I turn up in their conversations as an example (figurative; the 1st person is extremely rare).

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты случаешься в моей жизни слишком редко.
nonpast.2sg.gloss: You turn up in my life far too rarely (a poetic usage).

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы случаемся в этом городе раз в год.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We happen to be in this town once a year (a rare colloquial usage).

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы случаетесь здесь в самый нужный момент.
nonpast.2pl.gloss: You turn up here at exactly the right moment (a rare colloquial usage).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *trava.
commonMistakes: Confusing трава (grass, the living plant) with сено (hay, the dried cut form).

aspectUsage: Зависеть is an imperfective stative verb with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: From за- + висеть (to hang), shifted to mean "to depend."
commonMistakes: Зависеть takes от + genitive; using a different preposition is a frequent error.

examples.gloss: The outcome depends on the weather (a permanent state).

examples.ru: Я не хочу ни от кого зависеть.
examples.gloss: I don't want to depend on anyone (an ongoing state).

synonymComparison.note: зависеть от + genitive is passive — being subject to something; полагаться на + accusative is active — relying on it. Both the preposition and the case differ.

past.m.gloss: The outcome depended on the weather.

past.f.ru: Её судьба зависела от одного решения.
past.f.gloss: Her fate hung on one decision.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm at the mercy of the train timetable.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you depend on this supplier?

etymology: Derived from медицина (medicine).
commonMistakes: Confusing медицинский (medical, pertaining to medicine) with здоровый (healthy, describing wellbeing).

etymology: Related to дерево (tree).
commonMistakes: Confusing деревня (village, a rural settlement) with город (city, the urban counterpart).

aspectUsage: Предать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective предавать.
etymology: From пре- + дать (to give), shifted to mean "to hand over/betray."
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of betrayal предать with the ongoing/habitual предавать.

examples.ru: Он предавал нас не один раз.
examples.gloss: He betrayed us more than once (repeated).

examples.ru: Нельзя предавать тех, кто тебе верит.
examples.gloss: You mustn't betray those who trust you (a general truth).

examples.ru: Он предал меня в самый трудный момент.
examples.gloss: He betrayed me at the hardest moment (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: предать is breaking the bond of trust itself; обмануть is deceiving someone about a fact. предать is far graver.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты предашь меня, если будет выгодно?
nonpast.2sg.gloss: Would you betray me if it paid?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Would you betray us for money?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll be the first to betray.

aspectUsage: Посадить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective сажать.
etymology: From по- + садить (to seat/plant).
commonMistakes: Посадить carries several senses — "to plant," "to seat," "to imprison" — requiring context to disambiguate.

governance.pattern: + accusative + в + accusative (to put someone in prison)

example.gloss: Sit the child on the chair.

examples.gloss: In spring we plant flowers (repeated, habitual).
Don't seat guests by the door.

examples.ru: Я посадил яблоню в прошлом году.
examples.gloss: I planted an apple tree last year (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: посадить is transitive — to seat someone; сесть is intransitive — to sit down yourself. Посади его vs Сядь changes who acts.

past.m.gloss: He planted a tree by the house.

past.f.gloss: She sat the child on her lap.

past.n.gloss: The farm planted a new orchard.

past.pl.ru: Мы посадили гостей за большой стол.
past.pl.gloss: We seated the guests at the big table.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll plant flowers in the spring.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you seat me by the window?

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он посадит нас в первый ряд.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll put us in the front row.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll plant trees along the road.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Could you seat us together?

imperative.pl.gloss: Please seat the children at the front.

aspectUsage: Отдыхать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective отдохнуть.
etymology: From от- + дыхать (to breathe), shifted to mean "to rest."
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing отдыхать with the single completed rest отдохнуть.

example.gloss: I'm taking a break from work.

examples.gloss: In summer we stay at the dacha (habitual).
He rests for an hour after work (repeated).
I had a good rest over the weekend (completed result).

synonymComparison.note: отдыхать is resting or holidaying; расслабляться is relaxing body and mind. отдыхать на море is a trip, расслабляться в ванне is a bath.

past.f.gloss: She was holidaying in the country.

past.n.gloss: The whole family was resting by the sea.

past.pl.gloss: We were holidaying in the mountains.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Do you ever rest at all?

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы отдыхаем две недели в августе.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We take two weeks off in August.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you holiday abroad?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они отдыхают на даче каждое лето.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They spend every summer at the dacha.

imperative.pl.gloss: Do rest, we'll finish up ourselves.

etymology: From в + ряд (in a row), shifted to express uncertainty.
commonMistakes: Вряд is always used together with ли, never standing alone — easy to overlook.

etymology: From French bottine.
commonMistakes: Confusing ботинок (a boot/ankle shoe) with туфля (a dress shoe, lower-cut).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *сърокъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing срок (a term/deadline, a defined period) with время (time, the general concept).

aspectUsage: Построить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective строить.
etymology: From по- + строить (to build).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of building построить with the ongoing process строить.

examples.ru: Они строят дом уже два года.
examples.gloss: They've been building the house for two years (in progress).
He's making plans for the future (ongoing).
We built the house in a year (completed result).

synonymComparison.note: построить is physical construction (and, figuratively, building relationships or plans); создать is creating something from nothing. построить дом vs создать компанию.

past.m.gloss: He built the house with his own hands.

past.n.gloss: The state built a new school.

past.pl.ru: Мы построили мост за два года.
past.pl.gloss: We built the bridge in two years.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll build a house by the river.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll build a sauna in the summer.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you have it built by spring?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll build the stadium by summer.

imperative.pl.gloss: Build a model and show it to us.

etymology: Derived from ответить (to answer).
commonMistakes: The instrumental form ответственностью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

etymology: Derived from дети (children).
commonMistakes: Confusing детство (childhood, the life stage) with молодость (youth, a slightly later/broader life stage).

etymology: From French étage.
commonMistakes: Confusing этаж (a floor/storey of a building) with пол (floor, the surface one walks on).

etymology: From Hebrew Miryam, a given name.
commonMistakes: Declines as a regular feminine noun; the pet form Маша, derived from it, is easy to overlook as a correspondence.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *slabъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing слабый (weak) with its opposite сильный (strong).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *малъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing the formal малый (used in set phrases/formal register) with the everyday synonym маленький.

etymology: The collective numeral form of три (three).
commonMistakes: Confusing трое (a collective numeral used for groups of people) with the plain numeral три.

etymology: From Dutch luik.
commonMistakes: Confusing люк (a hatch/manhole cover) with дверь (a door, a different kind of opening).

aspectUsage: Напоминать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective напомнить.
etymology: From на- + поминать (to remind).
commonMistakes: Напоминать carries two senses — "to remind" and "to resemble" — requiring context to disambiguate.

governance.pattern: + dative + о + prepositional (to remind someone of something)

examples.gloss: This song reminds me of childhood (a standing property).
Remind me every day (repeated, hence the imperfective imperative).
I reminded him about the debt (one completed act).
Remind me to call the doctor.

synonymComparison.note: For resemblance, напоминать + accusative (to call to mind) is close to быть похожим на + accusative (to look like); напоминать also covers similarity of mood or impression.

past.m.gloss: He reminded me of an old friend.

past.f.ru: Она напоминала о сроках каждый день.
past.f.gloss: She reminded us about the deadlines daily.

past.n.gloss: The place was reminiscent of a summer camp.

past.pl.gloss: We kept reminding clients about payment.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm reminding you about the meeting.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You remind me of my sister.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: This smell brings summer to mind.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We remind you of the safety rules.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You remind me of someone.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: These mountains are reminiscent of the Alps.

imperative.sg.gloss: Remind me about it more often.

imperative.pl.gloss: Keep reminding passengers about their tickets.

etymology: Borrowed from English gay.
commonMistakes: Confusing гей (a gay man, specifically) with ЛГБТ (a broader umbrella term).

aspectUsage: Пахнуть is an imperfective stative verb (smell) with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *pachnǫti.
commonMistakes: Confusing the stative "to smell of" пахнуть with the active "to sniff" нюхать.

examples.gloss: It smells nice in here (a state).
The house smelled of fresh bread (an ongoing state).

synonymComparison.note: пахнуть is intransitive — to give off a smell; нюхать is transitive — to smell something (accusative). Цветы пахнут vs Я нюхаю цветы reverses who does what.

past.m.gloss: The air smelled of the sea.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I smell of smoke after the campfire.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: It smells of coffee in here.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You smell of something delicious.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: Roses smell stronger in the evening.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *zelenъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing зелёный (green, the color) with its figurative sense "inexperienced" (a parallel to English usage).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *junъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing the more poetic/formal юный (young, youthful) with the everyday молодой.

etymology: From об- + a Proto-Slavic root *uti (to put on / wear).
commonMistakes: Обувь is a collective noun used only in the singular, with no plural form — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Запереть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective запирать.
etymology: From за- + переть (to push), shifted to mean "to close/lock."
commonMistakes: Confusing запереть (to lock) with закрыть (to close, a more general verb not implying locking).

governance.pattern: + accusative + на + accusative (to lock with a key)

example.gloss: He locked the door with the key.

governance.pattern: + accusative + в + prepositional (to shut someone in)

example.gloss: The cat got shut in the room.

examples.ru: Я всегда запираю дверь на два замка.

examples.gloss: Don't lock it, I'll be back soon.
He locked the house and left (one completed act).
Lock the gate for the night.

synonymComparison.note: запереть is to lock; закрыть is just to close. Закрой дверь and Запри дверь are two different instructions.

past.m.gloss: He locked the door with the key.

past.f.gloss: She locked the office and left.

past.n.gloss: The farm locked up the barn for the winter.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll lock the door when I leave.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you lock up the house yourself?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll lock the office at seven.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll lock the car in the car park.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you lock the office?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll lock the building up for the weekend.

imperative.sg.gloss: Lock the door from the inside.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *volja.
commonMistakes: Воля carries two senses — "will" and "freedom (as in release from prison)" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *prazdьnъ (empty, a day without work).
commonMistakes: Confusing праздник (a holiday/celebration, a festive occasion) with выходной (a day off, not necessarily festive).

aspectUsage: Учитывать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective учесть.
etymology: From у- + a root related to counting/considering.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing учитывать with the single completed act of taking into account учесть.

example.gloss: The client's view has to be taken into account.

governance.pattern: + что clause (to bear in mind that…)

example.gloss: Bear in mind that he's new.

examples.gloss: We always take the team's view into account (habitual).
He wasn't factoring in the risks (ongoing).
I've incorporated all your comments (completed result).
Bear that in mind for next time.

synonymComparison.note: учитывать is the one-word everyday verb; принимать во внимание (with the accusative) is the more formal written phrase. The meaning is essentially the same.

past.m.gloss: He took all the factors into account.

past.f.gloss: She took the guests' wishes into account.

past.pl.gloss: We factored the weather into our planning.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You're not taking what I say into account.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He takes every detail into account.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We take user feedback into account.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you factor in seasonality?

imperative.pl.gloss: Please take local rules into account.

etymology: Derived from сколько (how much).
commonMistakes: "Quantity" количество and "quality" качество sound similar but have opposite meanings.

etymology: Derived from глупый (foolish).
commonMistakes: The instrumental form глупостью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

etymology: Derived from остановить (to stop).
commonMistakes: Confusing остановка (a transit stop, the physical location) with перерыв (a break/pause, a temporal interruption).

aspectUsage: Угрожать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective пригрозить.
etymology: From у- + грозить (to threaten).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing угрожать with the single completed threat пригрозить.

governance.pattern: + dative + instrumental (to threaten someone with something)

example.gloss: He threatened me with a lawsuit.

examples.gloss: The danger threatens the whole district (an ongoing state).
He was constantly threatening to fire us (repeated).
He threatened me with dismissal once (one completed act).
His mother threatened to take the phone away.

synonymComparison.note: угрожать is to threaten harm and takes the dative; пугать is to frighten and takes the accusative. The case government is the opposite.

past.m.gloss: He threatened me over the phone.

past.n.gloss: The flood threatened the whole village.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you threatening the staff?

etymology: Derived from взорвать (to blow up).
commonMistakes: Confusing взрыв (explosion, the event) with бомба (bomb, the device causing it).

etymology: From велик (great) + an archaic root лепый (beautiful).
commonMistakes: Confusing великолепный (magnificent, a strong/elevated praise) with просто хороший (just good, much weaker) — a register difference.

etymology: From не + смотря (without looking).
commonMistakes: Несмотря is always used together with на (несмотря на) — easy to overlook.

etymology: From кое + кто (who).
commonMistakes: Confusing кое-кто (someone specific the speaker has in mind but doesn't name) with кто-то (someone, entirely unspecified).

aspectUsage: Отдохнуть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective отдыхать.
etymology: From от- + a root related to breathing, shifted to mean "to rest."
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed rest отдохнуть with the ongoing отдыхать.

example.gloss: I need a break from work.

governance.pattern: + accusative of duration (how long you rest)

examples.ru: Он отдыхал на берегу весь день.
examples.gloss: He rested on the shore all day (ongoing).

examples.ru: Я отдохнул и снова за работу.
examples.gloss: I took a rest and got back to work (completed result).
Let me rest for five minutes.

synonymComparison.note: отдохнуть is resting in general; выспаться is specifically getting enough sleep. Я отдохнул and Я выспался recover you in different ways.

past.m.gloss: He had a good rest in the summer.

past.n.gloss: The whole family got a rest at the sea.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you rest even a little?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you take a holiday this year?

imperative.pl.gloss: Rest a little before the journey.

aspectUsage: Умолять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective умолить.
etymology: From у- + молить (to beg/pray).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing умолять with the single completed successful plea умолить.

governance.pattern: + accusative + о + prepositional (to beg someone for something)
+ accusative + infinitive (to beg someone to do something)

examples.gloss: He kept begging her not to leave (ongoing).
I beg you, listen to me (the 1st person present works almost as an interjection).
He begged the doctor into seeing us (the pleading worked).

synonymComparison.note: умолять is the strongest form of asking — pleading, almost in tears; просить is the neutral 'to ask.' Умоляю! carries real urgency.

past.f.gloss: She begged him to come back.

past.n.gloss: The whole population was pleading for help.

past.pl.ru: Мы умоляли дать нам ещё день.
past.pl.gloss: We begged for one more day.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I beg you, think about it.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's pleading for a second chance.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You may plead, but the decision is made.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're begging them not to close the school.

imperative.sg.gloss: Don't plead with him, it's useless.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't plead — just explain the situation.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *běda.
commonMistakes: Confusing беда (a serious misfortune) with неприятность (a relatively minor trouble).

etymology: Derived from проклясть (to curse).
commonMistakes: Confusing проклятие (a supernatural curse) with ругательство (a swear word, a verbal insult).

etymology: Derived from помощь (help).
commonMistakes: Confusing помощник (assistant, a person who helps) with ассистент, often used in more formal/professional/academic contexts.

etymology: The past participle of открыть (to open).
commonMistakes: Confusing открытый (open, physical or figurative "open-minded") with откровенный (frank/candid, specifically about openness in speech).

etymology: Derived from чёрт (devil).
commonMistakes: Чёртов and чертовый are near-identical variant spellings with the same meaning — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from зад (back/rear).
commonMistakes: Confusing задний (rear, spatial position) with последний (last, in a sequence/order).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *koleno.
commonMistakes: The irregular plural колени (not колена) is often missed by learners.

etymology: From French princesse.
commonMistakes: Confusing принцесса (princess) with королева (queen, a higher royal title).

etymology: From English dock.
commonMistakes: Confusing док (a dock, for ships) with пристань (a pier/wharf, a related but distinct structure).

etymology: From Latin rosa.
commonMistakes: Confusing роза (rose, the specific flower) with цветок (flower, the general term).

etymology: Derived from искусный (skillful).
commonMistakes: Confusing искусство (art, the creative discipline) with мастерство (craftsmanship/skill, more technical proficiency).

etymology: From French prince.
commonMistakes: Confusing принц (prince) with король (king, a higher royal title).

etymology: Acronym for Соединённые Штаты Америки (United States of America).
commonMistakes: США is indeclinable, keeping the same form in every case — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from крупа (groat/grain), shifted to mean "large-grained," i.e., "large."
commonMistakes: Confusing крупный (large/major, often about scale or significance) with большой (big, a more general size term).

etymology: A fixed expression from the imperative of пожаловать (to favor/grant).
commonMistakes: Confusing пожалуй (a soft, tentative agreement, "I suppose") with может быть (maybe, a more neutral uncertainty).

etymology: Derived from дом (house).
commonMistakes: Домашний (home-related) and семейный (family-related) overlap, but домашний specifically concerns the home — easy to overlook.

etymology: An affectionate diminutive of мама (mom).
commonMistakes: Confusing the affectionate мамочка with the more neutral/formal мать (mother).

aspectUsage: Курить is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of smoking. покурить exists as a delimitative meaning "to smoke for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *kuriti.
commonMistakes: Confusing курить (to smoke, habitual activity) with дымить (to emit smoke, which can apply to objects too).

governance.pattern: with no object, describing a habit

examples.gloss: He has been smoking for twenty years (ongoing habit).
People don't smoke here (an impersonal 3rd plural stating a rule).

synonymComparison.note: 'To quit smoking' is бросить курить — a perfective plus an imperfective infinitive. курить itself has no perfective meaning 'to stop.'
покурить is the bounded perfective 'to have a smoke.' Пойдём покурим ('let's go for a smoke') is the common invitation.

past.m.gloss: He was smoking on the balcony.

past.f.gloss: She smoked when she was young.

past.n.gloss: A whole generation smoked back then.

past.pl.gloss: We were smoking by the entrance.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you smoke?

aspectUsage: Лить is imperfective; its perfective varies by meaning (налить means "to pour into a container").
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *liti.
commonMistakes: Лить's perfective isn't limited to налить — multiple perfectives exist depending on the outcome, easy to overlook.

example.gloss: Don't pour water on the floor.

examples.gloss: Don't pour in so much oil.
Pour me some tea, please (the perfective of filling a vessel).
I poured water into the glass.

synonymComparison.note: лить is the act of pouring or flowing; налить is pouring something into a container. Prefixes split the meanings further: пролить (to spill), вылить (to pour out).

past.n.gloss: It poured from the sky without a break.

past.pl.gloss: We were pouring water on the fire.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm pouring water into the pot.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're pouring past the cup.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're pouring water into the barrel.

aspectUsage: Встречать is imperfective, pairing with the perfective встретить.
etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *vъstrěčati.
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing "to greet/meet" встречать with the single completed meeting встретить.

governance.pattern: + accusative (to see in a year or holiday)

example.gloss: We see in the New Year at home.

examples.ru: Я встречаю его каждый день в метро.
examples.gloss: I run into him every day on the metro (repeated).
She was greeting guests at the entrance (ongoing).
I ran into her by chance (one completed event).

synonymComparison.note: встречать + accusative is transitive — to meet or greet someone; the reflexive встречаться means meeting each other, and also 'to be dating.' встречаться с ним can mean 'she's seeing him.'

past.m.gloss: He met us at the station.

past.f.ru: Она встречала Новый год с друзьями.
past.f.gloss: She saw in the New Year with friends.

past.n.gloss: The agency met tourists at the airport.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm meeting a friend at the airport.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He greets every client in person.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We see in the New Year at home.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you meeting the delegation?

imperative.pl.gloss: Greet the guests at the entrance.

aspectUsage: Путешествовать is imperfective with no true perfective counterpart for the general act of traveling. попутешествовать exists as a delimitative meaning "to travel for a while," not a true pair.
etymology: From путь (way) + шествовать (to proceed).
commonMistakes: Confusing путешествовать (to travel, a general leisure activity) with ехать (to go by vehicle, a directional motion verb).

governance.pattern: + по + dative (the area you travel around)

examples.gloss: I like travelling alone (a general inclination).
They travelled around Asia for six months (ongoing).

synonymComparison.note: путешествовать implies travel as its own purpose; ездить is simply going back and forth by vehicle. Commuting is ездить, sightseeing is путешествовать.

past.n.gloss: The whole family travelled by car.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you travel with children?

nonpast.3pl.ru: Они путешествуют по стране на поезде.
nonpast.3pl.gloss: They're travelling around the country by train.

imperative.pl.gloss: Travel more — it broadens your outlook.

etymology: Derived from бороться (to struggle/wrestle).
commonMistakes: Confusing борьба (struggle/wrestling, figurative or the sport) with бой (a specific fight/battle).

aspectUsage: Заслужить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective заслуживать.
etymology: From за- + служить (to serve).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of earning заслужить with the ongoing state of deserving заслуживать.

examples.gloss: Work like that deserves praise (a standing judgement).
He spent years earning their trust (ongoing).
She earned the award by honest work.

synonymComparison.note: заслужить is to deserve or earn through effort; получить is simply to receive. Он получил награду ('he got the award') differs from Он заслужил награду ('he deserved it').

past.n.gloss: The company earned a good reputation.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll earn respect through what you do.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll earn their gratitude.

imperative.pl.gloss: Earn your clients' trust through your work.

etymology: From Latin inspector.
commonMistakes: Confusing инспектор (a formal investigative role) with полицейский (a general police officer).

etymology: From в + верх (top).
commonMistakes: Confusing вверх (direction, "upward") with наверху (location, "up above").

aspectUsage: Дойти is perfective, pairing with the imperfective доходить.
etymology: From до- + идти (to walk).
commonMistakes: Confusing дойти (to reach a destination on foot) with доехать (to reach by vehicle, a different verb).

example.gloss: We walked as far as the house.

governance.pattern: + до + genitive (figuratively: to get to the heart of something)

examples.ru: Я обычно дохожу до работы за полчаса.
examples.gloss: It usually takes me half an hour to walk to work (repeated).

examples.ru: Мы дошли до вершины к полудню.
examples.gloss: We reached the summit by noon (completed arrival).

examples.ru: Дойди до угла и поверни направо.
examples.gloss: Walk to the corner and turn right.

synonymComparison.note: дойти is reaching a point (marked with до + genitive), often with effort; прийти is arriving somewhere and takes в/на + accusative. Я дошёл до магазина vs Я пришёл в магазин.

past.m.gloss: He walked all the way home.

past.f.gloss: She got to the end of the book.

past.n.gloss: The letter only arrived a month later.

nonpast.2sg.ru: Ты дойдёшь до метро за пять минут.
nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll reach the metro in five minutes.

nonpast.3sg.ru: Он дойдёт до конца, чего бы это ни стоило.
nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll see it through, whatever it costs.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы дойдёте до площади по этой улице.
nonpast.2pl.gloss: This street will take you to the square.

imperative.sg.ru: Дойди до аптеки и купи лекарство.
imperative.sg.gloss: Walk to the pharmacy and buy the medicine.

imperative.pl.gloss: Walk to the end of the corridor.

etymology: An affectionate diminutive of папа (dad).
commonMistakes: Папочка refers to a male but declines like a feminine-pattern noun — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from отвратить (to turn away).
commonMistakes: Confusing the strongly negative отвратительный (disgusting) with the milder неприятный (unpleasant).

etymology: Derived from путешествовать (to travel).
commonMistakes: Confusing путешествие (a longer/adventurous journey) with поездка (a trip, more everyday).

aspectUsage: Приносить is imperfective, pairing with the perfective принести.
etymology: From при- + носить (to carry).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing/habitual приносить with the single completed act of bringing принести.

example.gloss: He brings the post every morning.

examples.gloss: Don't bring food in here (negative command, imperfective).
I've brought you a book (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: приносить is bringing by hand, on foot; привезти is bringing by vehicle. Russian motion verbs split by how you travel.

past.f.gloss: She brought the documents in person.

past.n.gloss: The business brought in a good income.

past.pl.gloss: We used to bring food to the neighbours.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I offer my apologies (a set phrase).

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We bring the documents in the morning.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Do you bring your own laptop?

aspectUsage: Наслаждаться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective насладиться.
etymology: From на- + a root related to сладкий (sweet).
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing наслаждаться (which takes the instrumental case) with the single completed enjoyment насладиться.

examples.gloss: She enjoys music every evening (habitual, ongoing).
I savoured that evening to the full (completed result).
Let me enjoy the peace for a moment.

synonymComparison.note: наслаждаться is savouring something at leisure; радоваться is being glad. Both take the instrumental, but наслаждаться implies lingering in it.

past.f.gloss: She was enjoying the view from the window.

past.n.gloss: The whole family was enjoying the trip.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He's enjoying the quiet of the garden.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Are you enjoying your holiday?

aspectUsage: Добавить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective добавлять.
etymology: From до- + an archaic root бавить (to add).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single completed act of adding добавить with the ongoing/repeated добавлять.

governance.pattern: + accusative + в + accusative (to add to something)

examples.ru: Я всегда добавляю молоко в кофе.
examples.gloss: I always add milk to my coffee (habitual).
I added him as a friend (one completed action).
I'd like to add one thought.

synonymComparison.note: добавить is adding to what's already there; положить is putting something in or down. Добавь соли and Положи соль start from different assumptions.

past.n.gloss: The app added a new feature.

past.pl.ru: Мы добавили два пункта в договор.
past.pl.gloss: We added two clauses to the contract.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll add you to the chat.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you add me to the list?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you add your signature?

etymology: From French journal.
commonMistakes: Confusing журнал (a magazine, periodical) with газета (newspaper, a different format/frequency).

aspectUsage: Застрелить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective застреливать.
etymology: From за- + стрелить (to shoot).
commonMistakes: Confusing застрелить (to shoot dead, a completed fatal act) with стрелять (to shoot, which doesn't imply a fatal hit).

example.gloss: He was shot with a pistol.

examples.ru: В те годы застреливали без суда.
examples.gloss: In those years people were shot without trial (repeated, historical).
Animals like that are no longer shot (current practice).
He accidentally shot the dog (one completed result).
The criminal was shot during the arrest.

synonymComparison.note: стрелять is the act of shooting, with the target in в + accusative; застрелить, with the prefix за-, means shooting dead and takes a direct accusative. The presence of the preposition is the giveaway.

past.m.gloss: He brought the animal down with one shot.

past.pl.gloss: They were shot on the spot.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'm not going to shoot anyone.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Carrying on like that you'll shoot someone.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll shoot the animal if he has to.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll shoot him by accident.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll shoot anyone who comes near.

etymology: Derived from давить (to press).
commonMistakes: Confusing давление (pressure, physical or figurative) with стресс (stress, specifically psychological strain).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *věkъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing век (century, or figuratively "age/era") with возраст (a person's age), despite the superficial parallel to English "age."

etymology: Derived from вина (guilt).
commonMistakes: Confusing the legal/moral виновный (guilty) with the more everyday synonym виноватый.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *deševъ.
commonMistakes: Confusing дешёвый (cheap) with its opposite дорогой (expensive).

etymology: From Greek tele (far) + a derivative of видеть (to see).
commonMistakes: Confusing телевизор (the TV set) with телевидение (television, the broadcasting medium/industry).

etymology: From без- + ум (intellect), "a state lacking reason."
commonMistakes: Confusing безумие (often hyperbolic "craziness/madness") with сумасшествие (insanity, a more clinical/serious term).

etymology: Acronym for дезоксирибонуклеиновая кислота (deoxyribonucleic acid).
commonMistakes: ДНК is indeclinable, keeping the same form in every case — easy to overlook.

etymology: From не + достаточно (enough).
commonMistakes: Недостаточно takes the genitive case — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Потратить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective тратить.
etymology: From по- + тратить (to spend).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of spending потратить with the ongoing тратить.

governance.pattern: + accusative + на + accusative (to spend X on Y)

example.gloss: We spent an hour on the road.

examples.ru: Я потратил на это весь день.
examples.gloss: I spent a whole day on it (completed result).

synonymComparison.note: потратить is the everyday 'to spend'; израсходовать means using a resource up and belongs to technical or accounting language — fuel, materials.

past.m.gloss: He used up all his strength.

past.f.gloss: She spent a month on it.

past.n.gloss: The ministry spent the whole budget.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I won't spend more than an hour.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll spend it all in a day.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы потратим на ремонт две недели.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll spend two weeks on the repairs.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll expend a lot of effort.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll use up the whole stock.

imperative.sg.gloss: Don't spend it all at once.

imperative.pl.gloss: Don't spend more than you need to.

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *sněgъ.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form sometimes takes the locative-type "в снегу" — easy to overlook.

etymology: Derived from груз (cargo).
commonMistakes: Confusing грузовик (a cargo truck) with фургон (a van, generally smaller).

etymology: Derived from холод (cold).
commonMistakes: Confusing холодильник (refrigerator, keeps cool) with морозильник (freezer, keeps frozen).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *pъtica.
commonMistakes: Confusing птица (bird, the general animal) with курица (chicken, a specific domesticated bird).

etymology: The past participle of дать (to give).
commonMistakes: Данный is used in formal documents; этот (this) is the more natural everyday equivalent — easy to overlook.

etymology: The past participle of проклясть (to curse).
commonMistakes: Confusing the verb-derived проклятый (cursed) with the milder, more colloquial чёртов (damn).

etymology: From French soupe.
commonMistakes: Confusing суп (soup, typically with solid ingredients) with бульон (broth, the clear liquid base).

aspectUsage: Перейти is perfective, pairing with the imperfective переходить.
etymology: From пере- + идти (to walk).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of crossing/switching over перейти with the ongoing process переходить.

governance.pattern: + к + dative (to move on to a topic or stage)
+ на + accusative (to move to another place or job)

example.gloss: He moved to a new job.

examples.ru: Я перехожу дорогу здесь каждый день.
examples.gloss: I cross the road here every day (repeated).
He crossed the street and vanished (one completed act).
Let's move on to the next item.

synonymComparison.note: перейти is crossing over — the boundary is the point; пройти is passing by or through. Compare перейти дорогу with пройти мимо.

past.m.gloss: He crossed to the other side.

past.n.gloss: The business passed to a new owner.

past.pl.gloss: We moved on to discussing details.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you switch to the new system?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll switch to a different plan.

imperative.pl.gloss: Move on to the next point.

etymology: Borrowed from English sheriff.
commonMistakes: Confusing шериф (sheriff, a US-specific role) with полицейский (a general police officer).

etymology: From Latin collega.
commonMistakes: Коллега is grammatically feminine-pattern but is a common-gender noun used for both men and women — easy to overlook.

etymology: From когда + то (once).
commonMistakes: Confusing когда-то (once, a vague past time) with когда-нибудь (someday, a vague future time).

etymology: From на + верх (top).
commonMistakes: Confusing наверху (location, "up above") with наверх (direction, "upward").

etymology: From Greek angelos via Church Slavonic.
commonMistakes: Confusing ангел (the religious being) with its figurative use as an affectionate term for a person.

etymology: Derived from тепло (warmth).
commonMistakes: Confusing тёплый (warm, a moderate temperature or figurative warmth) with горячий (hot, a higher degree).

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *jedva.
commonMistakes: Confusing едва (barely, just managing to) with почти (almost, not quite reaching).

etymology: Derived from лицо (face/person).
commonMistakes: The instrumental form личностью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Заработать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective зарабатывать.
etymology: From за- + работать (to work).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of earning заработать with the ongoing process зарабатывать.

example.gloss: He earned a lot of money.

examples.gloss: He earns his money by translating (instrumental of means, habitual).
How much do you earn? (ongoing income)
I earned enough for a car (completed result).
He earned a reputation as an honest man.

synonymComparison.note: зарабатывать is earning through your own work; получать is receiving what you're paid. Я зарабатываю vs Я получаю зарплату.

past.m.gloss: He earned enough for a flat.

past.f.ru: Она заработала первые деньги в школе.
past.f.gloss: She earned her first money at school.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll earn enough for the trip.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll make a name for himself.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll earn it within a month.

nonpast.2pl.ru: Вы заработаете больше в этом году.
nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll earn more this year.

etymology: From French maire.
commonMistakes: Confusing мэр (mayor, a city-level official) with губернатор (governor, a regional-level official).

etymology: Derived from a past-participle-like form of спустить (to lower).
commonMistakes: Спустя is also used postpositively after the noun (e.g. год спустя) — easy to overlook.

aspectUsage: Отвести is perfective, pairing with the imperfective отводить.
etymology: From от- + вести (to lead).
commonMistakes: Confusing отвести (to lead/take someone away) with увести (a near-synonym emphasizing removal from a place).

governance.pattern: + accusative + a destination (to take someone somewhere)
+ accusative + в сторону (to draw someone aside)

examples.ru: Я отвожу сына в школу каждое утро.
examples.gloss: I walk my son to school every morning (habitual).
I took her to the doctor (one completed act).

synonymComparison.note: отвести is taking someone on foot; отвезти is driving them. The verb changes with the mode of travel: отвести в школу, отвезти в аэропорт.

past.m.gloss: He took the children to nursery.

past.f.gloss: She looked away to one side.

past.n.gloss: Management allotted us a separate room.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you take the child to school?

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll take us to the spot.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Could you take me to the director?

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll show you to the hall.

imperative.sg.ru: Отведи его в сторону и объясни.

imperative.pl.gloss: Please show the guests to the hall.

etymology: A comparative-derived adjective of молодой (young).
commonMistakes: Confusing младший (younger, a relative comparison) with молодой (young, an absolute description).

etymology: Derived from способный (capable).
commonMistakes: The instrumental form способностью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

aspectUsage: Появляться is imperfective, pairing with the perfective появиться.
etymology: Derived from a root related to явить (to reveal).
commonMistakes: Confusing the habitual появляться with the single completed appearance появиться.

example.gloss: New ideas keep coming to us.

examples.ru: Он появляется на работе к обеду.
examples.gloss: He turns up at work around lunchtime (repeated).
New cafés keep opening in town (ongoing).
He appeared out of nowhere (a single event).

synonymComparison.note: появляться is showing up, for people and things alike; возникать leans toward abstract emergence, as in Возникла проблема ('a problem has arisen').

past.f.gloss: She turned up at every meeting.

past.n.gloss: The sun kept appearing from behind the clouds.

past.pl.gloss: Problems kept arising one after another.

nonpast.1sg.ru: Я появляюсь там раз в неделю.
nonpast.1sg.gloss: I show up there once a week.

nonpast.1pl.ru: Мы появляемся на экране каждый вечер.
nonpast.1pl.gloss: We appear on screen every evening.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You turn up at just the right moment.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: New models come out every year.

etymology: From Greek zone via French/German.
commonMistakes: Confusing зона (a zone, a defined functional area) with район (a general district/neighborhood).

etymology: An archaic particle marking reported speech.
commonMistakes: Де is nearly absent from modern Russian, surviving mainly in old literature or dialects — easy to overlook.

etymology: Borrowed via Turkic languages, ultimately possibly from Persian.
commonMistakes: Confusing чашка (a handled cup, for hot drinks) with стакан (a glass, without a handle).

etymology: The adverbial form of опасный (dangerous).
commonMistakes: Confusing the predicate/adverb опасно with the adjective опасный describing a noun directly.

etymology: Derived from напасть (to attack).
commonMistakes: Confusing нападение (an attack, a specific event) with агрессия (aggression, a broader behavioral/psychological concept).

etymology: Derived from четыре (four), the week's fourth day.
commonMistakes: Confusing четверг (Thursday) with четыре (four), despite the shared root.

etymology: From не + ведать (not known), originally "an unknown person, bride."
commonMistakes: Confusing невеста (bride/fiancée) with невестка (daughter-in-law/sister-in-law), a different family relation with a similar spelling.

etymology: From Latin procurator.
commonMistakes: Confusing прокурор (prosecutor, representing the state) with адвокат (defense attorney, representing the defendant).

aspectUsage: Захватить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective захватывать.
etymology: From за- + хватить (to grab).
commonMistakes: Захватить carries two senses — "to seize/capture" and "to bring along" — requiring context to disambiguate.

examples.ru: Этот сериал захватывает с первой серии.
examples.gloss: This series grips you from episode one (a standing property).
They were taking town after town (repeated, ongoing).
They seized the airport (one completed act).
Grab me a coffee while you're at it.

synonymComparison.note: захватить is grabbing something on the way or seizing it by force; взять is the neutral 'to take.' Захвати зонт carries that 'while you're at it' feel.

past.m.gloss: He took the documents with him.

past.f.ru: Она захватила зонт на всякий случай.
past.f.gloss: She took an umbrella just in case.

past.pl.gloss: We took food along for the journey.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: Will you grab me some water?

nonpast.2pl.gloss: Will you bring your passport?

etymology: Traces to Proto-Slavic *rana.
commonMistakes: Confusing рана (a physical wound) with травма (trauma, a broader term including psychological harm).

aspectUsage: Привыкнуть is perfective, pairing with the imperfective привыкать.
etymology: From при- + an archaic root выкнуть (to get used to).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed adaptation привыкнуть with the ongoing process привыкать.

governance.pattern: + к + dative (what you get used to)

example.gloss: I've got used to the cold.

governance.pattern: + infinitive (to get used to doing something)

example.gloss: He's used to getting up early.

examples.ru: Я постепенно привыкаю к новому городу.
examples.gloss: I'm gradually getting used to the new city (in progress).
I'm used to it now (the state has been reached; note the masculine past привык with no -л).
You'll get used to it, don't worry.

synonymComparison.note: привыкнуть is getting used to something psychologically; приспособиться is adapting by changing what you do. Both take к + dative.

past.m.gloss: He got used to the new job (as a -нуть verb, the masculine past is привык).

past.f.gloss: She got used to living alone.

past.n.gloss: A whole generation got used to it.

past.pl.gloss: We got used to the noise.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll get used to it in time.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You'll get used to it quickly.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll get used to the schedule.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll get used to the new rules.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll get used to the climate.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll get used to each other.

imperative.sg.ru: Привыкни к мысли, что это надолго.
imperative.sg.gloss: Get used to the idea that this will last.

imperative.pl.gloss: Please get used to the new procedure.

etymology: From Sanskrit sarkara via Persian/Arabic/Latin.
commonMistakes: Confusing сахар (sugar) with сладость (sweetness/a sweet treat, a broader term).

etymology: From в + нутро (the inside).
commonMistakes: Confusing внутрь (direction, "inward") with внутри (location, "inside").

etymology: Derived from выстрелить (to fire).
commonMistakes: Confusing выстрел (a single shot) with стрельба (shooting, the ongoing activity).

aspectUsage: Ошибиться is perfective, pairing with the imperfective ошибаться.
etymology: Traces to a Proto-Slavic root шиб- (to strike/miss).
commonMistakes: Confusing the single mistake ошибиться with the habitual ошибаться.

example.gloss: I made a mistake in my calculations.

governance.pattern: + instrumental (to get a number or address wrong)

examples.gloss: Everyone makes mistakes sometimes (a general truth).

examples.ru: Если я не ошибаюсь, это он.
examples.gloss: If I'm not mistaken, that's him (a set parenthetical).

synonymComparison.note: ошибиться is making a mistake in general; перепутать is mixing two things up, as in перепутать имена ('to confuse the names').

past.m.gloss: He had the wrong address (the masculine past is ошибся).

past.f.gloss: She made an error in her calculations.

past.n.gloss: The device got the measurement wrong.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I won't make that mistake again.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You won't go wrong if you ask.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll make a mistake if he rushes.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We won't go wrong with this choice.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You'll be mistaken if you believe him.

imperative.pl.gloss: Make sure you have the right door.

etymology: Borrowed from German Bord.
commonMistakes: The prepositional form takes the locative-type ending "на борту" rather than "на борте."

etymology: From a root related to зрак (sight/appearance).
commonMistakes: Confusing призрак (ghost, a supernatural entity) with тень (shadow, a physical optical phenomenon).

etymology: Derived from зло (evil).
commonMistakes: Confusing злой (angry/mean, a trait or state) with сердитый (angry, more specifically a temporary emotion).

etymology: From French détail.
commonMistakes: The instrumental form деталью (ending in -ью, soft declension) is easily confused with hard-declension patterns of other feminine nouns.

etymology: From Latin statutum via Polish.
commonMistakes: Статья carries two senses — "a news article" and "a legal article/clause" — requiring context to disambiguate.

etymology: Borrowed from English buck.
commonMistakes: Confusing the colloquial бакс with the formal доллар.

aspectUsage: Убежать is perfective, pairing with the imperfective убегать.
etymology: From у- + бежать (to run).
commonMistakes: Confusing the completed act of running away убежать with the ongoing fleeing убегать.

governance.pattern: + от + genitive (whom or what you run from)

example.gloss: You can't run away from your problems.

examples.ru: Кот всё время убегает на улицу.
examples.gloss: The cat keeps running off outside (repeated).
Don't run away from the conversation.
The dog ran off yesterday (one completed event).

examples.ru: Мне надо убежать на пять минут.
examples.gloss: I need to dash off for five minutes.

synonymComparison.note: убежать is leaving at a run, with urgency or flight about it; уйти is the neutral 'to leave.' Он ушёл and Он убежал paint very different pictures.

past.n.gloss: The milk boiled over (an idiomatic use).

past.pl.gloss: The children ran out into the yard.

nonpast.1sg.gloss: I'll dash off for a minute.

nonpast.2sg.gloss: You can't run away from this.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He'll bolt at the first opportunity.

nonpast.1pl.gloss: We'll run for it if we can.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You won't get away that fast.

nonpast.3pl.gloss: They'll slip out the back door.

aspectUsage: Обвинять is imperfective, pairing with the perfective обвинить.
etymology: From об- + винить (to blame, from вина "guilt").
commonMistakes: Confusing the ongoing обвинять with the single completed accusation обвинить.

governance.pattern: + accusative + в + prepositional (to accuse someone of something)

examples.gloss: He was charged with fraud (one completed accusation).
Don't be quick to blame someone.

synonymComparison.note: обвинять is accusing formally, with в + prepositional; винить is blaming more personally, with the same government. Legal contexts use обвинять.

past.n.gloss: The investigation accused him of negligence.

past.pl.gloss: We were being blamed for the delay.

nonpast.3sg.gloss: He blames his colleagues for the mistake.

nonpast.2pl.gloss: You're accusing him without evidence.

imperative.sg.ru: Не обвиняй его, он не виноват.
imperative.sg.gloss: Don't blame him, it isn't his fault.

etymology: Borrowed from Turkic languages.
commonMistakes: Confusing карман (a pocket, sewn into clothing) with сумка (a bag, a separate carried item).

aspectUsage: Подтвердить is perfective, pairing with the imperfective подтверждать.
etymology: From под- + твердить (to assert, from твёрдый "firm").
