commonMistakes: Takes над plus instrumental (издеваться над кем-то).

etymology: An adjective formed from достоять (an old root meaning 'to be worthy of').
commonMistakes: Also appears in the short form достоин.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of отпустить ('to let go, grant leave').
commonMistakes: Unlike каникулы (a student's break), отпуск primarily refers to a worker's paid leave.

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of Франция ('France').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse its declension with that of the country name Франция.

aspectUsage: Пообещать is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'promising,' paired with the imperfective обещать.
etymology: Formed from по- (prefix) plus обещать ('to promise').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective обещать.

etymology: An agent noun formed from the root of играть ('to play').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (игрока).

etymology: A borrowing from Italian scenario.
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively in худший сценарий ('worst-case scenario').

etymology: A borrowing from French attaque.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym оборона ('defense').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin canalis.
commonMistakes: Has both the sense of 'canal' and of a TV/information 'channel.'

etymology: Formed from в- ('into') plus переди (an old root for 'the front part').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym позади ('behind').

etymology: The adverbial form of реальный ('real').
commonMistakes: Also used colloquially as a mere intensifier ('really, seriously').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek daimon.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (демона).

aspectUsage: Пожениться is perfective, marking the single completed act of 'getting married' (as a couple), paired with the imperfective жениться. Its subject is always plural (the couple).
etymology: Formed from по- (prefix) plus жениться ('to marry').
commonMistakes: For a singular subject use жениться (a man marrying) or выйти замуж (a woman marrying).

aspectUsage: Ужинать is imperfective, meaning 'to have dinner,' paired with the perfective поужинать.
etymology: A verb formed from the root of ужин ('dinner').
commonMistakes: Easy to confuse with the similarly formed завтракать ('to have breakfast') and обедать ('to have lunch').

etymology: A colloquial adverb of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with напрасно, but зря sounds more colloquial.

aspectUsage: Бегать is a multidirectional motion verb with only an imperfective form (the unidirectional verb is бежать; the perfective varies by context, e.g. побежать).
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse it with the unidirectional бежать (repeated/multidirectional versus a single direction of running).

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with работа ('work'), but труд sounds more literary and emphasizes 'toil, effort.'

etymology: A noun formed from the root of устроить ('to arrange, set up').
commonMistakes: Has both the sense of 'device, mechanism' and of 'getting set up/placed' (e.g. for a job).

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of север ('north').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym южный ('southern').

aspectUsage: Меняться is imperfective, describing the process of 'changing (oneself),' paired with the perfective измениться.
etymology: A reflexive verb formed from the root of менять ('to change').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the transitive менять ('to change something') with the reflexive меняться ('to change oneself, or to swap').

etymology: A borrowing from Dutch roer.
commonMistakes: Note the set phrase за рулём ('behind the wheel, driving').

aspectUsage: Создавать is imperfective, describing the process of 'creating,' paired with the perfective создать.
etymology: Formed from с- ('together') plus давать (an old root meaning 'to give').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective создать.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin copia.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym оригинал ('original').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym горький ('bitter').

etymology: An interjection of onomatopoeic origin expressing enjoyment.

aspectUsage: Отвалить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective отваливать. Used slangily to mean 'to leave, get out.'

commonMistakes: A fairly crude slang term — avoid it in polite settings.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: The plural слёзы has irregular forms (this dictionary only covers the singular).

aspectUsage: Выступать is imperfective, meaning 'to speak publicly, perform,' paired with the perfective выступить.
etymology: Formed from вы- ('out') plus ступать (an old root meaning 'to step').
commonMistakes: Also has the sense 'to oppose' with против plus genitive (выступать против чего-то).

etymology: A borrowing from Latin magister.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (мастера).

etymology: A noun formed from an old root meaning 'to burn.'
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with огонь ('fire'), but пожар refers to an uncontrolled fire.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of собрать ('to gather').
commonMistakes: Has both the sense of 'meeting, gathering' and 'collected works.'

aspectUsage: Организовать is biaspectual (the same form serves as both imperfective and perfective), meaning 'to organize' — a common feature of borrowed verbs in -овать.
etymology: A borrowing from Latin organizare.
commonMistakes: Whether it reads as perfective or imperfective depends on context.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of прервать ('to interrupt').

aspectUsage: Предоставить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective предоставлять.
etymology: Formed from пред- ('before') plus доставить ('to deliver').
commonMistakes: Sounds more formal and bureaucratic than the plain verb дать ('to give').

aspectUsage: Направляться is imperfective, meaning 'to head toward,' paired with the perfective направиться.
etymology: A reflexive verb formed from the root of направление ('direction').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective направиться.

etymology: The adverbial form of медленный ('slow').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym быстро ('fast').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of извинить ('to forgive, excuse').
commonMistakes: More often used in the plural извинения than in the singular.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek talanton.

etymology: An ordinal numeral (adjective-type) formed from the root of четыре ('four').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also appears figuratively in яблоко раздора ('bone of contention').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of развести ('to separate, divide').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym брак ('marriage').

aspectUsage: Изучать is imperfective, describing the process of 'studying (systematically),' paired with the perfective изучить.
etymology: Formed from из- (a thoroughness prefix) plus учать (related to учить, 'to teach').

aspectUsage: Поживать is an imperfective verb meaning 'to be getting on, living,' an idiomatic verb with no corresponding perfective. It is frequent in the set phrase как поживаешь ('how are you doing?').

aspectUsage: Выслушать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective выслушивать.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.

etymology: The adverbial form of внезапный ('sudden').
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with вдруг, but внезапно sounds more bookish.

commonMistakes: Also used figuratively as a 'mask hiding one's true self' (снять маску).

etymology: The adverbial form of специальный ('special').
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with намеренно ('deliberately'), but специально is more common colloquially.

aspectUsage: Обмануть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective обманывать.

commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective обманывать.

aspectUsage: Сжечь is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective сжигать.

aspectUsage: Творить is imperfective, meaning 'to create,' or colloquially 'to be up to (something troublesome),' paired with the perfective сотворить.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.

aspectUsage: Предупреждать is imperfective, meaning 'to warn,' paired with the perfective предупредить.
etymology: Formed from пред- ('before') plus упреждать (an old root meaning 'to anticipate').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective предупредить.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of завести ('to start up, establish').

aspectUsage: Приближаться is imperfective, describing the process of 'approaching,' paired with the perfective приблизиться.

aspectUsage: Совершать is imperfective, describing the process of 'carrying out, performing,' paired with the perfective совершить.

aspectUsage: Выстрелить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective стрелять.

etymology: A borrowing from Italian concerto.
commonMistakes: Refers generally to any type of musical performance, regardless of genre.

aspectUsage: Отстать is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'falling behind, leaving someone alone,' paired with the imperfective отставать.

aspectUsage: Раскрыть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective раскрывать.

aspectUsage: Тянуть is imperfective, describing the process of 'pulling, dragging,' paired with the perfective потянуть.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of священный ('sacred').

aspectUsage: Превратиться is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective превращаться.

commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective предпочитать.

aspectUsage: Починить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective чинить.
etymology: Formed from по- (prefix) plus чинить ('to repair').
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively in починить отношения ('to repair a relationship').

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of стоять ('to stand').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym временный ('temporary').

aspectUsage: Нарушить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective нарушать.
etymology: Formed from на- (prefix) plus рушить (an old root meaning 'to destroy').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym соблюдать ('to observe/comply with').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of выбрать ('to choose'), used only in the plural.
commonMistakes: There is no singular form — it is always treated as plural.

aspectUsage: Вспоминать is imperfective, describing the process of 'recalling,' paired with the perfective вспомнить.
etymology: Formed from воз- ('again') plus поминать (an old root meaning 'to remember').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective вспомнить.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Note the instrumental form зимой ('in winter') as a common adverbial usage.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of присутствовать ('to be present').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym отсутствие ('absence').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of весить ('to weigh').
commonMistakes: Has both a literal sense ('weight') and a figurative sense ('importance, influence').

aspectUsage: Выдать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective выдавать.
etymology: Formed from вы- ('out') plus дать ('to give').
commonMistakes: Used not only literally ('to issue') but also figuratively ('to let slip a secret, betray').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of драться ('to fight').
commonMistakes: Refers to a smaller-scale personal 'fight, brawl' than бой ('battle').

etymology: Formed from с- ('together') plus часть ('part, fate').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym несчастье ('misfortune').

etymology: A borrowing from French paquet.
commonMistakes: Has both the sense of a '(plastic) bag' and of a 'package, bundle (of services, etc.).'

aspectUsage: Упоминать is imperfective, meaning 'to mention,' paired with the perfective упомянуть.
etymology: Formed from у- (intensifying prefix) plus поминать (an old root meaning 'to remember').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective упомянуть.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of расти ('to grow').
commonMistakes: Has both a personal sense ('height') and an economic sense ('growth').

aspectUsage: Владеть is an imperfective verb describing the state of 'owning, mastering.' The derived овладеть describes the related completed act of 'acquiring/mastering,' but is a related word rather than a true aspectual pair.
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Takes the instrumental case (владеть чем-то).

etymology: An intensifying adjective of slang origin related to гребсти/грёб ('to row').
commonMistakes: A quite crude colloquial term — avoid it in polite settings.

etymology: A borrowing from French corridor.
commonMistakes: Unlike холл ('a wide lobby'), коридор refers to a narrow hallway.

etymology: A feminine noun formed from the root of красивый ('beautiful').
commonMistakes: Worth learning alongside the masculine counterpart красавец ('handsome man').

aspectUsage: Родить is perfective, meaning 'to give birth.' The corresponding imperfective is рожать (родить itself is sometimes used biaspectually).
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Because of its biaspectual use, context determines whether it reads as perfective or imperfective.

aspectUsage: Лечь is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective ложиться.
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective ложиться.

aspectUsage: Жалеть is imperfective, describing the process of 'feeling sorry, regretting,' paired with the perfective пожалеть.
etymology: A verb formed from the root of жаль ('a pity').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective пожалеть.

etymology: A borrowing from French motif.
commonMistakes: Has both a 'motive' sense and a musical 'motif' sense.

etymology: An adverb formed from the root of буква ('letter').
commonMistakes: Also used colloquially as a mere intensifier ('really, just').

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of вчера ('yesterday').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym сегодняшний ('today's').

etymology: A month name borrowed from Latin Maius.
commonMistakes: Month names are usually lowercase.

etymology: The adverbial form of скучный ('boring').
commonMistakes: The person feeling bored takes the dative rather than being the subject (мне скучно).

etymology: A noun formed from the root of договориться ('to come to an agreement').
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with контракт (more colloquial), but договор covers a broader range of formal agreements/treaties.

aspectUsage: Солгать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective лгать.
etymology: Formed from с- (a completive prefix) plus лгать ('to lie').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective лгать.

etymology: A determiner of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with другой ('other'), but иной sounds more bookish.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also appears figuratively in колесо судьбы ('the wheel of fate').

aspectUsage: Покидать is imperfective, meaning 'to leave,' paired with the perfective покинуть.
etymology: Formed from по- (prefix) plus кидать (an old root meaning 'to throw').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective покинуть.

etymology: The adverbial form of естественный ('natural').
commonMistakes: Also used colloquially as an expression of agreement meaning 'of course.'

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of цена ('price, value').
commonMistakes: Unlike дорогой ('expensive'), ценный includes non-monetary 'value' as well.

etymology: An archaic demonstrative determiner of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Rarely used in modern Russian — carries an archaic, literary tone.

aspectUsage: Беречь is imperfective, meaning 'to cherish, protect,' paired with the perfective сберечь.
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective сберечь.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin reputatio.
commonMistakes: Unlike имидж ('a surface image'), репутация refers to longer-standing trust/standing.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of допросить ('to interrogate').
commonMistakes: Unlike следствие ('investigation' in general), допрос refers to the specific act of 'questioning.'

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal sense (city 'square') and a mathematical sense ('area').

etymology: A comparative adverb formed from низкий ('low').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym выше ('higher').

etymology: A borrowing from French visite.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with посещение ('visit' in general), but визит often implies a more formal visit.

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of общество ('society').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym личный ('personal').

aspectUsage: Настать is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'arriving (a time),' paired with the imperfective наставать. Its subject is typically an inanimate time expression, and an imperative is practically never used.
etymology: Formed from на- (prefix) plus стать ('to become').
commonMistakes: The subject is limited to inanimate time expressions.

etymology: Formed from не- (negation) plus надолго ('for a long time').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym надолго ('for a long time').

etymology: A month name derived from Latin septem.
commonMistakes: Month names are usually lowercase.

aspectUsage: Попасться is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective попадаться.
etymology: Formed from по- (prefix) plus пасться (related to падать, 'to fall').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective попадаться.

etymology: A compound noun formed from пол- ('half') plus часа (the genitive form of 'hour').
commonMistakes: Note the irregular compound declension (e.g. получаса).

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of тайна ('secret').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym явный ('obvious').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of тревожить ('to alarm').
commonMistakes: Unlike страх ('fear of something specific'), тревога refers to a more diffuse 'anxiety.'

etymology: A borrowing from Latin objectum.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with предмет ('thing'), but объект is more formal and technical.

etymology: An agent noun formed from the root of продать ('to sell').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (продавца).

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of гражданин ('citizen').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym военный ('military').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym тихий ('quiet').

aspectUsage: Проследить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective прослеживать.
etymology: Formed from про- ('through') plus следить (related to след, 'track').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective прослеживать.

etymology: The comparative of короткий ('short'), colloquially used as a discourse connector.
commonMistakes: Worth learning its colloquial 'in short, anyway' usage.

aspectUsage: Давить is imperfective, describing the process of 'pressing, pushing,' paired with the perfective надавить.
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Used not only literally ('to press') but also figuratively ('to pressure someone psychologically').

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of знать ('to know').
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with известный ('known'), but знаменитый implies a stronger 'famous, celebrated.'

aspectUsage: Кормить is imperfective, describing the process of 'feeding,' paired with the perfective накормить.
etymology: A verb formed from the root of корм ('feed, fodder').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective накормить.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of признать ('to acknowledge').
commonMistakes: Has both the sense of 'confession' and 'recognition/acclaim.'

etymology: A borrowing from Greek technologia.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with техника ('technology/equipment' broadly), but технология refers to a more systematic 'process, method.'

etymology: A borrowing from Latin principium.
commonMistakes: Unlike правило ('rule,' a specific instruction), принцип refers to a more fundamental 'principle.'

aspectUsage: Просыпаться is imperfective, meaning 'to wake up,' paired with the perfective проснуться.
etymology: Related to the root of сыпаться ('to scatter'), via the prefix про-.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective проснуться.

etymology: A borrowing from French régisseur.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (режиссера). The standard spelling is режиссёр.

etymology: Formed from не- (negation) plus вероятный ('probable,' related to верить, 'to believe').
commonMistakes: Used more as an emphatic 'unbelievable' than literally 'improbable.'

etymology: Formed from кое- (an indefiniteness prefix) plus какой ('what kind').
commonMistakes: Carries a casual, understated nuance of 'a few, some.'

etymology: A noun formed from the root of дышать ('to breathe').
commonMistakes: Also appears figuratively in затаить дыхание ('to hold one's breath').

etymology: An abbreviation of господин ('Mr.'), indeclinable.
commonMistakes: It does not actually decline (this dictionary shows all cases as the same word for convenience).

aspectUsage: Указывать is imperfective, describing the process of 'indicating, pointing out,' paired with the perfective указать.
etymology: Formed from у- (intensifying prefix) plus казывать (an old root meaning 'to show').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective указать.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with дедушка (an affectionate form), but дед is plainer and more neutral. Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (деда).

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also used politically to mean a 'wing/faction' of an organization (левое крыло партии).

aspectUsage: Прожить is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'living (for a period),' paired with the imperfective проживать.
etymology: Formed from про- ('through') plus жить ('to live').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective проживать.

etymology: A noun related to полагать (an old root meaning 'to place').
commonMistakes: Also appears figuratively in положить на полку ('to shelve/put off a plan').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of охотиться ('to hunt').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (охотника).

aspectUsage: Приготовиться is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective приготовляться.
etymology: Formed from при- (prefix) plus готовиться ('to prepare oneself').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective приготовляться.

etymology: The adverbial form of официальный ('official').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym неофициально ('unofficially').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also used colloquially as an insult for an unpleasant man.

etymology: Formed from мёд ('honey') plus ведь (an old root meaning 'knower'), originally 'honey-knower.'
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (медведя).

etymology: A borrowing from Latin fructus.
commonMistakes: Distinguish it from овощ ('vegetable').

etymology: A nominalized neuter form of целый ('whole, complete').
commonMistakes: Note its declension follows adjective patterns.

aspectUsage: Подавать is imperfective, describing the process of 'serving, submitting,' paired with the perfective подать.
etymology: Formed from под- ('under') plus давать ('to give').
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively in подавать надежды ('to show promise').

aspectUsage: Заболеть is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'becoming ill,' paired with the imperfective болеть.
etymology: Formed from за- (an initiating prefix) plus болеть ('to be sick').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective болеть.

aspectUsage: Присмотреть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective присматривать.
etymology: Formed from при- (prefix) plus смотреть ('to look').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective присматривать.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of напиться ('to drink').
commonMistakes: Worth pairing with еда ('food') as the general term for 'drink.'

etymology: Formed from the interjection ну ('come on') plus the softening suffix -ка.
commonMistakes: Softens a command — note its function in imperative sentences.

aspectUsage: Приводить is imperfective, describing the process of 'bringing, leading,' paired with the perfective привести.
etymology: Formed from при- ('toward') plus водить ('to lead').
commonMistakes: Worth learning the idiom приводить в порядок ('to put in order').

etymology: A diminutive of стол ('table').
commonMistakes: Note the restaurant idiom забронировать столик ('to reserve a table').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively as an insult meaning 'a treacherous person.'

etymology: A borrowing from English lift.
commonMistakes: Distinguish it from эскалатор ('escalator').

aspectUsage: Замолчать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective замолкать.
etymology: Formed from за- (an initiating prefix) plus молчать ('to be silent').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective замолкать.

etymology: Formed from в- ('in') plus двоём (related to два, 'two').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym одному ('alone').

etymology: Formed from не- (negation) plus виновный ('guilty,' related to вина, 'guilt').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym виновный ('guilty').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin status.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with положение ('situation/standing' in general), but статус is more formal.

aspectUsage: Требоваться is imperfective, describing the process of 'being required,' paired with the perfective потребоваться. Its subject is normally inanimate, and an imperative is practically never used.
etymology: A reflexive verb formed from the root of требовать ('to demand').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective потребоваться.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym перед ('front').

etymology: Formed from перед ('before') plus идущий (related to идти, 'to go').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym следующий ('next').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek aither.
commonMistakes: Has a broadcast sense ('airwaves') distinct from the older chemical term 'ether.'

etymology: A borrowing from Greek organon.
commonMistakes: Has both an anatomical sense ('(body) organ') and an institutional sense ('(governmental) body').

aspectUsage: Отнести is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective относить.
etymology: Formed from от- ('away') plus нести ('to carry').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective относить.

etymology: A borrowing from Italian studio.
commonMistakes: Has both the sense of a 'studio apartment' and a '(recording/production) studio.'

etymology: A noun formed from the root of нарушить ('to violate').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym соблюдение ('compliance').

etymology: An agent noun related to an old root connected to творить ('to create').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (художника).

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of один ('one').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of просить ('to ask for').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of складывать ('to stack').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also appears figuratively in в хвост очереди ('at the back/tail of the line').

etymology: An agent noun formed from the root of победить ('to win').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (победителя).

etymology: A borrowing from French expert.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (эксперта).

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym север ('north').

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of честь ('honor').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym лживый ('deceitful').

aspectUsage: Наступить is perfective, marking a single completed act of 'stepping on' or '(a time) arriving,' paired with the imperfective наступать.

commonMistakes: Also appears figuratively in наступить на те же грабли ('to repeat the same mistake').

aspectUsage: Присматривать is imperfective, meaning 'to watch over, look after,' paired with the perfective присмотреть.
etymology: Formed from при- (prefix) plus сматривать (an old root related to смотреть, 'to look').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective присмотреть.

etymology: Formed from не- (negation) plus легко ('easily').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym легко ('easily').

etymology: A colloquial slang noun, reportedly derived from хрен ('horseradish').
commonMistakes: A quite colloquial slang term — avoid in formal writing.

etymology: A noun formed from the root of страдать ('to suffer').
commonMistakes: Refers to a more intense 'passion' than увлечение ('hobby, interest').

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of Китай ('China').

etymology: A noun formed from the root of улыбаться ('to smile').
commonMistakes: Unlike смех ('laughter,' which has a sound), улыбка refers to a quiet facial expression.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek methodos.
commonMistakes: Near-synonymous with способ ('way' in general), but метод refers to a more systematic 'method.'

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Unlike звук ('sound'), буква refers to the written letter itself.

aspectUsage: Заканчивать is imperfective, describing the process of 'finishing,' paired with the perfective закончить.
etymology: Formed from за- (prefix) plus канчивать (related to конец, 'end').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the perfective закончить.

aspectUsage: Говориться is an imperfective verb expressing the passive/impersonal 'it is said,' with no perfective counterpart in this usage.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek klinike.

etymology: A borrowing from English site.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek drakon.

aspectUsage: Направить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective направлять.

aspectUsage: Отследить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective отслеживать.

aspectUsage: Одолжить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective одалживать.

aspectUsage: Обманывать is imperfective, describing the process of 'deceiving,' paired with the perfective обмануть.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.

etymology: An adjective formed from the root of частить ('to do frequently').

aspectUsage: Побежать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective бежать (originally an inchoative meaning 'to start running,' but taught as the standard aspectual pair).

commonMistakes: Pairs with the unidirectional бежать, not the multidirectional бегать.

etymology: A word derived from a root related to рядить ('to arrange').
commonMistakes: More organized/military in connotation than группа ('group' in general).

aspectUsage: Удалить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective удалять.
etymology: Formed from даль ('distance') plus the prefix у-.
commonMistakes: Very commonly used in the digital sense of 'to delete.'

etymology: A borrowing from French cousin.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (кузена); the feminine form is кузина.

etymology: An adjective derived from центр ('center').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym периферийный ('peripheral').

etymology: A slang noun derived from the vulgar хуй.
commonMistakes: Even more vulgar than фигня or хрень.

etymology: A word derived from двор ('court, yard').
commonMistakes: Similar to замок ('castle'), but дворец emphasizes a residential/ceremonial 'palace' over fortification.

etymology: An adjective derived from звезда ('star').
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively for 'star-like, celebrity' status (e.g. звёздная болезнь, 'star syndrome').

etymology: A substantivized adjective derived from пожар ('fire').
commonMistakes: A substantivized, animate adjective that declines following adjective endings.

etymology: An adjective derived from a borrowing of Greek politikos.
commonMistakes: Broader than государственный ('state'), covering political activity in general.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin, sharing a root with давать ('to give').
commonMistakes: More abstract and literary than подарок ('a concrete gift') — often means 'a talent, a bestowed gift.'

etymology: Formed from the prefix по- plus среди ('among'); takes the genitive case.
commonMistakes: Unlike среди ('among, in the midst of several things'), посреди emphasizes being 'right in the middle.'

etymology: A borrowing from Italian bravo.
commonMistakes: An interjection of applause/praise that never inflects.

etymology: A noun derived from the root of повредить ('to damage').
commonMistakes: Has both a physical 'damage' sense and a medical 'injury' sense.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin legenda.
commonMistakes: Often contains a historical element, unlike миф ('myth,' more supernatural).

etymology: An adjective of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has several senses: physically 'sharp,' intensely 'acute (pain),' and 'spicy (food).'

aspectUsage: Заехать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective заезжать.
etymology: Formed from ехать ('to go by vehicle') plus the prefix за-.
commonMistakes: Note the imperative заезжай uses a different stem than the infinitive.

etymology: A colloquial diminutive of карта ('a card').
commonMistakes: Very commonly used instead of карта in colloquial speech (e.g. банковская карточка = 'bank card').

aspectUsage: Нажать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective нажимать.
etymology: Formed from жать ('to press, squeeze') plus the prefix на-.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal physical 'to press' sense and a digital 'to click' sense.

aspectUsage: Присаживаться is imperfective, describing the process of 'sitting down briefly,' paired with the perfective присесть.
etymology: A reflexive form derived from сажать ('to seat') plus the prefix при-.
commonMistakes: The imperative присаживайтесь ('please take a seat') is an extremely common polite phrase.

etymology: Formed from где ('where') plus the indefiniteness suffix нибудь.
commonMistakes: Unlike где-то ('somewhere specific but unknown'), где-нибудь means 'anywhere at all.'

etymology: A colloquial shortening of прямо ('directly, really').
commonMistakes: A clipped colloquial form of прямо — use only in casual speech.

etymology: A borrowing from French département.
commonMistakes: Often a larger, more official organizational unit than отдел ('a department' generally).

etymology: A female first name of Greek origin.
commonMistakes: As a proper noun it is normally capitalized, though this dictionary's data uses lowercase; the diminutive form is Лена.

aspectUsage: Проникнуть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective проникать.
etymology: An old root plus the prefix про- ('through').
commonMistakes: Note the irregular masculine past form проник, which drops the -ну- suffix.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both a plant 'leaf' sense and a 'sheet (of paper)' sense, with different plural forms depending on meaning (листья = leaves, листы = sheets).

etymology: A noun derived from собственный ('one's own').
commonMistakes: Focuses on legal ownership, more than имущество ('property/assets' themselves).

etymology: An adjective derived from наука ('science').
commonMistakes: Don't confuse it with технический ('technical').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek diskos.
commonMistakes: Has both a storage-media 'disc' sense and a computer 'hard disk' sense.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both an animal 'chicken/hen' sense and a food 'chicken meat' sense.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin effectus.
commonMistakes: More specific than результат ('result' in general) — refers to a particular 'effect, impact.'

etymology: An adjective derived from солнце ('sun').
commonMistakes: Also appears in many idioms, such as солнечный зайчик ('a reflected ray of light').

aspectUsage: Тащить is imperfective, meaning 'to drag, haul.' The related потащить means 'to start dragging,' with the perfective varying by destination.
etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: A unidirectional verb of motion, distinct from the multidirectional торгать.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Very commonly used figuratively in ни капли ('not a drop, not at all').

etymology: A noun derived from воскресение ('resurrection'), meaning 'the day of resurrection.'
commonMistakes: Day names are written with a lowercase letter in running text.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek tomos.
commonMistakes: Refers to a 'volume' of a book — distinct from the name Том.

etymology: The irregular plural of дитя ('child'), of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: An irregular plural with a different root from the singular ребёнок.

aspectUsage: Глянуть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective глядеть.
etymology: A colloquial word derived from глядеть ('to look').
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with the colloquial взглянуть ('to glance').

etymology: The plural of a word derived from родить ('to give birth').
commonMistakes: The singular родитель refers to 'one parent/guardian.'

etymology: The irregular plural of человек ('person'), of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: An irregular plural with a different root from the singular человек.

etymology: A word of Tatar origin, always used in the plural.
commonMistakes: There is no singular form — it is always treated as plural.

etymology: An adverb derived from крайний ('extreme').
commonMistakes: Stronger than очень ('very') — emphasizes 'extremely.'

etymology: A borrowing from Latin minimum.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym максимум ('maximum'); also used adverbially to mean 'at least.'

etymology: A borrowing from English trolleybus.
commonMistakes: Differs from автобус ('bus') by drawing power from overhead wires.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: A colloquial word for 'sense, use'; the negative нет толку is especially common.

aspectUsage: Умываться is imperfective, describing the process of 'washing one's face,' paired with the perfective умыться.
etymology: A reflexive form derived from мыть ('to wash') plus the prefix у-.
commonMistakes: Specific to washing the face, unlike мыться ('to wash/bathe the whole body').

aspectUsage: Изменять is imperfective, describing the process of 'changing,' paired with the perfective изменить.
etymology: An old root meaning 'other' plus the prefix из-.
commonMistakes: Besides 'to change,' it also means 'to cheat on (a spouse)' (изменять мужу/жене).

etymology: The instrumental form of путь ('a path'), grammaticalized as a preposition; it takes the instrumental case.
commonMistakes: Not about a physical 'path' — it means 'by means of' in an abstract sense.

etymology: An adverb derived from грустный ('sad').
commonMistakes: Commonly used as an impersonal predicate meaning '(someone) feels sad.'

etymology: An adjective derived from восток ('east').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym западный ('western').

etymology: An indefinite determiner of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: More literary than the colloquial какой-то, meaning 'a certain, some.'

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both an ornamental 'poppy flower' sense and an edible 'poppy seed' sense.

etymology: An adjective derived from низ ('bottom').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym верхний ('upper').

etymology: A borrowing from French kilomètre.
commonMistakes: Note the special plural forms needed after numerals (e.g. километров for 5+).

etymology: A borrowing from French campagne.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse with the identically-pronounced компания ('a company, business').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin, sharing a root with война ('war').
commonMistakes: More literary/historical than солдат ('a modern soldier'); being animate, the accusative matches the genitive form (воина).

etymology: A borrowing of Polish origin.
commonMistakes: Unlike брюки ('trousers,' plural), a skirt is counted in the singular.

etymology: A collective noun derived from человек ('person').
commonMistakes: An abstract collective noun always used in the singular.

etymology: A noun derived from страх ('fear'), meaning 'something that wards off danger.'
commonMistakes: Refers to a specific 'insurance policy,' more concrete than страхование ('insurance' as a system).

etymology: A borrowing from Greek epeisodion.
commonMistakes: Similar to серия ('a series installment'), but эпизод can also refer to a standalone 'scene, incident.'

aspectUsage: Соврать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective врать.
etymology: Formed from врать ('to lie') plus the prefix с-.
commonMistakes: A colloquial word, distinct from the more formal лгать.

etymology: A noun derived from a root related to вести ('to know, lead').
commonMistakes: The plural сведения often means 'information, data.'

etymology: A neuter noun derived from право ('law, right') plus судить ('to judge').
commonMistakes: More abstract than суд ('a court, trial') — refers to 'justice' as a system.

aspectUsage: Целоваться is imperfective, meaning 'to kiss each other,' paired with the perfective поцеловаться.
etymology: The reflexive form of целовать ('to kiss').
commonMistakes: Целовать means 'to kiss (someone),' while целоваться means 'to kiss each other.'

etymology: A borrowing from Latin alibi.
commonMistakes: An indeclinable noun — the same form is used in every case.

etymology: A noun derived from ценить ('to value, appreciate').
commonMistakes: Has both a school 'grade' sense and a general 'evaluation' sense.

aspectUsage: Предположить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective предполагать.
etymology: Formed from положить ('to put') plus the prefix пред-.
commonMistakes: Means 'to suppose, assume' — not based on certain knowledge.

etymology: An adjective derived from космос ('space, cosmos').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym земной ('terrestrial').

etymology: A word derived from за- ('behind') plus падать ('to fall,' as the sun sets).
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym восток ('east').

etymology: An adverb of direction formed from на- plus левый ('left').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym направо ('to the right').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek prōtokollon.
commonMistakes: Has both a meeting 'minutes' sense and a legal 'report, record' sense.

etymology: A noun derived from неудача ('failure').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (неудачника); the feminine form is неудачница.

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively for 'venom, spite' (слова, полные яда, 'words full of venom').

etymology: A borrowing from French vélocipède.
commonMistakes: Inanimate, not treated as an animate noun.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin candidatus.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (кандидата).

etymology: A vulgar feminine slang noun derived from дурной ('foolish').
commonMistakes: A very insulting word; the masculine form is дурак — use with great care.

aspectUsage: Состоять is imperfective, expressing a relational/stative sense of 'consisting of,' with no perfective counterpart.
etymology: Formed from стоять ('to stand') plus the prefix со-.
commonMistakes: The object is expressed with из + genitive (состоять из чего), or в + prepositional (состоять в чём).

aspectUsage: Включать is imperfective, meaning 'to include, turn on,' paired with the perfective включить.
etymology: An old root meaning 'to close' plus the prefix в-.
commonMistakes: Has both a 'to turn on' sense and a 'to include' sense.

aspectUsage: Похоронить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective хоронить.
etymology: Formed from хоронить ('to bury') plus the prefix по-.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'to bury' sense and a figurative 'to bury (hopes)' sense.

aspectUsage: Осознать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective осознавать.
etymology: An old root meaning 'to know' plus the prefix о-.
commonMistakes: Carries a deeper nuance of 'coming to realize/be aware of' than понять.

aspectUsage: Довериться is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective доверяться.
etymology: A word derived from the reflexive of доверять ('to trust').
commonMistakes: The object is expressed in the dative case (довериться кому-чему).

etymology: A borrowing of Turkish origin.
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively for 'a puppet-like person.'

etymology: A borrowing from Greek technē.
commonMistakes: Has both a physical 'equipment' sense and an abstract 'technique' sense.

aspectUsage: Наделать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective наделывать.
etymology: Formed from делать ('to do') plus the prefix на-.
commonMistakes: Often carries a negative nuance of 'doing a lot of (something undesirable).'

etymology: An adjective derived from запад ('west').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym восточный ('eastern').

etymology: A word derived from an old root meaning 'to rise up,' as the sun rises.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym запад ('west').

etymology: A noun derived from сказать ('to tell').
commonMistakes: Refers to a supernatural 'fairy tale,' distinct from легенда ('legend,' with historical elements).

etymology: A noun derived from отличить ('to distinguish').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym сходство ('similarity'); the prepositional phrase в отличие от ('unlike') is very common.

etymology: An interjection of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Used both for pain ('ouch') and admiration/exclamation.

etymology: A noun derived from снять ('to take, capture [a photo]').
commonMistakes: Refers to a single 'captured shot,' more specific than фотография ('photograph' in general).

etymology: A neuter noun derived from война ('war').
commonMistakes: More literary/historical than the modern армия ('army').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (раба); also used figuratively, as in раб привычки ('a slave to habit').

etymology: A borrowing from German Knopf.
commonMistakes: Has both a physical 'button' sense and an on-screen digital 'button' sense.

aspectUsage: Рисовать is imperfective, meaning 'to draw,' paired with the perfective нарисовать.
etymology: A word derived from a root based on German risen.
commonMistakes: Distinguishes artistic 'drawing' from чертить ('to draft technical diagrams').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin prostituta.
commonMistakes: A very sensitive word — use with care.

etymology: An adjective derived from жуть ('terror, dread').
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with страшный ('scary'), but colloquially also means 'tremendous.'

etymology: The pronoun кто ('who') with the indefinite particle -либо.
commonMistakes: More literary than кто-нибудь, meaning 'anyone at all.'

aspectUsage: Восстановить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective восстанавливать.
etymology: A compound formed from ставить ('to stand') plus the prefix вос-.
commonMistakes: Has several senses: physical 'restoration,' health 'recovery,' and abstract 'reinstating.'

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (коня); more literary/masculine in tone than the neutral лошадь ('horse').

etymology: A noun derived from the root of обидеть ('to hurt').
commonMistakes: Refers to a feeling of being 'hurt, offended,' mainly in interpersonal contexts.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin gubernator.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (губернатора).

etymology: A noun derived from выразить ('to express').
commonMistakes: Has both a linguistic 'expression/phrase' sense and a facial 'expression' sense.

etymology: An adverb of negated place formed from ни- plus где ('where').
commonMistakes: Used together with the verb negation не — this is standard grammar, not a double negative.

aspectUsage: Приветствовать is biaspectual, using the same form for both imperfective and perfective meanings.
etymology: A verb derived from привет ('greeting').
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'to greet' sense and an abstract 'to welcome (a decision)' sense.

aspectUsage: Переходить is imperfective, meaning 'to cross, move over,' paired with the perfective перейти.
etymology: Formed from ходить ('to walk') plus the prefix пере-.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'to cross' sense and an abstract 'to move on (to a topic)' sense.

etymology: A neuter noun of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Also used affectionately to mean 'a treasure (a cherished person or thing).'

aspectUsage: Засунуть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective засовывать.
etymology: Formed from сунуть ('to shove') plus the prefix за-.
commonMistakes: Colloquial, with a slightly careless nuance of 'shoving in.'

etymology: A borrowing from French comité.
commonMistakes: Often a more permanent body than комиссия ('a commission for a specific purpose').

aspectUsage: Пригодиться is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective пригождаться.
etymology: Formed from годиться ('to be fit') plus the prefix при-.
commonMistakes: Often used predictively, meaning 'will come in handy (in the future).'

aspectUsage: Заснуть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective засыпать.
etymology: An old root meaning 'to sleep' plus the prefix за- (inchoative).
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym проснуться ('to wake up').

etymology: A word formed from благо ('good') plus дарить ('to give').
commonMistakes: More abstract and formal than the colloquial спасибо ('thanks').

etymology: An adjective derived from the past passive participle of вооружить ('to arm').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym безоружный ('unarmed').

etymology: A borrowing from French pilote.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (пилота); nearly synonymous with лётчик ('aviator,' somewhat dated).

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both a 'serving platter' sense and a 'dish (as in a recipe)' sense.

etymology: A slang noun derived from отстояться ('to settle, as sediment').
commonMistakes: A colloquial slang word for 'something terrible' — avoid in formal settings.

aspectUsage: Указать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective указывать.
etymology: An old root meaning 'to show' plus the prefix у-.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'to point to' sense and an abstract 'to indicate' sense.

etymology: An adjective derived from век ('a century, age').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym временный ('temporary').

etymology: An adverb derived from ровный ('even, uniform').
commonMistakes: Has both a time sense ('exactly') and a physical sense ('evenly, smoothly').

etymology: A feminine noun derived from мелкий ('small').
commonMistakes: Has both a 'small change (coins)' sense and a 'trifle, minor thing' sense.

etymology: A noun derived from снять ('to shoot, capture').
commonMistakes: Refers to the 'filming/shooting process,' not a single photograph.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin ius.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (юриста); broader than адвокат ('courtroom lawyer').

etymology: A noun derived from подозревать ('to suspect').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym доверие ('trust').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin socialis.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with общественный ('public'), but more common in contexts of social structure/welfare.

etymology: An adjective derived from государство ('state, nation').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym частный ('private').

etymology: A noun derived from тихий ('quiet').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym шум ('noise'); distinguish from молчание ('silence,' the absence of speech).

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Refers to a geometric 'sphere,' unlike мяч ('a ball used in sports').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin october.
commonMistakes: Month names are written with a lowercase letter in running text.

etymology: A noun derived from печь ('to bake').
commonMistakes: Refers both to the act of 'baking' and, more commonly in speech, the 'baked goods' themselves.

etymology: A borrowing from Hebrew āmēn.
commonMistakes: Besides the religious 'amen,' colloquially also means 'that's that, the end.'

aspectUsage: Наплевать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective плевать. In the figurative sense of 'not caring,' both are used.
etymology: Formed from плевать ('to spit') plus the prefix на-.
commonMistakes: Far more commonly used in the slang sense of 'not caring' than the literal 'to spit.'

etymology: A borrowing from Greek periodos.
commonMistakes: Refers to a more bounded 'period' than время ('time' in general).

etymology: A word derived from Czech robota.
commonMistakes: Treated as animate — the accusative matches the genitive form (робота).

aspectUsage: Сводить is perfective, meaning 'to take someone somewhere and bring them back.' Its corresponding imperfective is водить (multidirectional).
etymology: Formed from водить ('to lead') plus the prefix с-.
commonMistakes: Denotes a round trip — taking someone somewhere and coming back.

etymology: An adverb derived from неловкий ('awkward').
commonMistakes: Commonly used as an impersonal predicate meaning '(someone) feels awkward/embarrassed.'

aspectUsage: Уснуть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective засыпать.
etymology: An old root meaning 'to sleep' plus the prefix у-.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with заснуть ('to fall asleep').

etymology: A noun derived from украсть ('to steal').
commonMistakes: Refers to covert 'theft,' unlike ограбление ('robbery,' with violence).

etymology: A noun derived from образовать ('to form, educate').
commonMistakes: More institutional than обучение ('the process of learning/training').

aspectUsage: Велеть is biaspectual, using the same form for both imperfective and perfective meanings.
etymology: A root of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Close to приказать ('to order'), but somewhat archaic/literary.

etymology: A noun derived from страдать ('to suffer').
commonMistakes: Denotes deep, prolonged 'suffering,' more than боль ('pain' itself).

aspectUsage: Разочаровать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective разочаровывать.
etymology: Formed from очаровать ('to charm') plus the negating prefix раз-.
commonMistakes: The reflexive разочароваться means 'to feel disappointed (oneself),' while разочаровать means 'to disappoint someone.'

etymology: A substantivized neuter form of второй ('second,' the ordinal).
commonMistakes: A substantivized adjective meaning 'main course' in a restaurant context, declining by adjective rules.

etymology: A colloquial adverb formed by doubling чуть ('slightly').
commonMistakes: More colloquial and endearing than немного, meaning 'just a tiny bit.'

etymology: A borrowing of Persian origin.
commonMistakes: A hard-sided 'suitcase,' unlike сумка ('a bag' in general).

etymology: An adverb derived from высокий ('high').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym низко ('low'); also used figuratively, as in высоко оценить ('to hold in high esteem').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'bread crumb' sense and an affectionate term for a child ('sweetie').

etymology: A noun derived from питать ('to nourish').
commonMistakes: More literary than еда ('food' in everyday speech); also used figuratively, as in духовная пища ('spiritual nourishment').

etymology: An archaic adverb formed from с- plus перва ('first').
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with сначала, but with a more colloquial/archaic flavor.

aspectUsage: Твориться is imperfective, denoting an event in progress; it has no direct perfective in this meaning.
etymology: The reflexive form of творить ('to create').
commonMistakes: More colloquial and tinged with surprise/confusion than происходить ('to happen').

etymology: A borrowing from French milliard.
commonMistakes: Corresponds to English 'billion' — don't confuse it with миллион ('million').

etymology: A noun derived from существовать ('to exist').
commonMistakes: More abstract/philosophical than жизнь ('life' in the sense of living).

etymology: A borrowing from Greek kosmos.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with вселенная ('universe' as existence), but mainly refers to 'outer space' as a destination.

aspectUsage: Упомянуть is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective упоминать.
etymology: An old root meaning 'mind, memory' plus the prefix у-.
commonMistakes: Lighter in nuance than сказать ('to say') — means 'to mention, bring up in passing.'

aspectUsage: Выступить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective выступать.
etymology: Formed from ступить ('to step') plus the prefix вы-.
commonMistakes: Has multiple senses: to 'perform' on stage, to 'speak' publicly, or to 'oppose' politically.

etymology: A borrowing from Latin traditio.

commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym явный ('overt, obvious').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin ianuarius.
commonMistakes: Month names are written with a lowercase letter in running text.

aspectUsage: Поместить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective помещать.
etymology: An old root meaning 'place' plus the prefix по-.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'to place/situate' sense and a media 'to publish/post' sense.

etymology: A borrowing from German Schiene.
commonMistakes: Refers specifically to the rubber 'tire,' unlike колесо ('the entire wheel assembly').

aspectUsage: Деться is perfective, meaning 'to disappear, go off somewhere,' paired with the imperfective деваться.
etymology: The reflexive form of an old root meaning 'to put.'
commonMistakes: Used almost exclusively in questions and negative constructions.

etymology: A colloquial noun derived from учить ('to teach/learn').
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with обучение ('the more formal process of education'), but учёба is colloquial, referring to the student's own 'studying.'

etymology: A colloquial diminutive of красавец ('handsome man').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (красавчика); a friendly, colloquial word for 'a handsome guy.'

etymology: A neuter noun derived from государь ('sovereign, ruler').
commonMistakes: Refers to the political 'state,' unlike страна ('country' geographically/culturally).

etymology: A noun derived from набрать ('to gather').
commonMistakes: Has both a physical 'set, kit' sense and a personnel 'recruitment, enrollment' sense.

etymology: A borrowing from English safe.
commonMistakes: Refers to a small, sturdy personal 'safe,' unlike хранилище ('a larger vault/storage').

aspectUsage: Поужинать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective ужинать.
etymology: Formed from ужинать ('to have dinner') plus the prefix по-.
commonMistakes: Don't confuse the aspect usage with the imperfective ужинать.

etymology: A word derived from вера ('belief').
commonMistakes: More mathematical/statistical ('probability') than возможность ('possibility' in general).

etymology: An adjective derived from жир ('fat').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym постный ('lean, low-fat'); also used for 'bold (font)' (жирный шрифт).

etymology: A word derived from ходить ('to walk') plus the prefix по-.
commonMistakes: Usually a more serious 'trek, expedition' than прогулка ('a casual walk'), though colloquially it can also mean 'a trip to the store.'

etymology: A borrowing from Latin imperator.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (императора); a different title from царь ('Russian tsar').

etymology: A word derived from перед ('before'), meaning 'that which precedes.'
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym недостаток ('disadvantage').

etymology: A native word of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: The idiom за решёткой ('behind bars, in prison') is common.

etymology: An adjective derived from вне ('outside').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym внутренний ('internal').

etymology: A word derived from ходить ('to walk, to use up') plus the prefix рас-.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym доход ('income').

etymology: An archaic neuter noun derived from весёлый ('cheerful').
commonMistakes: The modern form is веселье — веселие has an archaic, literary flavor.

etymology: An adjective formed from между ('between') plus народ ('people, nation').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym местный ('local').

etymology: A borrowing from French mode.
commonMistakes: Refers to societal 'fashion,' unlike стиль ('personal style').

aspectUsage: Переезжать is imperfective, meaning 'to move (residence),' paired with the perfective переехать.
etymology: Formed from ехать ('to go by vehicle') plus the prefix пере-.
commonMistakes: Unlike the literal 'to cross by vehicle,' mainly used in the sense of 'moving house.'

aspectUsage: Подвезти is perfective, meaning 'to give a ride,' paired with the imperfective подвозить.
etymology: Formed from везти ('to carry') plus the prefix под-.
commonMistakes: Refers to 'driving someone to their destination.'

etymology: A borrowing transmitted via Italian falso.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym настоящий ('real, genuine').

aspectUsage: Кататься is an imperfective-only multidirectional motion verb; the unidirectional counterpart is катиться, and the perfective depends on context (e.g. покататься, 'to ride for a while').
etymology: The reflexive form of катить ('to roll').
commonMistakes: Distinguish the multidirectional кататься from the unidirectional катиться.

etymology: A collective numeral derived from четыре ('four').
commonMistakes: Used for counting people, with grammatical behavior distinct from the standard numeral четыре.

aspectUsage: Отрезать is perfective, marking a single completed act, with the corresponding imperfective резать ('to cut' in general).
etymology: Formed from резать ('to cut') plus the prefix от-.
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'to cut off' sense and a figurative 'to cut off (a path)' sense.

etymology: A word derived from посетить ('to visit').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (посетителя); refers to someone 'visiting a place,' distinct from клиент ('a business customer').

etymology: An adjective derived from слава ('fame').
commonMistakes: Often used colloquially to mean 'nice, lovely,' more than знаменитый ('famous').

etymology: A colloquial diminutive of картина ('painting').
commonMistakes: A casual word for 'picture, illustration,' lighter than картина ('a formal painting').

etymology: A word derived from футбол ('football/soccer'), originally referring to a player's jersey.
commonMistakes: Unlike рубашка ('a buttoned shirt'), refers to a casual 'T-shirt.'

etymology: A word derived from против ('against').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (противника); more neutral than враг ('enemy,' hostile).

etymology: A word derived from покупать ('to buy').
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (покупателя); more specific than клиент ('customer' for services).

etymology: A word derived from ходить ('to walk') plus the prefix под-.
commonMistakes: Broader than метод ('a specific method') — refers to an overall 'approach.'

etymology: A conjunction formed from при ('at, upon') plus чем ('what').
commonMistakes: The standard spelling includes ё: причём; used to introduce additional information, meaning 'moreover.'

aspectUsage: Стремиться is imperfective, meaning 'to strive toward.' The related устремиться carries a different sense of 'rushing/heading toward something, concentrating.'
etymology: The reflexive form of an old root meaning 'stream, flow.'
commonMistakes: The object is expressed with к + dative (стремиться к чему).

etymology: An adjective derived from ядро ('nucleus, core').
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with атомный ('atomic'), but ядерный is more common in military and physics contexts.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek phantasia.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with воображение ('imagination' as a faculty), but фантазия can also mean a specific 'fantasy, daydream.'

etymology: A noun derived from произвести ('to produce').
commonMistakes: Refers to the act/process of 'production,' unlike продукция ('the goods produced').

etymology: An adjective of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym частый ('frequent').

etymology: A feminine noun of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with центр ('the physical/spatial center'), but середина also covers the 'midpoint' of a period/range; the idiom золотая середина ('golden mean, balance') is common.

aspectUsage: Основать is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective основывать.
etymology: A word derived from основа ('foundation').
commonMistakes: Implies a more formal, organized 'founding' than создать ('to create' plainly).

etymology: An adjective of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym тусклый ('dim'); used both of literal light 'brightness' and a 'vivid, striking (personality)' sense.

etymology: An adjective of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Has both a weather sense ('clear, sunny') and an explanatory sense ('clear, lucid').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek Khristos, meaning 'the anointed one.'
commonMistakes: Has irregular declension — the genitive/accusative form христа differs considerably from the nominative.

etymology: A noun derived from использовать ('to use').
commonMistakes: Nearly synonymous with применение ('application, practical use'), though использование is standard in instruction manuals.

aspectUsage: Вступить is perfective, marking a single completed act, paired with the imperfective вступать.
etymology: Formed from ступить ('to step') plus the prefix в-.
commonMistakes: Has both an organizational 'to join' sense and a legal 'to take effect' sense.

etymology: A borrowing from Greek leōn.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (льва); note the vowel drop in declension (лев → льва).

etymology: An adverb derived from дорогой ('expensive').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym дешево ('cheaply'); also used figuratively in дорого обойтись ('to cost dearly').

etymology: A word derived from верх ('top') plus the prefix по-.
commonMistakes: Also used figuratively to mean 'superficial' (поверхностный).

etymology: A neuter noun of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: More formal/nautical than корабль ('ship' in general); note the irregular plural суда.

etymology: A borrowing from French passager.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (пассажира).

etymology: A noun derived from привыкнуть ('to get used to').
commonMistakes: Refers to a personal behavioral 'habit,' unlike традиция ('a socially inherited tradition').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek tonos.
commonMistakes: Has both a vocal 'tone of voice' sense and a color 'shade/tone' sense.

etymology: A feminine noun derived from верх ('top').
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'mountain peak' sense and a figurative 'pinnacle (of a career)' sense.

etymology: A borrowing from French personnage.
commonMistakes: Being an animate noun, the accusative matches the genitive form (персонажа); broader than герой ('the protagonist specifically').

aspectUsage: Занимать is imperfective, meaning 'to occupy, borrow,' paired with the perfective занять.
etymology: An old root meaning 'to take' plus the prefix за-.
commonMistakes: Has both an 'occupying (a place/position)' sense and a 'borrowing (money)' sense.

etymology: A word derived from красный ('red').
commonMistakes: Unlike цвет ('color' itself), refers to the applied substance — 'paint.'

etymology: An adjective of Old Slavic origin.
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym неравный ('unequal'); the idiom на равных ('on equal footing') is common.

etymology: An adverb derived from редкий ('rare').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym часто ('often').

etymology: A noun derived from развить ('to develop').
commonMistakes: Refers to qualitative, staged 'development,' more than рост ('quantitative growth').

etymology: A borrowing from Greek tragōdia.
commonMistakes: Has both a literary 'tragedy' sense and a real-life 'tragic event' sense.

etymology: A word derived from a borrowing of Greek ēlektron.
commonMistakes: An abstract concept always used in the singular — 'electricity.'

etymology: A noun derived from понять ('to understand').
commonMistakes: Refers to 'understanding, comprehension' itself, unlike осознание ('awareness, realization').

etymology: A borrowing from Latin actus.
commonMistakes: Has multiple senses: a single 'act (of violence),' a legal 'document/deed,' and a theatrical 'act.'

etymology: A borrowing from Latin cultura.
commonMistakes: Has both a national/social 'culture' sense and a personal 'refinement, manners' sense (культура поведения, 'the culture of behavior').

etymology: A numeral of Old Slavic origin meaning 'forty.'
commonMistakes: Follows an unusual declension pattern — the genitive, dative, instrumental, and prepositional forms are all сорока.

etymology: A colloquial diminutive of книга ('book').
commonMistakes: A casual, affectionate word compared to книга; also appears in set phrases like записная книжка ('notebook').

etymology: A feminine noun derived from молить ('to beseech').
commonMistakes: Refers to the 'prayer' text/words itself, distinct from молиться ('to pray,' the act).

etymology: An adjective derived from нерв ('nerve').
commonMistakes: Best learned alongside its antonym спокойный ('calm'); has both a medical 'nervous (system)' sense and a psychological 'nervous, jittery' sense.

etymology: A noun derived from падать ('to fall').
commonMistakes: Has both a literal 'fall' sense and an economic/figurative 'decline, downfall' sense.
